fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: Mass and covering exponents for fixed-length honeycomb walks
fields.name: Nienhuis's 3/4 exponent for self-avoiding walk on the honeycomb lattice, in diameter form
fields.field: Self-avoiding walk; two-dimensional critical phenomena
fields.statement: Let $\mathbb P_n$ be the uniform law on $n$-step self-avoiding walks from a fixed vertex of a planar lattice. Nienhuis's Coulomb-gas analysis of the dilute $O(n)$ model at $n=0$ (1982) predicts the size exponent $\nu=3/4$: a typical $n$-step walk has spatial extent $n^{3/4}$, equivalently its trace has mass dimension $4/3$; Lawler, Schramm and Werner's conjectured $SLE_{8/3}$ scaling limit gives the same value. On the honeycomb lattice Duminil-Copin and Smirnov proved that the connective constant is $\sqrt{2+\sqrt2}$, but no polynomial size exponent was known; the best fixed-length bound was sub-ballistic (Krachun-Panagiotis: within $Cn/\log n$). Does a uniform $n$-step self-avoiding walk on the honeycomb lattice have spatial extent $n^{3/4+o(1)}$?
fields.posedBy: Bernard Nienhuis (prediction from the dilute O(n) model)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Nienhuis, Phys. Rev. Lett. 49 (1982), for the exponent 3/4 at n=0. The prediction concerns end-to-end distance and other size statistics; this paper treats diameter, local mass and covering numbers.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family has thirteen manuscripts, all dated September 26, 2026. The principal manuscript proves the fixed-length geometric statement from analytic inputs (strip-crossing mass, nesting around faces, marked-polygon and arc bounds) whose proofs are in the twelve companion manuscripts.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the abstract, introduction and Theorem 1.1 of 'Mass and covering exponents for fixed-length honeycomb walks' were read against Nienhuis's prediction as the manuscript cites it. Theorem 1.1 gives, for every $\delta,k>0$ and every large integer $n$, an event of probability at least $1-Cn^{-k}$ on which the diameter lies in $[n^{3/4-\delta},n^{3/4+\delta}]$ and local mass and covering numbers have exponent $4/3$. The proof imports analytic inputs proved in twelve companion manuscripts, which were skimmed, not refereed. The release's Lean formalization for this family (HoneycombBridgeFiniteness, HoneycombFreeEnergy, CriticalStripMass) covers supporting statements only: finiteness of bridge sums, existence of the free energy and the strip-crossing mass law. Its scope note says the mean-length and 3/4 spatial laws are outside it, so this entry is unreviewed, not Lean-checked. The paper states that it gives no lower bound on the end-to-end distance at fixed length, no scaling limit and no universality across lattices.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $\delta>0$ and $k>0$ there are $C_{\delta,k}$ and $n_0$ such that for every integer $n\ge n_0$, with $\mathbb P_n$-probability at least $1-C_{\delta,k}n^{-k}$, the diameter satisfies $n^{3/4-\delta}\le D(\gamma)\le n^{3/4+\delta}$, and simultaneously for all visited $z$ and $s\in[1,n]$ the ball mass is within $n^{\pm\delta}$ of $\min\{n,s^{4/3}\}$ and the covering number by $s$-balls within $n^{\pm\delta}$ of $1+ns^{-4/3}$. Corollaries: span at least $n^{3/4-\delta}$ in each lattice normal, covering dimension $4/3$, radius of gyration $n^{3/4+o(1)}$ and $\mathbb E_n[D^p]=n^{3p/4+o(1)}$. Not shown: a fixed-length lower bound for the end-to-end distance (a companion has it only on a density-one set of lengths), an exponent without $n^{o(1)}$ slack, other lattices, or convergence to $SLE_{8/3}$.
fields.significanceNote: Nienhuis's 3/4 exponent is the central prediction for planar self-avoiding walk, open since 1982; no polynomial size exponent had been proved on any lattice. This is the diameter form on the honeycomb lattice with n^o(1) slack, so it sits below the full prediction. Placed below the Benjamini-Schramm p_c < p_u conjecture (66), above the Rohde-Schramm FK-SLE conjecture (52) and Cardy's formula for square-lattice bond percolation (48).

fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: Critical strip-crossing mass on the honeycomb lattice
fields.name: The $N^{-1/4}$ law for the critical strip-crossing mass of honeycomb self-avoiding walk
fields.field: Self-avoiding walk; parafermionic observables
fields.statement: On the honeycomb lattice at the critical weight $x_c=1/\sqrt{2+\sqrt2}$, let $B_N$ be the total weight of self-avoiding paths from a fixed boundary point of a strip of height $N$ to its opposite side. Duminil-Copin and Smirnov's parafermionic identity, which proved the value of the connective constant, gives $c/N\le B_N\le 1$. Lawler, Schramm and Werner's boundary exponent $5/8$ predicts a boundary-to-boundary mass of power $-5/4$, and summing over the far side predicts $B_N\approx N^{-1/4}$; Duminil-Copin and Smirnov state this prediction explicitly (Annals 2012, Section 4). Beaton, Bousquet-Melou, de Gier, Duminil-Copin and Guttmann proved $B_N\to0$, and Krachun and Panagiotis a polynomial upper bound with exponent $10^{-10}$. Is the critical strip-crossing mass of order $N^{-1/4}$?
fields.posedBy: Hugo Duminil-Copin and Stanislav Smirnov (explicit prediction, from the Lawler-Schramm-Werner boundary exponent)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Duminil-Copin and Smirnov, Ann. of Math. 175 (2012), Section 4, for the explicit prediction; the exponent goes back to Nienhuis (1982) and Lawler-Schramm-Werner (2004).
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The principal manuscript, 'Critical strip-crossing mass on the honeycomb lattice' (September 26, 2026), belongs to a thirteen-manuscript family on honeycomb walks; several companions re-derive the same bridge-mass law in other conventions and use it as input for fixed-length size exponents.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 of 'Critical strip-crossing mass on the honeycomb lattice' was read against the prediction as Duminil-Copin and Smirnov state it; it gives $B_N\asymp N^{-1/4}$ with constants independent of $N$, in the manuscript's port convention. Lean: lean/ComparatorChallenges/CriticalStripMass.json exists and its solution module OAI.Combinatorics.StripMass.Main is present at the pinned commit; the challenge is not in the formalization catalogue (formalization.yaml). The statement file CriticalStripMass.lean was read here: theorem critical_strip_mass asserts finiteness of the strip sums, $c\,A_N+B_N=1$, $m_N$ comparable to $N^{3/4}$, bridge mass comparable to $N^{-1/4}$ for all $N\ge1$, and monotonicity, with paths encoded as duplicate-free chains of adjacent triangles of the dual triangular lattice. That states the headline. Not rebuilt here, and the match between the triangle encoding and the paper's port convention was read but not audited line by line.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $N\ge1$ the strip sums are finite, $c\mathcal A_N+\mathcal B_N=1$ with $c=\cos(3\pi/8)$, $m_{N+1}-m_N\asymp\mathcal B_N$, the first rightward displacement moment of arches satisfies $m_N\asymp N^{3/4}$, and the bridge mass satisfies $\mathcal B_N\asymp N^{-1/4}$, nonincreasing in $N$, with constants independent of $N$. The route computes $m_N$ through rhombic transfer matrices and a positive integral, then recovers $\mathcal B_N$ from its increments. Not shown: a limiting constant for $N^{1/4}\mathcal B_N$, statements about walks of fixed length (treated in companions), or other lattices.
fields.significanceNote: A precisely stated quantitative prediction in the parafermionic program for honeycomb self-avoiding walk, recorded by Duminil-Copin and Smirnov in 2012 and attacked by Beaton et al., Glazman-Manolescu and Krachun-Panagiotis. Famous within one community. Level with the Ellipsoid Fitting Conjecture (30), below Feige's Conjecture (35) and well below Cardy's formula for square-lattice bond percolation (48).

fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: The weak pinned planar distance theorem
fields.name: The weak pinned Erdős distance conjecture: some point determines n^(1-o(1)) distinct distances (Erdős Problem 604, first part)
fields.field: Combinatorial geometry; distinct distances
fields.statement: For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb R^2$ and a pin $x\in P$ let $D_x(P)=\{\|y-x\|:y\in P\setminus\{x\}\}$. The integer grid shows that every pin can see as few as order $n/\sqrt{\log n}$ distances. Erdős asked (1957, Problem 16, and repeatedly later; erdosproblems.com Problem 604, a 500 dollar problem) whether every set of $n$ points in the plane has a point $x$ with $|D_x(P)|\gg n^{1-o(1)}$, or even $\gg n/\sqrt{\log n}$. Guth and Katz settled the unpinned count up to $\log n$, but for pinned distances the best exponent was $0.8641\ldots$ (Katz-Tardos 2004). The weak pinned conjecture is the first form: for every $\varepsilon>0$, does every sufficiently large $n$-point planar set have a point determining at least $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ distinct distances?
fields.posedBy: Paul Erdős
fields.ageNote: Erdős, Some unsolved problems, Michigan Math. J. 4 (1957), Problem 16, as cited by the manuscript; the name 'weak pinned conjecture' follows arXiv:2505.06590 (Conjecture 4.7). erdosproblems.com lists the question as Problem 604.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The principal manuscript is 'The weak pinned planar distance theorem' (September 23, 2026); its family also contains a separate unit-distance manuscript of the same date, entered separately.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 were read against Erdős's question as recorded on erdosproblems.com (Problem 604) and in the manuscript. Corollary 1.2 gives, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, that all but $o(n)$ points of any $n$-point planar set determine at least $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ distances, uniformly over configurations, with no rate. Lean: formalization.yaml lists comparator ComparatorChallenges/PinnedDistances.json, declaration OAI.WeakPinned.main in OAI/Geometry/PinnedDistances/Main.lean. The statement file was read here: main says that for each $s>0$ the supremum over $n$-point planar sets of the fraction of ordered pairs $(x,y)$ whose distance fiber at $x$ has at least $n^s$ points tends to $0$. That is the paper's Theorem 1.1, which is stronger than the headline; the headline follows by the five-line pigeonhole count printed as Corollary 1.2, which is not itself formalised. Not rebuilt here. The proof uses real-closed-field transfer to number fields and the product formula.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every fixed $s>0$, $F_n(s)\to0$, where $F_n(s)$ is the largest fraction, over $n$-point planar sets, of ordered distinct pairs $(x,y)$ such that at least $n^s$ points of the set lie at distance $\|y-x\|$ from $x$. Corollary 1.2: for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$ the fraction of pins with fewer than $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ distinct distances tends to $0$ uniformly, so every large set has such a pin, and in fact all but $o(n)$ points are. No explicit rate is given. Not shown: the stronger form $\gg n/\sqrt{\log n}$ in Erdős's question, the averaged conjecture $\sum_x|D_x|\gg n^2/\sqrt{\log n}$, or any quantitative form of the $n^{o(1)}$ loss.
fields.significanceNote: The weak form of Erdős's 500 dollar pinned-distance problem; the exponent had stood at Katz-Tardos's 0.864 for twenty years, and the pinned question is a central problem of incidence geometry after Guth-Katz. Placed below the Hadwiger-Nelson five-color step (55) and the Falconer distance conjecture (60), just above Erdős's planar unit distance conjecture as the catalog scores it (40), far above Erdős Problem 654 (10).

fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: A power saving for planar unit distances
fields.name: A power saving over the Spencer-Szemerédi-Trotter n^(4/3) bound for planar unit distances (Erdős Problem 90)
fields.field: Combinatorial geometry; unit distances and incidences
fields.statement: Let $u(n)$ be the largest number of pairs at distance exactly $1$ among $n$ points of the Euclidean plane. Erdős introduced the problem in 1946, showed $u(n)\ge n^{1+c/\log\log n}$ and conjectured $u(n)=n^{1+o(1)}$ (erdosproblems.com Problem 90). Spencer, Szemerédi and Trotter proved $u(n)=O(n^{4/3})$ in 1984, and no better exponent was known; Valtr's metric with $n^{4/3}$ unit pairs shows that an improvement must use a special feature of the Euclidean metric, as the problem record notes. In 2026 an OpenAI construction disproved Erdős's conjecture with $u(n)\ge n^{1+\varepsilon}$ for infinitely many $n$ (Sawin: exponent $1.0141$). Can the upper exponent $4/3$ be lowered by a fixed amount: is $u(n)=O(n^{4/3-\delta})$ for some absolute $\delta>0$?
fields.posedBy: Paul Erdős (problem, 1946); the 4/3 upper bound is due to Spencer, Szemerédi and Trotter (1984)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Erdős (Amer. Math. Monthly 1946) for the problem and Spencer-Szemerédi-Trotter (1984) for the exponent 4/3, and phrases its result as answering whether that exponent can be lowered, without a separate posing reference. The erdosproblems.com record of Problem 90 names O(n^(4/3)) as the best known upper bound.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The principal manuscript is 'A power saving for planar unit distances' (September 23, 2026). It cites the earlier OpenAI construction disproving Erdős's n^(1+o(1)) conjecture and the human exposition by Alon et al.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the unit-distance problem as posed: it gives absolute $C$ and $1\le\beta<4/3$ with $u(n)\le Cn^\beta$ for all $n$, a power saving with no explicit $\beta$. Lean: lean/ComparatorChallenges/PlanarUnitDistances.json exists and its solution module OAI.Geometry.UnitDistances.Main is present at the pinned commit; the challenge is not in the formalization catalogue (formalization.yaml). The statement file was read here: theorem main asserts that there are $C,\beta$ with $0<C$, $1\le\beta<4/3$ and $u(n)\le Cn^\beta$ for every $n$, where $u(n)$ is the largest number of unordered pairs at Euclidean distance $1$ in an $n$-point subset of the plane. That states the headline. Not rebuilt here. The proof combines random cuttings, entropy and prediction arguments with heights of algebraic numbers; the saving is non-effective.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are absolute constants $0<C<\infty$ and $1\le\beta<4/3$ such that every set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane has at most $Cn^\beta$ unordered pairs at distance $1$, for every $n$. This is the first improvement of the 1984 exponent $4/3$. It leaves a gap to the lower bound $n^{1.0141}$ (Sawin) from the 2026 disproof of Erdős's $n^{1+o(1)}$ conjecture, and $\delta=4/3-\beta$ is not made explicit. Not addressed: distinct distances, higher dimensions, or other norms (for Valtr's metric $4/3$ is sharp).
fields.significanceNote: The 4/3 exponent stood for over forty years and is the textbook example of an incidence bound that needs Euclidean structure to improve. A power saving on a bound, so scored below the parent unit distance problem as the catalog scores it (40), level with the Euclidean Steinitz-Bergstrom conjecture (38), below the Heilbronn triangle power-saving lower bound (40) and the Hadwiger-Nelson five-color step (55).

fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: The Singer conjecture in dimension four
fields.name: The Singer conjecture in dimension four: L2-Betti numbers of closed aspherical four-manifolds vanish outside degree two
fields.field: L2-invariants; aspherical manifolds
fields.statement: For a closed connected aspherical $n$-manifold $M$ with fundamental group $\Gamma$, the $L^2$-Betti numbers $b_p^{(2)}(\widetilde M)$ are von Neumann dimensions of the $L^2$-homology of the universal cover. Singer proposed obtaining the sign of the Euler characteristic of nonpositively curved manifolds from vanishing of $L^2$-harmonic forms outside the middle degree (recorded by Dodziuk, 1979). The Singer conjecture in its aspherical form (Davis-Okun 2001, Conjecture 0.3; Kirstein-Kremer-Lück 2025, Conjecture 4.1) asserts $b_p^{(2)}(\widetilde M)=0$ for $p\ne n/2$, which in dimension $2m$ gives $(-1)^m\chi(M)\ge0$. In dimension four Poincaré duality reduces it to $b_1^{(2)}=0$; known cases needed extra structure (right-angled Coxeter groups, hierarchies, Kähler surfaces). Does every closed connected aspherical four-manifold satisfy $b_p^{(2)}(\widetilde M)=0$ for all $p\ne2$?
fields.posedBy: I. M. Singer (as recorded by Dodziuk); aspherical formulation by Davis and Okun and by Lück
fields.ageNote: Singer's proposal is recorded by Dodziuk, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1979), p. 396, in the nonpositively curved setting; the manuscript cites Davis-Okun (Geom. Topol. 2001, Conjecture 0.3) and Kirstein-Kremer-Lück (2025, Conjecture 4.1) for the aspherical form. The date of Singer's own suggestion is not given.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family is a single manuscript, 'The Singer conjecture in dimension four' (September 25, 2026). It cites a companion release manuscript constructing a PD4 group without an aspherical manifold model, to which its theorem applies.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 were read against the Singer conjecture as the manuscript states it. Corollary 1.2 is exactly the four-dimensional case for closed connected aspherical topological four-manifolds, orientable or not, smoothable or not; Theorem 1.1 extends it to finite aspherical integral Poincaré complexes of formal dimension four, a formulation the manuscript attributes to Lück (Remark 11.3 of his approximation survey). There is no Lean formalization for this family. The proof, a long argument on boundaries, annuli, pretrees and path pushing, was not refereed. The conjecture in other dimensions is untouched, so the entry is the dimension-four special case.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if $Q$ is a finite connected aspherical integral Poincaré complex of formal dimension four, with any orientation character, then $b_p^{(2)}(\widetilde Q)=0$ for $p\ne2$. Corollary 1.2: the same holds for every closed connected aspherical topological four-manifold, so the Singer conjecture holds in dimension four. Stated consequences: $\chi(Q)=b_2^{(2)}(\widetilde Q)\ge0$, so closed aspherical four-manifolds have nonnegative Euler characteristic; $\chi(M)\ge|\sigma(M)|$ for oriented $M$; limits of normalized Betti numbers along residual towers of covers. Not shown: the Singer conjecture in any other dimension, or any computation of $b_2^{(2)}$.
fields.significanceNote: The Singer conjecture is a central open problem of L2-topology; its four-dimensional case is the first open one and gives nonnegative Euler characteristic for closed aspherical four-manifolds, itself a long-asked question. A special case of the full conjecture. Placed below the Borel conjecture in dimension four (60) and the Eilenberg-Ganea conjecture (55), above Wall's manifold-realization question for PD groups (42) and the group-ring Determinant Conjecture (35).

fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: Additive hardness and unbounded configuration gaps in bin packing
fields.name: The Modified Integer Round-Up Conjecture for bin packing (Scheithauer-Terno)
fields.field: Bin packing and cutting stock; configuration LP integrality gap
fields.statement: In one-dimensional bin packing (cutting stock), the Gilmore-Gomory configuration linear program assigns nonnegative weights to feasible bin patterns and minimizes their total subject to covering the item demands; its value $LP(I)$ is a lower bound for the optimum number of bins $OPT(I)$. The integer round-up property $OPT(I)=\lceil LP(I)\rceil$ fails (Marcotte 1985-86), but all known instances satisfied $OPT(I)\le\lceil LP(I)\rceil+1$. Scheithauer and Terno (1995, 1997) investigated this modified bound, now known as the Modified Integer Round-Up Conjecture. Does every bin packing instance satisfy $OPT(I)\le\lceil LP(I)\rceil+1$?
fields.posedBy: Guntram Scheithauer and Johannes Terno
fields.ageNote: Scheithauer and Terno, Eur. J. Oper. Res. 84 (1995) and Oper. Res. Lett. 20 (1997), as cited by the manuscript, which calls the bound the Modified Integer Round-Up Conjecture.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family is a single manuscript, 'Additive hardness and unbounded configuration gaps in bin packing' (September 24, 2026); the same reduction also answers the additive-approximation question, entered separately.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the conjecture: for every $c\ge0$ it gives a rational instance with all sizes above $1/6$, integral $LP(I)=B$ and $OPT(I)>B+c$; taking $c=1$ contradicts the conjecture with no ceiling ambiguity. Lean: formalization.yaml lists comparator ComparatorChallenges/BinPackingGap.json, declaration OAI.BinPackingGap.main_results in OAI/Computability/BinPacking/Main.lean. The statement was read here: its first conjunct says that for every $c$ there are an instance with $5B$ items, sizes in $(1/6,1)$, $B+c<opt$, and both the individual-copy and the size-type configuration LP values equal to $B$, the LPs being infima of fractional covers. That states the headline. Not rebuilt here. The instances come from a vertex-cover reduction and grow very fast with $c$.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every integer $c\ge0$ there are a finite rational instance $I$, every item larger than $1/6$ (so at most five items per bin), and an integer $B$ with $LP(I)=B$ and $OPT(I)>B+c$; the same LP value holds for the stronger formulation whose patterns are subsets of individual item copies. So the additive integrality gap of the configuration LP is unbounded and the Modified Integer Round-Up Conjecture is false. Not shown: a gap growing like $\log OPT$ in the instance size, matching the Hoberg-Rothvoss upper bound; the paper says it obtains no such lower bound.
fields.significanceNote: A well-known structural conjecture of cutting-stock theory since 1995, widely believed true and the target of computational searches that never found a gap above one. Famous within one community. fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: Additive hardness and unbounded configuration gaps in bin packing
fields.name: Bin packing within an additive constant: is there a polynomial-time algorithm using at most OPT + C bins?
fields.field: Approximation algorithms; hardness of bin packing
fields.statement: Bin packing is NP-hard and admits no multiplicative ratio below $3/2$ unless P = NP, but its asymptotic behaviour is much better: Fernandez de la Vega and Lueker gave an asymptotic scheme, Karmarkar and Karp (1982) an algorithm using $OPT+O(\log^2OPT)$ bins, Rothvoss $OPT+O(\log OPT\log\log OPT)$ and Hoberg and Rothvoss $OPT+O(\log OPT)$. No hardness of any additive form was known, so even an $OPT+1$ algorithm was not excluded. Williamson and Shmoys list the question among the open problems of their 2011 book (Chapter 17, Problem 3). Is there a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, for some absolute constant $C$, packs every instance into at most $OPT(I)+C$ bins?
fields.posedBy: David P. Williamson and David B. Shmoys (listed open problem), in the line of Karmarkar and Karp's additive algorithm
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Williamson-Shmoys, The Design of Approximation Algorithms (2011), Chapter 17, Problem 3. The question is older, following Karmarkar-Karp (1982), but the manuscript gives no earlier posing reference.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family is a single manuscript, 'Additive hardness and unbounded configuration gaps in bin packing' (September 24, 2026); the same reduction also disproves the Modified Integer Round-Up Conjecture, entered separately.

fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: Topological triviality of mu-constant families of surface singularities
fields.name: The Lê-Ramanujam mu-constant problem for surface singularities: are mu-constant families in three variables topologically trivial?
fields.field: Singularity theory; equisingularity
fields.statement: Let $f_t:(\mathbb C^N,0)\to(\mathbb C,0)$ be a holomorphic one-parameter family with isolated critical points at the origin, and $\mu(f_t)=\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal O_{\mathbb C^N,0}/(\partial f_t/\partial x_i)$ its Milnor number. Lê and Ramanujam (1976) proved that constant $\mu$ implies constant embedded topological type whenever $N\ne3$, using the h-cobordism theorem, and Timourian and King obtained topological triviality of the family of functions there. The argument fails for complex surfaces, $N=3$, where Briançon-Speder examples show that $\mu$-constant families need not be Whitney equisingular. This remaining case is the surface case of the $\mu$-constant problem. Is every $\mu$-constant holomorphic family of isolated hypersurface singularities in $\mathbb C^3$ topologically trivial?
fields.posedBy: Lê Dũng Tráng and C. P. Ramanujam (the case left open by their theorem)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Lê and Ramanujam, Amer. J. Math. 98 (1976), whose theorem excludes hypersurface dimension two, and calls the remaining case 'the surface case of the mu-constant problem' without a separate posing reference.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family is a single manuscript, 'Topological triviality of mu-constant families of surface singularities' (September 24, 2026).
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the problem as the manuscript frames it: for a holomorphic family $F$ on $\mathbb C^3\times\Delta$ with isolated critical points and constant Milnor number there is, after shrinking, a homeomorphism germ $\Phi(x,t)=(\phi_t(x),t)$, jointly continuous with continuous inverse, with $\phi_t(0)=0$ and $f_t\circ\phi_t=f_0$. Topological right-triviality implies constancy of the embedded topological type, so this answers the surface case in full. There is no Lean formalization. The proof uses semistable reduction, the threefold log minimal model program, the Fernández de Bobadilla-Pełka equimultiplicity theorem, Okuma's simultaneous resolution and Langer's orbifold Bogomolov-Miyaoka-Yau inequality; it was not refereed.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every holomorphic one-parameter family $f_t$ of isolated hypersurface singularities in $\mathbb C^3$ with constant $\mu(f_t,0)$ is topologically right-trivial: after shrinking there is a homeomorphism germ $\Phi(x,t)=(\phi_t(x),t)$, with $\Phi$ and $\Phi^{-1}$ jointly continuous, $\phi_t(0)=0$, $\phi_0=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_t(\phi_t(x))=f_0(x)$. With Lê-Ramanujam and Timourian-King this gives $\mu$-constant topological triviality in every dimension. The key step shows that constant $\mu$ forces constancy of Wahl's logarithmic invariant $-P^2$ for non-log-canonical germs. Not shown: Whitney equisingularity (false in general), families over higher-dimensional parameter spaces, or Zariski's multiplicity question.

Famous within singularity theory. Placed below Zariski's multiplicity conjecture (52), level with Kuznetsov's rationality conjecture (45), above the Lipman-Zariski conjecture (42).

fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: Elementary positivity of chromatic quasisymmetric functions
fields.name: The Shareshian-Wachs conjecture: elementary positivity of chromatic quasisymmetric functions of natural unit interval graphs
fields.field: Algebraic combinatorics; chromatic symmetric functions
fields.statement: For a weakly increasing $h$ with $i\le h(i)\le n$, the natural unit interval graph $G$ on $[n]$ has edges $\{i,j\}$ with $i<j\le h(i)$. Shareshian and Wachs defined $X_G(x;q)=\sum_\kappa q^{\mathrm{asc}(\kappa)}x_\kappa$, summed over proper colorings and weighted by the number of edges $i<j$ with $\kappa(i)<\kappa(j)$, proved it symmetric and Schur-positive, and conjectured that its coefficients in the elementary basis lie in $\mathbb N[q]$ (and are palindromic and unimodal). At $q=1$ this is the Stanley-Stembridge conjecture via Guay-Paquet's reduction, proved by Hikita in 2024, whose formula gives positivity for each positive real $q$ but not coefficientwise. Does $X_G(x;q)$ expand in the elementary basis with coefficients in $\mathbb N[q]$ for every natural unit interval graph?
fields.posedBy: John Shareshian and Michelle L. Wachs
fields.ageNote: Shareshian and Wachs, Chromatic quasisymmetric functions and Hessenberg varieties (CRM Series, 2012; arXiv 1106.4287), and Adv. Math. 295 (2016), both cited by the manuscript.

The statement file was read here: for every natural unit interval graph given by a monotone extensive $h$, the witness assigns a partition to each permitted nondescent permutation so that, for every number $r$ of variables, the chromatic polynomial over Polynomial N (proper colorings weighted by $q^{\mathrm{asc}}$) equals the sum of $q^{\mathrm{ginv}}e_\theta$. fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: The critical dimension for one-phase Bernoulli minimizers
fields.name: The critical dimension of the one-phase Bernoulli free boundary problem: is it seven?
fields.field: Free boundary problems; Alt-Caffarelli functional
fields.statement: For nonnegative $v\in H^1(B)$ the one-phase Bernoulli (Alt-Caffarelli) energy is $J(v;B)=\int_B(|\nabla v|^2+\mathbf 1_{\{v>0\}})\,dx$. By Weiss's monotonicity formula and dimension reduction, the regularity of minimizing free boundaries is governed by the least dimension $d_*$ admitting a nonzero, nonflat, one-homogeneous global minimizer: free boundaries are smooth below $d_*$ and singular sets have dimension at most $n-d_*$. Caffarelli, Jerison and Kenig settled dimension three, Jerison and Savin (2015) proved flatness through dimension four, so $d_*\ge5$, and De Silva and Jerison (2009) constructed a nonflat minimizing cone in dimension seven, so $d_*\le7$, by analogy with the Simons cone for minimal surfaces. Is $d_*=7$, that is, is every one-homogeneous global minimizer in dimensions five and six flat?
fields.posedBy: Open after De Silva and Jerison (2009) and Jerison and Savin (2015); the manuscript names no single poser
fields.ageNote: The manuscript calls it 'the critical-dimension question whether d* = 7', citing De Silva-Jerison (J. Reine Angew. Math. 2009) for d* <= 7 and Jerison-Savin (GAFA 2015) for d* >= 5, but gives no posing reference; the question has been open in this form at least since 2009.

The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family is a single manuscript, 'The critical dimension for one-phase Bernoulli minimizers' (September 24, 2026). Its key inequality is checked by an exact finite certificate, with Python reproduction scripts shipped in the release.

The new content is flatness in dimensions five and six; existence in dimension seven is De Silva and Jerison's 2009 cone. So this entry is unreviewed. The flatness proof rests on a universal tensor inequality verified by an exact finite certificate; the release's reproduction scripts were not run here and, by their own README, do not certify the correspondence between formulas and code.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every nonzero one-homogeneous global minimizer of the one-phase Bernoulli energy in $\mathbb R^d$, $1\le d\le6$, is flat, $u=(x\cdot e)_+$, and a nonflat one-homogeneous global minimizer exists in $\mathbb R^7$, so $d_*=7$. Corollary 1.2: the interior free boundary of a local minimizer in $\mathbb R^n$ is smooth for $n\le6$, its singular set is locally finite for $n=7$ and has Hausdorff dimension at most $n-7$ for $n\ge7$, sharp by products of the De Silva-Jerison cone. Method: a Hessian-shape test function and vector field on the spherical link, with an exactly verified polynomial inequality. Not shown: classification of stable but non-minimizing cones, two-phase or vector-valued versions, or rigidity of non-homogeneous entire stable solutions.
fields.significanceNote: The critical dimension is the main structural question of the Alt-Caffarelli theory, the free-boundary analogue of Simons's theorem on minimal cones, open between five and seven since 2015. Famous within free-boundary regularity. Placed below the planar Mumford-Shah conjecture (52) and C1 regularity of infinity-harmonic functions (42), level with the Lane-Emden conjecture (40).

fields.name: Saxl's conjecture: the tensor square of the staircase representation contains every irreducible representation of the symmetric group

u$ of $n$ the Kronecker coefficient $g(\lambda,\mu,
u)=\dim\mathrm{Hom}_{S_n}(S^
u,S^\lambda\otimes S^\mu)$ is the multiplicity of the Specht module $S^
u$ in $S^\lambda\otimes S^\mu$. Let $ho_m=(m,m-1,\ldots,1)$ be the staircase partition of $N_m=m(m+1)/2$. Known cases covered hooks, two-row shapes, double and triple hooks, partitions comparable to $ho_m$ in dominance order, and random partitions with high probability. u)$ be the Kronecker coefficients of $S_n$. otin\{2,4,9\}$ have an irreducible representation whose tensor square contains every irreducible representation?

fields.name: Shokurov's bounded klt complements conjecture for Fano type contractions with finite rational coefficients
fields.field: Birational geometry; complements and the minimal model program
fields.statement: Let $f:X\to Z$ be a contraction of normal quasi-projective complex varieties with $X$ of Fano type over $Z$, and $(X,\Delta)$ an $\epsilon$-lc pair of dimension $d$ with coefficients in a fixed finite set $I\subset[0,1]\cap\mathbb Q$ and $-(K_X+\Delta)$ nef over $Z$. A monotone klt $n$-complement near $z\in Z$ is a boundary $\Delta^+\ge\Delta$ with $(X,\Delta^+)$ klt and $n(K_X+\Delta^+)\sim0$ over a neighbourhood of $z$. Shokurov introduced complements and conjectured their boundedness; Birkar proved boundedness of lc complements, but a bounded klt index depending only on $d$, $\epsilon$ and $I$ was known only over curves (Birkar) and surfaces (Chen). In the formulation of B. Chen (2024, Conjecture 1.1): is there $M=M(d,\epsilon,I)$ such that every such contraction has a klt $M$-complement near every point of $Z$?

fields.name: The approximation threshold for metric $k$-median: is $1+2/e$ attainable?
fields.field: Approximation algorithms; clustering
fields.statement: In metric $k$-median, finite sets of clients $J$ and candidate facilities $F$ lie in a common metric space, and one opens at most $k$ facilities to minimize the total distance from clients to their nearest open facility. Approximating within any factor below $1+2/e\approx1.736$ is NP-hard in this candidate-facility model, by the Max-$k$-Coverage gap. Algorithms improved from the first constant factor (Charikar-Guha-Tardos-Shmoys) through $3+\varepsilon$ local search (Arya et al.), Li-Svensson's route past factor three, $2.675+\varepsilon$ (Byrka et al.) and $2.613$ (Gowda et al.) to $2+\varepsilon$ (Cohen-Addad et al., announced 2025). Is there, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a polynomial-time $(1+2/e+\varepsilon)$-approximation, so that $1+2/e$ is the exact approximation threshold?
fields.posedBy: Implicit in the 1+2/e hardness bound of Jain, Mahdian and Saberi (2002); the manuscript names no poser
fields.ageNote: The manuscript does not attribute the question; it cites the hardness through Anand-Lee (2024) and Feige (1998). Matching the 1+2/e lower bound has been a standard open question in approximation algorithms since that bound appeared around 2002, but that dating comes from the general literature, not from this manuscript, so yearPosed is left empty.

fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, a deterministic algorithm running in time polynomial in the binary input length (the polynomial depends on $\varepsilon$) returns $S\subseteq F$ with $|S|\le k$ and cost at most $(1+2/e+\varepsilon)\mathrm{OPT}_k$, for arbitrary $k$ and arbitrary finite rational metrics with specified candidate facilities. Corollary 1.2: under $P\ne NP$, the infimum of polynomial-time approximation factors in this model is $1+2/e$, the lower bound being the known coverage gap. It does not give a $(1+2/e)$-approximation itself, does not settle the model where every client is a candidate facility ($F=J$), whose lower bound differs, and claims no practical running time. The companion proves a randomized $(2-\sigma)$-approximation for an absolute $\sigma>0$ by anchor recovery and bounded-price payment accounting.

fields.name: Gersten's conjecture: are Baumslag-Solitar-free one-relator groups hyperbolic?
fields.field: Geometric group theory; one-relator groups
fields.statement: The Baumslag-Solitar groups $\mathrm{BS}(m,n)=\langle a,t\mid ta^mt^{-1}=a^n\rangle$, $m,n\ne0$, are the basic obstructions to word-hyperbolicity among one-relator groups: a hyperbolic group contains none of them. Gersten asked whether they are the only subgroup obstructions. Known cases included proper-power relators (Newman's spelling theorem), relators of primitivity rank other than two (Louder-Wilton, Linton) and ascending HNN extensions of free groups (Mutanguha). Let $G=\langle X\mid r\rangle$ with $X$ finite. If $G$ contains no subgroup isomorphic to $\mathrm{BS}(m,n)$ for any nonzero $m,n$, must $G$ be word-hyperbolic?
fields.posedBy: S. M. Gersten, 'Problems on automatic groups' (MSRI Publications 23, p. 228)
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with one fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The companion on virtual compact specialness (same date) uses this paper's hyperbolicity and Magnus-subgroup results at two points; this paper in turn quotes the companion only for the free-by-cyclic corollary.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 of the principal manuscript was read against Gersten's question as the paper quotes it from Gersten (1992, p. 228); it is the conjecture in full, for every finite generating set and relator, including trivial relators and proper powers, with no torsion-freeness hypothesis. The paper notes that excluding all $\mathrm{BS}(1,n)$ is equivalent. The proof rests on Linton's one-relator hierarchy and quasiconvexity theorems and a new combination theorem for HNN extensions; it was not refereed here. There is no Lean formalization for this family (no lean/docs/258.md at the pinned commit).
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if a one-relator group $\langle X\mid r\rangle$, $X$ finite, contains no $\mathrm{BS}(m,n)$ with $m,n\ne0$, it is word-hyperbolic. The technical core is a combination theorem for a class of HNN extensions of torsion-free hyperbolic groups with free, possibly proper edge groups, applied along the Magnus-Moldavanskii hierarchy. Combined with the companion and with Kielak-Linton, Corollary: every Baumslag-Solitar-free one-relator group is virtually free-by-cyclic, with a finite-index embedding in a free-by-$\mathbb Z$ group with finitely generated kernel. The paper does not treat infinitely generated or multi-relator groups. Unrelated to the K-theoretic Gersten conjecture addressed in family 209 of the same release.

fields.name: Are hyperbolic one-relator groups virtually compact special?
fields.field: Geometric group theory; special cube complexes
fields.statement: A group is virtually compact special if a finite-index subgroup is the fundamental group of a compact nonpositively curved cube complex admitting a local isometry to the Salvetti complex of a right-angled Artin group; for hyperbolic groups this gives residual finiteness, linearity and separability of quasiconvex subgroups. Wise proved it for one-relator groups with torsion (answering Baumslag's 1967 residual-finiteness question for that class) and asked, in his question on cocompact cubulation of hyperbolic groups with hierarchies, about hyperbolic one-relator groups in general. Linton settled the case where all two-generator subgroups are free. Is every word-hyperbolic one-relator group $F(X)/\langle\langle r\rangle\rangle$ virtually compact special?
fields.posedBy: Daniel T. Wise, 'The cubical route to understanding groups', ICM 2014 (Problem 13.15)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Wise's ICM 2014 Problem 13.15, a broader cubulation question in which Wise singled out hyperbolic one-relator groups, and Wise's Conjecture 17.8 (virtually free-by-cyclic) as recalled by Kielak-Linton. Baumslag's 1967 Conjecture A is the older residual-finiteness question for the torsion case only.

The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. fields.name: An FPRAS for counting common bases of two matroids
fields.shortName: Counting common bases of two matroids
fields.field: Approximate counting; matroids; Markov chains
fields.statement: Given independence oracles for two matroids $M_1,M_2$ of the same rank $r$ on $[n]$, estimate $|\mathcal B(M_1)\cap\mathcal B(M_2)|$, the number of common bases. The problem contains counting bases of one matroid (FPRAS by Anari-Liu-Oveis Gharan-Vinzant) and counting perfect matchings of a bipartite graph (the Jerrum-Sinclair-Vigoda permanent FPRAS). For intersections only coarse or exponential-factor approximations were known, and Anari-Oveis Gharan-Vinzant's $2^{O(r)}$-factor method is fully polynomial only for $r=O(\log n)$. Cryan, Guo and Mousa asked for a rapidly mixing chain sampling common bases. Is there a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for the number of common bases of two arbitrary matroids given by independence oracles?
fields.posedBy: Cryan, Guo and Mousa (Ann. Probab. 2021) asked for a fast sampler; the FPRAS question is Problem 1 of Section 13.2 of Kuikui Liu's dissertation (2023)
fields.ageNote: Year of the Cryan-Guo-Mousa journal version the manuscript cites; the question is likely older folklore in approximate counting, but the manuscript gives no earlier source.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with one fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. A later manuscript in the family (5 October 2026) extends the method to common integer bases of two polymatroids with binary capacities and builds on this paper's transport and trace estimates.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. The challenge statement was read here: it fixes an explicit oracle register machine and asserts one program and polynomial $B$ in $n$, the binary input length, $\lceil\varepsilon^{-1}\rceil$ and $\log\delta^{-1}$ such that, for all equal-rank matroids on $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ with exact independence oracles, every run halts within $B$ oracle calls and bit operations, outputs zero when the count is zero, and at least a $1-\delta$ fraction of random tapes give relative error at most $\varepsilon$. That is the headline claim. Not rebuilt here. The polymatroid extension is not formalized.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: one randomized oracle algorithm, given independence oracles for rank-$r$ matroids on $[n]$ and rational $\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1)$, outputs $\widehat Z$ within relative error $\varepsilon$ of the number of common bases with probability at least $1-\delta$, outputs zero when there are none, and uses polynomially many oracle calls and bit operations on every execution. Corollaries give FPRASes and almost-uniform samplers for common independent sets of prescribed, unrestricted or maximum size, even for different ranks. The method is a Jerrum-Sinclair-Vigoda style annealed chain with defect states, using the homogeneous Tutte theorem of Branden-Huh (Lorentzian polynomials). It gives no exact counting and no deterministic algorithm, and does not treat three or more matroids. The October companion gives an FPRAS for common integer bases of two polymatroids with binary capacities.

fields.significanceNote: Approximately counting common bases of two matroids generalizes the permanent FPRAS and single-matroid basis counting, and was a well-known open problem in approximate counting. fields.name: Termination of flips for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary
fields.field: Birational geometry; minimal model program
fields.statement: The Termination of Flips Conjecture of the minimal model program asserts that every sequence of flips (more generally, every program of $K_X+B$-negative divisorial contractions and flips) for a log canonical pair $(X,B)$ is finite. In dimension four it was known for terminal fourfolds (Kawamata), canonical pairs (Fujino), klt pairs with $-(K_X+B)$ numerically equivalent to an effective divisor (Alexeev-Hacon-Kawamata), pseudo-effective lc pairs (Chen-Tsakanikas, Moraga) and klt pairs with big boundary (Han-Liu-Zhuang). Does every minimal model program for a projective log canonical fourfold with rational boundary, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, terminate for every choice of negative extremal rays, without pseudo-effectivity or bigness assumptions?
fields.posedBy: The Termination of Flips Conjecture of the minimal model program (Shokurov's difficulty method; the manuscript points to Chen-Tsakanikas for the statement)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites the conjecture through the introduction of Chen-Tsakanikas (2023) and does not date it. It is usually traced to the 1980s minimal model program (Shokurov 1985; Kawamata-Matsuda-Matsuki 1987), but that dating is not given in the manuscript, so yearPosed is left empty.

fields.name: The higher-dimensional Erdos distinct-distances conjecture
fields.field: Combinatorial geometry; incidence geometry
fields.statement: For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb R^d$ let $\Delta(P)=\{|p-q|:p\ne q\in P\}$. Erdos introduced the distinct-distances problem in 1946; the integer grid $\{1,\ldots,t\}^d$ shows that $n$ points can determine only $O(n^{2/d})$ distances when $d\ge3$. Known lower bounds fell short of this exponent: $n^{0.5643}$ and $n^{2/d-2/(d(d+2))}$ (Solymosi-Vu), $n^{3/5}$ up to logarithms in $\mathbb R^3$ via Guth-Katz, and $n^{2/3-o(1)}$ in $\mathbb R^3$ (Tidor-Yu-Zakharov). For every fixed $d\ge3$, is there $c_d>0$ such that every set of $n\ge2$ points in $\mathbb R^d$ determines at least $c_dn^{2/d}$ distinct distances?
fields.posedBy: Paul Erdos (1946, 'On sets of distances of n points'); the higher-dimensional form as recorded by Bardwell-Evans-Sheffer and Tidor-Yu-Zakharov
fields.ageNote: The manuscript says Erdos introduced the problem in 1946 and cites Bardwell-Evans-Sheffer (2019) and Tidor-Yu-Zakharov (2026) for the higher-dimensional conjecture; it does not quote the higher-dimensional form from the 1946 paper itself.

The proof runs a minimal-counterexample induction on dimension through rigid-motion flats, Hilbert function estimates and approximate complete intersections; it was not refereed here. The paper itself notes an earlier claim of the same bound (Aksoy Yazici) that was withdrawn as incorrect. No Lean formalization exists for this family.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every integer $d\ge3$ there is $c_d>0$ such that every set of $n\ge2$ distinct points in $\mathbb R^d$ determines at least $c_dn^{2/d}$ distinct distances, matching the integer grid up to the constant. fields.name: Long-time Boltzmann-Grad limit for stable finite-range radial potentials
fields.field: Kinetic theory; derivation of the Boltzmann equation
fields.statement: Lanford (1975) derived the Boltzmann equation from Newtonian hard spheres in the Boltzmann-Grad limit, but only for a short time; King and Pulvirenti-Saffirio-Simonella did the same for potentials. Deng, Hani and Ma (arXiv 2024) extended the hard-sphere derivation to every finite interval on which the Boltzmann solution is regular with Gaussian decay, and discussed the extension to smooth interaction potentials, where encounters last positive time and several particles interact at once, as a further problem. For a stable, finite-range radial potential, does the Boltzmann-Grad limit hold on every such regular kinetic interval, not just for short times?

fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites version 3 (2025) of the Deng-Hani-Ma preprint, first posted in 2024. The underlying question of deriving Boltzmann beyond Lanford's short time is decades older.

The wording of the Deng-Hani-Ma problem itself was not read here. The proof was not refereed. No Lean formalization exists for this family.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1: for a stable finite-range radial potential, a grand-canonical initial law with pair exclusion and $C^1$ density with spatially summable Gaussian bounds on it and its gradient, and any $T$ for which the Boltzmann equation with that potential's scattering has a classical solution with uniform Gaussian velocity bound on $[0,T]$, all fixed-order rescaled factorial marginals converge in $L^1$ to $f(t)^{\otimes s}$ uniformly on $[0,T]$; empirical averages converge in probability. It assumes, rather than proves, existence of the regular kinetic solution, so it gives no global-in-time statement, and it does not treat long-range or non-radial potentials or give a rate.

fields.name: Long-time nonequilibrium fluctuations of the hard-sphere gas (finite-dimensional laws)
fields.field: Kinetic theory; fluctuation theory
fields.statement: Beyond the Boltzmann equation, the fluctuations of the empirical measure of a dilute hard-sphere gas are expected to be Gaussian and governed by the linear fluctuating Boltzmann equation. Bodineau, Gallagher, Saint-Raymond and Simonella proved this for short times away from equilibrium and for long times at equilibrium. After deriving the Boltzmann equation on every regular kinetic interval, Deng, Hani and Ma identified long-time nonequilibrium fluctuations as a further application of their method. Do the fluctuations of a hard-sphere gas converge to the Gaussian solution of the linear fluctuating Boltzmann equation throughout every interval on which the Boltzmann solution is regular, without an equilibrium or small-data assumption?

fields.name: The unrestricted infinite matroid intersection and packing/covering conjectures
fields.field: Infinite matroid theory
fields.statement: Work with infinite matroids in the sense of Bruhn-Diestel-Kriesell-Pendavingh-Wollan. Two matroids $M,N$ on a common ground set $E$ satisfy intersection if some $J$ independent in both splits as $J=J_M\sqcup J_N$ with $\mathrm{cl}_M(J_M)\cup\mathrm{cl}_N(J_N)=E$. Nash-Williams conjectured this for finitary matroids, and Joo proved it for countable ground sets; Bowler and Carmesin formulated the unrestricted Matroid Intersection Conjecture and the packing/covering conjecture (every family has a partition $E=P\sqcup C$ with disjoint spanning sets in each $M_i\restriction P$ and independent sets in each contraction onto $C$ covering $C$) and showed them related. Joo asked whether intersection holds for two partitional matroids on a countable set. Do every two infinite matroids on a common ground set satisfy intersection, and does every family have a packing/covering partition?
fields.posedBy: Nathan Bowler and Johannes Carmesin (Combinatorica 2015), extending Nash-Williams' intersection conjecture; Joo (2021, Question 1.5) for partitional matroids
fields.ageNote: Nash-Williams' original finitary intersection conjecture is older and is not settled here; the year is that of Bowler-Carmesin's unrestricted formulation, which is what is disproved.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with one fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The family has one manuscript; the construction is formalized in Lean (see verification).
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 were read against the conjectures as the paper quotes them from Bowler-Carmesin and Joo. formalization.yaml lists ComparatorChallenges/InfiniteMatroid.json with declaration OAI.InfiniteMatroidCounterexample.main in OAI/Combinatorics/InfiniteMatroid/Main.lean (file exists at the pinned commit). Its statement, read here, gives two Mathlib matroids (which allow infinite ground sets with the maximality axiom) on a countable infinite type, both self-dual, with no independent cover $I_0\cup I_1$ of the ground set and no packing/covering partition: the headline disproof. lean/docs/185.md also links InfiniteMatroidCorollaries.json (module OAI.Combinatorics.InfiniteMatroid.Corollaries, file exists, not in the formalization catalogue), whose statement adds that both matroids are partitional and fail intersection, and that the separate covering and packing conjectures fail. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: in ZFC there are a countably infinite set $E$ and two self-dual infinite matroids $M_0,M_1$ on $E$ with $I_0\cup I_1\ne E$ for all independent $I_0,I_1$; the pair has no packing/covering partition, so the infinite matroid packing/covering conjecture is false. Corollary 1.2: the same partitional pair fails intersection, refuting the unrestricted infinite Matroid Intersection Conjecture and answering Joo's Question 1.5 negatively. The examples are neither finitary nor cofinitary, so Nash-Williams' original conjecture for finitary matroids and the cofinitary cases are untouched. The local building block also answers the Bowler-Geschke ZFC question on self-dual uniform matroids (separate entry).

fields.name: Can an infinite self-dual uniform matroid be constructed in ZFC?
fields.field: Infinite matroid theory; set theory
fields.statement: An infinite matroid is uniform if exchanging any element of a basis for any element outside it again gives a basis. Bowler and Geschke developed a basis criterion for infinite uniform matroids and constructed countable self-dual uniform examples under Martin's axiom for countable posets, hence under the continuum hypothesis, and left open whether such a matroid exists in ZFC alone. Gollin and Joo recorded even the ZFC existence of a uniform matroid of infinite rank and infinite corank as open. Is there, provably in ZFC, an infinite self-dual uniform matroid?
fields.posedBy: Nathan Bowler and Stefan Geschke (Proc. AMS 2016); recorded again by Gollin and Joo (2025)
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with one fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. This answer is a building block of the infinite matroid packing/covering counterexample in the same manuscript.

fields.name: The generalized Mukai conjecture on Picard number and pseudoindex of Fano manifolds
fields.field: Algebraic geometry; Fano manifolds and rational curves
fields.statement: For a Fano manifold $X$ of dimension $n$, Picard number $\rho_X$ and pseudoindex $\iota_X=\min\{-K_X\cdot C\}$ over rational curves $C$, Mukai (1988) conjectured an index version of a bound on $\rho_X$, and Bonavero, Casagrande, Debarre and Druel formulated the pseudoindex strengthening, proving it for $n\le4$ and for toric cases. Later work covered $n=5$ (Andreatta-Chierici-Occhetta), $\iota_X>n/3$ (Novelli-Occhetta, Novelli) and toric, horospherical and spherical varieties. Does every smooth complex Fano manifold of positive dimension satisfy $\rho_X(\iota_X-1)\le n$, with equality only for $(\mathbb P^{\iota_X-1})^{\rho_X}$?
fields.posedBy: Bonavero, Casagrande, Debarre and Druel, 'Sur une conjecture de Mukai' (Comment. Math. Helv. 2003), strengthening Mukai (1988)
fields.ageNote: Mukai's index version dates from 1988; the pseudoindex form proved here is the 2003 BCDD formulation.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with one fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The family has a single manuscript.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. The proof goes through small quantum cohomology, descendant lower bounds on moduli of stable maps and a recurrence argument, then the BCDD ordered-chain method at equality; it was not refereed here and leans on virtual-class technology. No Lean formalization exists for this family.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every smooth connected complex projective Fano manifold of positive dimension $n$ has $\rho_X(\iota_X-1)\le n$, with equality if and only if $X\cong(\mathbb P^{\iota_X-1})^{\rho_X}$. Consequently Mukai's original index version also holds. The paper treats smooth complex Fano manifolds only: singular ($\mathbb Q$-factorial Gorenstein) Fano varieties beyond the known toric, horospherical and spherical cases, and positive characteristic, are not covered.

fields.name: The Mezard-Parisi formula for diluted spin glasses: the Panchenko-Talagrand equality conjecture
fields.field: Spin glass theory; diluted mean-field models
fields.statement: In diluted spin glasses such as the Viana-Bray model each spin has a finite mean number of interactions. Mezard and Parisi proposed a hierarchical cavity description of the limiting free energy by nested laws of local fields, with replica symmetry breaking. Franz-Leone obtained replica-symmetric and one-step bounds for even arity by Guerra's interpolation, and Panchenko and Talagrand proved the arbitrary finite-level hierarchical upper bounds for Poisson even-arity Ising models with factorized interactions under a positivity condition, conjecturing equality. In that class, is the limiting pressure equal to the infimum of the Mezard-Parisi trial functional over all finite hierarchy depths and trial laws?
fields.posedBy: Dmitry Panchenko and Michel Talagrand, 'Bounds for diluted mean-fields spin glass models' (PTRF 2004), conjecture after Theorem 4
fields.ageNote: The physical prediction is Mezard-Parisi (2001); the precise variational equality conjecture proved here is the one stated by Panchenko-Talagrand in 2004.

The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The family has a single manuscript; its main theorem is formalized in Lean (see verification).

fields.name: Smith-Toda complexes V(n) at every height when the prime may vary
fields.field: Stable homotopy theory; chromatic homotopy
fields.statement: At a prime $p$, a Smith-Toda complex $V(n)$ is a finite $p$-local spectrum whose Brown-Peterson homology is $BP_*/(p,v_1,\ldots,v_n)$ as a $BP_*BP$-comodule, each generator killed to its first power. Adams, Smith and Toda constructed $V(1)$, $V(2)$, $V(3)$ for $p>2,4,6$; Nave proved that $V((p+1)/2)$ does not exist for $p\ge7$; and Culver-Zhang (2023 version) recorded the existence of $V(4)$ as open at every prime. Hopkins-Smith periodicity realizes suitable higher powers, not first powers. The Smith-Toda realization problem asks for which $n$ and $p$ the complex $V(n)$ exists. For every height $n$, does $V(n)$ exist at some prime $p$?
fields.posedBy: The Smith-Toda realization problem (Smith 1970, Toda 1971); V(4) recorded open by Culver and Zhang (2023 arXiv version)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript frames this as the Smith-Toda realization problem, citing Smith (1970) and Toda (1971), and does not name a poser for the all-height, varying-prime form; 1971 is the date of Toda's paper. The V(4) record is from the September 2023 version of Culver-Zhang.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with one fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human-edited). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. A companion of the same date constructs V(4) explicitly at p = 1009 by a direct obstruction computation.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 of the principal manuscript and the companion's main theorem were read against the realization problem. The principal theorem gives, for each $n$, a prime depending on $n$ (no bound on it), via an ultraproduct of $p$-local categories and descent to one prime; the companion gives $V(4)$ at $p=1009$. Neither proof was refereed here. The paper states that it does not claim one prime for all heights, a bound on the prime, or a ring structure. No Lean formalization exists for this family.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $n\ge0$ there are a prime $p$ and a finite $p$-local spectrum $X$ with $BP_*X\cong BP_*/(p,v_1,\ldots,v_n)$ as comodules with the canonical coaction and generator in degree zero. The companion constructs $V(4)$ at $p=1009$, answering the existence question Culver-Zhang recorded as open at every prime. Partial for the realization problem: no explicit or effective prime for $n\ge5$, no statement that $V(n)$ exists for all large $p$, no multiplicative structure, and nothing on the gap between Nave's nonexistence range and the constructed cases.

fields.name: Gaboriau's fixed price problem: do all essentially free p.m.p. actions of a countable group have the same cost?
fields.field: Measured group theory; cost of measure-preserving actions
fields.statement: For a countable group $\Gamma$ acting by measure-preserving Borel automorphisms on a standard probability space, the cost of the orbit equivalence relation is the infimum of the total measure of generating graphings (Levitt 1995). A group has fixed price if all its essentially free probability-measure-preserving actions have the same cost. Gaboriau showed that free groups $F_n$ have fixed price $n$ and that many groups with commuting or amenable structure have fixed price one, and asked whether every countable group has fixed price. Does every countable group have fixed price, or are there two essentially free p.m.p. actions of one group with different costs?
fields.posedBy: Damien Gaboriau (building on the notion of cost introduced by Gilbert Levitt)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Gaboriau, Cout des relations d'equivalence et des groupes, Invent. Math. 139 (2000), for the fixed-price problem, and Levitt (1995) for the definition of cost. The question may have circulated slightly earlier; the manuscript gives no earlier statement.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the vast majority of results were obtained with one fixed procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier results produced by the models. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family is a single manuscript (October 5, 2026). Its INPUTS.md says it was developed from an intermediate source argument and that the available source record does not establish that it was the final revision of that argument; it also says the result is distinct from the fixed-price-one question for property (T) groups.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 and its proof assembly (the conclusion section) were read against the fixed-price question as Gaboriau posed it. The theorem gives the amalgam $\Gamma=A*_J(J\times\langle t\rangle)$ with $A$ free of rank 100, a Bernoulli action of cost at least $1+\eta$, and finite height extensions of cost at most $1+99/M$; both actions are essentially free, so this is a direct negative answer to the general question. The proof (deployment and compression of graphings, finite permutation models, an Arzhantseva-Ol'shanskii type rank bound) was not refereed and there is no Lean formalization. The manuscript's INPUTS.md notes that it was developed from an intermediate argument whose final revision status is not recorded.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: let $A=F(a,b_1,\dots,b_{99})$, $w=ab_1ab_2\cdots ab_{99}a$, $J=\langle b_1,\dots,b_{99},w\rangle$ and $\Gamma=A*_J(J\times\langle t\rangle)$. With $K=e^{96}96^{99}/95^{95}$, $0<\alpha<1/200$, $K\alpha^3<1/2$ and $\eta=\alpha/100$, the free part of the Bernoulli action on $[0,1]^\Gamma$ has cost at least $1+\eta$, while the skew action on $X\times\mathbb Z/M$ via $\chi(a)=1$, $\chi(b_i)=\chi(t)=0$ has cost at most $1+99/M$. Taking $M>\max\{100,99/\eta\}$ gives two essentially free p.m.p. actions of one finitely generated group with different costs. It does not address the fixed-price-one question for groups with property (T), the fixed price of any specific classical group, or the rank-gradient consequences of fixed price.

fields.name: A cubic lower bound for the border determinantal complexity of the permanent (beyond the quadratic Mignon-Ressayre barrier)
fields.shortName: Cubic border determinantal lower bound for the permanent
fields.field: Algebraic complexity; permanent versus determinant, geometric complexity theory
fields.statement: The determinantal complexity $\mathrm{dc}(f)$ of a polynomial $f$ is the least $n$ with $f=\det(A_0+\sum_j x_jA_j)$ for $n\times n$ complex matrices, and the border determinantal complexity $\mathrm{bdc}(f)$ is the least $n$ such that $f$ is a coefficientwise limit of such determinants. Valiant's algebraic completeness theory (1979) makes the growth of $\mathrm{dc}(\mathrm{per}_m)$ the algebraic analogue of P versus NP: it is conjectured to be superpolynomial, and the Mulmuley-Sohoni geometric complexity program targets $\mathrm{bdc}$. The best lower bounds were quadratic: $\mathrm{dc}(\mathrm{per}_m)\ge m^2/2$ (Mignon-Ressayre 2004) and $\mathrm{bdc}(\mathrm{per}_m)\ge m^2/2$ (Landsberg-Manivel-Ressayre 2010). How fast must $\mathrm{bdc}(\mathrm{per}_m)$ grow; in particular, can the quadratic lower bound be improved?
fields.posedBy: Leslie Valiant (permanent versus determinant, algebraic completeness); border version from the Mulmuley-Sohoni geometric complexity program
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Valiant (1979) for the completeness framework, Mulmuley-Sohoni (2001, 2008) for the orbit-closure formulation, and Landsberg-Manivel-Ressayre (2010) for the previous border bound $m^2/2$. Superpolynomial growth remains the open target; this is a new polynomial bound on a tracked quantity.
fields.aiRole: The release README says the vast majority of results were obtained with one fixed procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier results produced by the models. This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human edited). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family is a single manuscript (September 24, 2026), with a Lean formalization of the two headline bounds.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Its statement OAI.PermanentBorder.permanent_cubic_lower_bounds was read here: for $m\ge1408$, any $n$ with a sequence of affine $n\times n$ pencils whose determinant coefficients converge to those of $\mathrm{per}_m$ (and any exact representation) satisfies $m^3/(5529600e)\le n$. This is the headline claim. Not rebuilt here. The paper's branching-program consequences are outside the formal statement.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: $\mathrm{bdc}(\mathrm{per}_m)\ge cm^3$ for $m\ge m_0$, with $c=1/(5529600e)$ and $m_0=1408$, over $\mathbb C$ with arbitrary affine-linear entries and coefficientwise limits at fixed size; the same bound holds for $\mathrm{dc}$, and affine-linear algebraic branching programs for $\mathrm{per}_m$ need $\Omega(m^3)$ vertices and edges (also in the border sense at fixed budget). The route is a smooth-hypersurface bound $(r-1)(d-1)/(4e)$ for forms of degree $r$ in $d$ variables, applied to a coefficient polynomial extracted from a permanent. It remains a fixed polynomial bound: superpolynomial $\mathrm{dc}$ or $\mathrm{bdc}$ for the permanent, and VP versus VNP, stay open.

fields.name: Simon's Problem 7 (1984): a continuum phase transition for a stable tempered pair potential, on an open interval of densities
fields.field: Classical statistical mechanics; continuum phase transitions
fields.statement: Fix a pair potential $v$ on $\mathbb R^3$ that is stable, $\sum_{i<j}v(x_i-x_j)\ge-CN$, and tempered, $|v(x)|\le C(1+|x|)^{-3-\epsilon}$. For $N$ particles in a volume $\Lambda$ at inverse temperature $\beta$, let $Z_\Lambda=\int\prod d^3p_i\,d^3x_i\,e^{-\beta H}$ with $H=\sum p_i^2/2+\sum_{i<j}v(x_i-x_j)$; as $\Lambda\to\mathbb R^3$ with $N/|\Lambda|\to\rho$, $|\Lambda|^{-1}(-\ln Z_\Lambda)$ converges to a function $f(\beta,\rho)$ concave in $\beta$. A first-order phase transition is a failure of $f$ to be $C^1$ in $\beta$. Rigorous transitions were known for lattice systems and only one rather artificial continuum model. Simon's Problem 7: show that for suitable choices of $v$, and for $\rho$ sufficiently large, $f$ is non-$C^1$ at some $\beta$.
fields.posedBy: Barry Simon (Problem 7, Fifteen problems in mathematical physics)
fields.ageNote: Simon, Fifteen problems in mathematical physics, in Perspectives in Mathematics (Birkhauser, 1984), Section 7, Problem 7 (read here from the scanned original); the manuscripts cite it without a problem number. fields.name: A polynomial-time factor-2 approximation for shortest common superstring (the question behind the Tarhio-Ukkonen greedy conjecture)
fields.shortName: Factor-2 approximation for shortest common superstring
fields.field: Approximation algorithms; string algorithms
fields.statement: Given a finite set $\mathcal S$ of strings, the shortest common superstring problem asks for a shortest string containing every member of $\mathcal S$ as a contiguous substring; it is NP-hard and MAX-SNP-hard. Tarhio and Ukkonen (1988) conjectured that the greedy maximum-overlap merging procedure is a 2-approximation. fields.name: The Virasoro conjecture for smooth complete intersections in projective space (and its transfer to projective bundles)
fields.field: Algebraic geometry; Gromov-Witten theory
fields.statement: For a smooth projective variety $X$, let $Z_X=\exp(\sum_g\hbar^{g-1}F_g^X)$ be the total descendant Gromov-Witten potential. Eguchi, Hori and Xiong (1997) proposed target-dependent differential operators $L_k^X$, $k\ge-1$, built from the Poincare pairing, a Hodge grading and cup product with $c_1(TX)$, generalising the Witten-Kontsevich KdV constraints for a point; Eguchi, Jinzenji and Xiong extended them to odd and off-diagonal classes. The Virasoro conjecture asserts $L_k^XZ_X=0$ for all $k\ge-1$. Genus zero, Calabi-Yau targets with $H^1=0$, curves, toric bundles and semisimple theories (Givental-Teleman) were known, but non-semisimple higher-genus targets largely were not. Does the Virasoro conjecture hold, in every genus and curve class with arbitrary insertions, for every smooth complete intersection in projective space?
fields.posedBy: Tohru Eguchi, Kentaro Hori and Chuan-Sheng Xiong (extended by Eguchi, Jinzenji and Xiong)
fields.ageNote: Eguchi, Hori and Xiong, Quantum cohomology and Virasoro algebra, Phys. Lett. B 402 (1997), cited by the manuscript; odd-class extension Eguchi-Jinzenji-Xiong, Nucl. Phys. B 510 (1998).

The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The proof (degeneration with a weight spectral sequence, cap tests, a Hodge-Riemann positivity detector) was not refereed and there is no Lean formalization. The manuscripts use established degeneration and toric-bundle transfer results as stated inputs.
fields.resultNote: Principal theorem: for a smooth complete intersection $X\subset\mathbb P^N_{\mathbb C}$, $L_k^XZ_X=0$ for all $k\ge-1$ in Getzler's first-Hodge-degree superspace convention, coefficientwise in every genus and curve class, with arbitrary insertions from $H^*(X;\mathbb C)$. Companion: if the full constraints hold for a smooth connected projective base $B$, they hold for $\mathbb P_B(E)$ for any algebraic vector bundle $E$ of rank at least 2 (no splitting or positivity), hence for projective-bundle towers. The conjecture for general smooth projective varieties (for example general hypersurfaces in other ambients, or varieties with no degeneration to known pieces) remains open.

fields.name: Gwynne and Miller's graph-metric conjecture for critical FK planar maps (0 < q < 4) and spanning-tree-weighted maps, finite spherical case
fields.shortName: Gwynne-Miller conjecture for FK and spanning-tree maps
fields.field: Random planar maps; Liouville quantum gravity
fields.statement: Random planar maps decorated by statistical-mechanics models are expected to converge, as metric measure spaces, to Liouville quantum gravity (LQG) surfaces with the matching parameter $\gamma$: uniform maps to the Brownian map ($\gamma=\sqrt{8/3}$, Le Gall, Miermont), and other ensembles to the $\gamma$-LQG sphere equipped with the intrinsic metric constructed by Ding-Dubedat-Dunlap-Falconet, Gwynne-Miller and others. Gwynne and Miller's Conjecture 1.7 states that graph distances, suitably rescaled, converge to the $\gamma$-LQG metric for several ensembles, explicitly including critical Fortuin-Kasteleyn (FK) maps with $q\in(0,4)$, $q=2+2\cos(\pi\gamma^2/2)$, $\gamma\in(\sqrt2,2)$, and spanning-tree-weighted maps at $\gamma=\sqrt2$. For these finite spherical ensembles, do rescaled graph distances converge in law to the $\gamma$-LQG sphere?
fields.posedBy: Ewain Gwynne and Jason Miller (Conjecture 1.7)
fields.ageNote: Gwynne and Miller, Existence and uniqueness of the Liouville quantum gravity metric for gamma in (0,2), Invent. Math. (2021), Conjecture 1.7, cited by the manuscript; arXiv 1905.00383 (2019). The broader expectation of LQG metric limits for decorated maps is older.

fields.name: Sheffield's finite-volume continuum random tree prediction for critical FK planar maps with q > 4
fields.shortName: CRT limit of FK planar maps above q = 4
fields.field: Random planar maps; scaling limits
fields.statement: A critical Fortuin-Kasteleyn planar map with $n$ edges is a rooted planar map $M$ with an edge subset $A$, sampled with weight $q^{\ell(M,A)/2}$, where $\ell$ counts primal-dual interfaces.
