fields.name: The Ball-Evans approximation problem in three dimensions: strong approximation of Sobolev homeomorphisms by diffeomorphisms
fields.field: Geometric function theory; Sobolev homeomorphisms and nonlinear elasticity
fields.statement: In nonlinear elasticity a deformation is a map between domains whose injectivity expresses non-interpenetration. Smooth approximation of a Sobolev map is elementary if injectivity is dropped, but convolution destroys it. Ball, attributing the question to Evans, asked whether a Sobolev homeomorphism $f\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^n)$ can be approximated in the $W^{1,p}$ norm by diffeomorphisms (or piecewise affine homeomorphisms). In the plane this was proved for $1<p<\infty$ (Iwaniec-Kovalev-Onninen) and $p=1$ (Hencl-Pratelli); in dimensions $n\ge4$ it fails for $1\le p<\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ (Hencl-Vejnar, Campbell-Hencl-Tengvall). In dimension three: for bounded domains $\Omega,\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^3$ and $1\le p<\infty$, is every $W^{1,p}$ homeomorphism $f:\Omega\to\Lambda$ a strong $W^{1,p}$ limit of smooth diffeomorphisms onto $\Lambda$?
fields.posedBy: John M. Ball, attributing the question to Lawrence C. Evans
fields.ageNote: Ball, Singularities and computation of minimizers for variational problems, in Foundations of Computational Mathematics (Oxford, 1999), LMS Lecture Note Series 284 (2001), Section 3, cited by the manuscripts; Ball says the question is due to Evans, who may have raised it earlier.

Classified partial because the posed question is dimension-free: dimension two was already known, dimensions four and up are negative for small $p$ and otherwise untouched. The papers state that no convergence of inverses is claimed. Not refereed; no Lean formalization.
fields.resultNote: Theorems: for nonempty bounded connected open $\Omega,\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^3$ and a homeomorphism $f\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ onto $\Lambda$, there are $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms $f_j:\Omega\to\Lambda$ with $\|f_j-f\|_{W^{1,p}}\to0$; proved for $1\le p\le2$ in one manuscript and for all finite $p>2$ in the other. The method first builds onto locally bi-Lipschitz approximants with small Sobolev error, then smooths them with fine pointwise control using three-dimensional PL topology (Moise, Bing, Hamilton). It does not give convergence of inverses, approximation by piecewise affine maps with inverse control, or anything in dimensions $n\ge4$ for $p\ge\lfloor n/2\rfloor$.

fields.name: The Blass-Gurevich-Shelah conjecture: choiceless polynomial time with counting does not capture polynomial time
fields.shortName: CPT with counting does not capture PTIME
fields.field: Finite model theory; descriptive complexity
fields.statement: Immerman and Vardi showed that fixed-point logic captures polynomial time on ordered finite structures; Chandra-Harel and Gurevich asked whether some logic captures polynomial time on unordered structures, and Gurevich conjectured not. Blass, Gurevich and Shelah introduced choiceless polynomial time (CPT), which computes with hereditarily finite sets over the input atoms under polynomial resource bounds without arbitrary choices, and its extension by a cardinality operation. CPT with counting was long the most prominent candidate logic for polynomial time: it defines the Cai-Furer-Immerman queries that defeat fixed-point logic with counting. Blass, Gurevich and Shelah conjectured in their 1997 preprint that the counting extension is still a proper fragment of polynomial time. Is there a polynomial-time, isomorphism-invariant query on finite structures that CPT with counting cannot define?

fields.name: The endpoint case of Carleson's pointwise convergence problem for the Schrodinger equation: a.e. convergence for data in H^{n/(2(n+1))}
fields.shortName: Endpoint of Carleson's Schrodinger convergence problem
fields.field: Harmonic analysis; dispersive equations and pointwise convergence
fields.statement: Carleson asked for which Sobolev exponents $s$ the free Schrodinger evolution $e^{it\Delta}f$ converges to $f$ almost everywhere as $t\to0$ for every $f\in H^s(\mathbb R^n)$. In one dimension the answer is $s\ge1/4$ (Carleson; Dahlberg-Kenig). Bourgain's 2016 counterexample showed that $s\ge n/(2(n+1))$ is necessary for $n\ge2$ but did not rule out equality; Du, Guth and Li (planar) and Du and Zhang ($n\ge3$) proved convergence for every $s>n/(2(n+1))$, leaving only the endpoint. Does $e^{it\Delta}f\to f$ almost everywhere for every $f\in H^{n/(2(n+1))}(\mathbb R^n)$, $n\ge2$ (in the plane, for $H^{1/3}$)?
fields.posedBy: Lennart Carleson (the convergence problem); the endpoint left open after Bourgain (2016), Du-Guth-Li (2017) and Du-Zhang (2019)
fields.ageNote: Carleson, Some analytic problems related to statistical mechanics (Lecture Notes in Math. 779, 1980), cited by the manuscripts. The endpoint became the remaining case only after Du-Guth-Li and Du-Zhang; the manuscripts cite no separate statement of the endpoint question.

The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family has two manuscripts dated September 24, 2026: the planar endpoint $H^{1/3}(\mathbb R^2)$ and the endpoint in every dimension $n\ge3$.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the main theorems of both manuscripts were read against Carleson's problem and the endpoint left by Bourgain and Du-Zhang. The evolution is defined by taking the Gaussian-regularisation limit first, on one full-measure spatial set and for all $0<t<1$, which the papers state explicitly; this is a standard way to give meaning to $e^{it\Delta}f$ pointwise. The planar paper says its maximal estimate has local $L^1$ output and that the stronger endpoint local $L^3$ maximal estimate is not asserted. Not refereed; no Lean formalization.
fields.resultNote: Planar theorem: for every $f\in H^{1/3}(\mathbb R^2)$ there is a full-measure set $E_f$ on which the Gaussian-regularised evolution has a limit for every $0<t<1$ and converges to $f$ as $t\downarrow0$. Higher-dimensional theorem: the same for $f\in H^{n/(2(n+1))}(\mathbb R^n)$, every $n\ge3$. With Bourgain's necessary condition this gives the exact range $s\ge n/(2(n+1))$ for $n\ge2$. Not shown: the endpoint local $L^3$ maximal inequality in the plane, sharp $L^p$ maximal estimates at the endpoint in higher dimensions, or results for other dispersive equations or convergence along curves.

fields.name: The sharp exponential singularity rate of symmetric random sign matrices: P(det A_n = 0) = (1/2 + o(1))^n
fields.shortName: Sharp singularity rate of symmetric sign matrices
fields.field: Random matrix theory; discrete random matrices
fields.statement: Let $A_n$ be a symmetric $n\times n$ matrix whose entries on and above the diagonal are independent uniform signs. Two rows agree with probability about $2^{-n}$, so $\Pr(\det A_n=0)\ge2^{-n+o(n)}$, and it is generally believed that $\Pr(\det A_n=0)=\Theta(n^22^{-n})$, mirroring the non-symmetric case where Tikhomirov proved the rate $(1/2+o(1))^n$. Symmetry destroys row independence: Costello, Tao and Vu proved $\Pr(\det A_n=0)\to0$, followed by polynomial and stretched-exponential bounds and the exponential bound $e^{-cn}$ of Campos, Jenssen, Michelen and Sahasrabudhe. Is the singularity probability of a symmetric random sign matrix $(1/2+o(1))^n$, i.e. governed by two equal rows at exponential scale?
fields.posedBy: Kevin Costello, Terence Tao and Van Vu, and Van Vu in later surveys (as the belief that the probability is of order n^2 2^{-n})
fields.ageNote: The OpenAI manuscripts cite no posing source. Campos-Jenssen-Michelen-Sahasrabudhe (arXiv 2105.11384, 2021) write that it is 'generally believed' that the probability is $\Theta(n^22^{-n})$, citing Costello-Tao-Vu (Duke 2006) and two Vu surveys; 2006 is that earliest cited source.

fields.name: The entanglement area law for gapped ground states in two dimensions
fields.shortName: 2D area law for gapped ground states
fields.field: Quantum many-body systems; entanglement and spectral gaps
fields.statement: Let $H=\sum_X h_X$ be a Hamiltonian on finitely many spins $\mathbb C^q$ placed on a finite domain $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^2$, with interactions of bounded range $R$ and norm at most $J$, and a unique ground state $\Omega$ separated from the rest of the spectrum by a gap $\Delta>0$ independent of the system size. Hastings (2007) proved that in one dimension the entanglement entropy $S_\Omega(A)$ of any interval is bounded by a constant depending only on $q,R,J,\Delta$. The gap-to-area-law conjecture asks for the higher-dimensional analogue; in two dimensions only subvolume or near-linear bounds for frustration-free, locally gapped models were known. Is there a constant $C=C(q,R,J,\Delta)$ such that $S_\Omega(A)\le C|\partial A|$ for every region $A$ of every such two-dimensional system?
fields.posedBy: The gap-to-area-law conjecture, cited by the manuscript to M. B. Hastings (2007) and Arad, Landau and Vazirani (2012)
fields.ageNote: Area scaling of entanglement goes back to Bombelli-Koul-Lee-Sorkin (1986) and Srednicki (1993). The lattice conjecture for gapped ground states is cited by the manuscript to Hastings 2007, whose one-dimensional proof left higher dimensions open.

The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The family has a companion manuscript of the same date, 'Polynomial PEPS approximation of gapped square-grid ground states', which uses this paper's collar estimates as its analytic input.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the conjecture. It assumes only a uniform gap for the full Hamiltonian (no local gap, no frustration-freeness, no commutativity) on any finite induced subgraph of the square lattice, including domains with holes, and bounds the entropy of every subset by a constant times its edge boundary, uniformly in domain size and shape. The release has no Lean formalization for this family. The result is two-dimensional only: the paper makes no claim for $\mathbb Z^d$ with $d\ge3$. The constant is existential.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for fixed $q,R,J,\Delta$ there is $C$ such that for every finite induced domain $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^2$ and every Hamiltonian of range $R$ and term norm $J$ with a unique ground vector $\Omega$ and $H-E_0\ge\Delta(1-|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|)$, every $A\subseteq\Lambda$ has $S_\Omega(A)\le C|\partial_\Lambda A|$. Corollary 1.2 gives the vertex-boundary forms. The companion proves that on open $L\times L$ grids with nearest-neighbour interactions the ground state has a PEPS approximation of bond dimension $CL^c$ and global error $L^{-1}$. It does not treat dimensions three and higher, Renyi entropies, or degenerate ground states, and gives no explicit constant.

fields.name: Polynomial-bond-dimension PEPS approximation of gapped ground states on an open square grid
fields.shortName: Polynomial PEPS for gapped 2D ground states
fields.field: Tensor networks; projected entangled-pair states
fields.statement: A projected entangled-pair state (PEPS) on a lattice places a tensor at each site, with one virtual index of dimension $D_e$ per incident edge, and contracts the virtual indices. In one dimension, gapped ground states have matrix-product approximations of polynomial bond dimension (Hastings 2007). Cirac, Garre-Rubio and Perez-Garcia (2019, Section 2.2, Questions 7-8) asked whether a spectral gap likewise ensures polynomial bond dimension at inverse-polynomial Hilbert-space error in two dimensions, for translation-invariant finite-range Hamiltonians on a torus; the best known general bound was quasipolynomial under an extra density-of-states hypothesis. Does the unique ground state of a uniformly gapped local Hamiltonian on an $L\times L$ lattice admit a PEPS approximation with bond dimension polynomial in $L$ and error inverse-polynomial in $L$?
fields.posedBy: J. Ignacio Cirac, Jose Garre-Rubio and David Perez-Garcia (Questions 7-8, Rev. Mat. Complut. 2019)
fields.aiRole: The release README says every result in openai/math was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against Questions 7-8 of Cirac, Garre-Rubio and Perez-Garcia as the manuscript reports them. The posed formulation is translation-invariant on a torus; the theorem instead treats arbitrary (not necessarily translation-invariant) on-site and nearest-neighbour interactions on an open square, so it neither contains nor is contained in the posed case, hence Variant. It is an existence result: no efficient construction or contraction is claimed. It depends on the companion area-law paper, which is also unreviewed. No Lean formalization.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for fixed $q\ge2$, $J,\Delta>0$ there are $C,c$ such that for every $L\ge2$ and every Hamiltonian on the open grid $\{1,\dots,L\}^2$ with on-site and nearest-neighbour terms of norm at most $J$, a unique ground vector $\Omega$ and global gap $\Delta$, some PEPS $\Phi$ on the same grid with bond dimension at most $CL^c$ satisfies $\min_\theta\|\Phi/\|\Phi\|-e^{i\theta}\Omega\|\le L^{-1}$. It does not treat the torus or translation-invariant formulation of the posed question, longer-range interactions, the structural (injective, gapped parent) PEPS conjecture of Schwarz-Buerschaper-Eisert, or efficient algorithms.

fields.name: Can worst-case trace reconstruction be done with polynomially many traces?
fields.field: Trace reconstruction; deletion channels
fields.statement: An unknown binary string $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ is passed repeatedly through a deletion channel that removes each bit independently with known probability $q\in(0,1)$ and concatenates the survivors; each output is a trace. Worst-case trace reconstruction asks how many independent traces $T_q(n)$ suffice to recover every $x$ with probability at least $2/3$. The problem was formulated by Batu, Kannan, Khanna and McGregor (2004). For fixed $q$ the best upper bounds fell from $\exp(\widetilde O(\sqrt n))$ (Holenstein et al. 2008) to $\exp(O(n^{1/3}))$ (De-O'Donnell-Servedio; Nazarov-Peres 2017), $\exp(O(n^{1/5}\log^5 n))$ (Chase 2021) and a quasipolynomial bound (Burudgunte-Valiant-Wang 2026), while the best lower bound was $\Omega(n^{3/2}/\log^7 n)$ (Chase 2021). For a fixed deletion probability, is $T_q(n)$ bounded by a polynomial in $n$?
fields.posedBy: Open since Batu, Kannan, Khanna and McGregor formulated worst-case trace reconstruction (SODA 2004); the manuscript calls it the polynomial-sample question without naming who first asked it
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Batu, Kannan, Khanna and McGregor (2004) for the problem and Holenstein et al. (2008) for the first subexponential bound; it gives no explicit first statement of the polynomial question, so 2004 dates the problem rather than that sentence.

The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The family has two later companions (October 5, 2026): a uniform quasipolynomial-time reconstruction algorithm for known rational retention probability, and an improved quasipolynomial sample upper bound. They give upper bounds and are links here.

They give $T_{q,s}(n)\ge n^{c\log(q^3\log n)}$ along any sequence with $q^3\log n\to\infty$, and $T_{q,s}(n)/n^A\to\infty$ for every fixed $q,s,A$, with unrestricted computation and randomized estimators. The challenge is not in lean/formalization.yaml; lean/ComparatorChallenges/TraceReconstruction.json exists with solution_module OAI.Probability.TraceReconstruction, whose file exists at the pinned commit. The statement TraceReconstruction.lean was read here; not rebuilt here. Its three theorems define the sample complexity as an infimum over budgets admitting an estimator (a probability kernel on complete traces) and state: superpolynomial growth of sample complexity for every fixed $q\in(0,1)$ and $s\in(0,1]$, superpolynomially small minimum one-trace total variation, and the quantitative bound. This states the headline negative answer. Permitted axioms: propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for fixed $s\in(0,1]$ and $0<c<1/(4\log 2)$, $T_{q,s}(n)\ge n^{c\log(q^3\log n)}$ eventually whenever $q^3\log n\to\infty$; so $T_q(n)=n^{\Omega(\log\log n)}$ at every fixed $q$, a negative answer to the polynomial question. Theorem 1.2: the minimum total variation between one-trace laws of distinct length-$n$ words is $o(n^{-A})$ for all $A$. The companions give a matching-type upper side: quasipolynomial samples and bit complexity with a uniform decoder for known rational retention, and polynomial bounds when $q\le n^{-\varepsilon}$. A gap remains between $\log T$ of order $\log n\log\log n$ (lower) and a power of $\log n$ (upper); the exact complexity is not determined.

fields.name: Talagrand's conjecture that fractional and integral expectation thresholds agree up to a constant
fields.field: Probabilistic combinatorics; thresholds
fields.statement: For an increasing family $\mathcal F$ of subsets of a finite set $X$, call $\mathcal F$ $p$-small if some family $\mathcal G$ with every member of $\mathcal F$ containing a member of $\mathcal G$ has $\sum_{S\in\mathcal G}p^{|S|}\le1/2$; the expectation threshold $q(\mathcal F)$ is the largest such $p$. The fractional expectation threshold $q_f(\mathcal F)$ allows instead weights $g(S)\in[0,1]$ with $\sum_{S\subseteq H}g(S)\ge1$ for $H\in\mathcal F$ and $\sum_S g(S)p^{|S|}\le1/2$, so $q\le q_f$. Frankston-Kahn-Narayanan-Park and Park-Pham proved the Kahn-Kalai comparisons with the threshold $p_c$; special cases of Talagrand's comparison were known for weights on singletons, pairs, cliques and bounded-size sets. Talagrand (2010, Conjecture 6.3) asked: is there a universal constant $L$ with $q_f(\mathcal F)\le L\,q(\mathcal F)$ for every increasing family?
fields.posedBy: Michel Talagrand (Conjecture 6.3, 'Are many small sets explicitly small?', STOC 2010)

fields.name: Talagrand's discrete convexity conjecture
fields.field: Probabilistic combinatorics; Bernoulli product measures and covers
fields.statement: Let $\mu_p$ be the product Bernoulli measure on subsets of $[N]$. A family $\mathcal A$ is $p$-small if there are sets $I$ with $\sum p^{|I|}\le1/2$ such that every member of $\mathcal A$ contains one of them. For a family $\mathcal D$ and an integer $k$, let $E_k(\mathcal D)$ be the sets contained in no union of $k$ members of $\mathcal D$. By analogy with his Gaussian convexity question, Talagrand (2010, Conjecture 7.1; also Research Problem 13.3.2 in his 2021 book) conjectured that a fixed number of members of a sufficiently likely family covers everything outside a $p$-small family. Is there a universal integer $k$ such that $\mu_p(\mathcal D)\ge1-1/k$ implies that $E_k(\mathcal D)$ is $p$-small, for every $N$, every $p\in(0,1)$ and every family $\mathcal D$?

fields.name: The Ascoli-He-Park-Talagrand graph-decomposition conjecture at the expectation threshold
fields.field: Random graphs; thresholds for subgraph containment
fields.statement: For a graph $H$ on at most $n$ vertices let $p_c(H;n)$ be the least $p$ at which $G(n,p)$ contains a copy of $H$ with probability $1/2$, and $q(H;n)$ its integral expectation threshold. The Park-Pham theorem gives $p_c(H;n)\le Cq(H;n)\log|E(H)|$, and the logarithm cannot be dropped in general. Ascoli, He, Park and Talagrand (2026, Conjecture 8.1) proposed that it can be removed after cutting $H$ into boundedly many pieces, and proved bounded-degeneracy cases. Are there absolute constants $k$ and $L$ such that the edges of every graph $H$ on at most $n$ vertices split into $k$ subgraphs $H_1,\dots,H_k$ with $p_c(H_i;n)\le L\,q(H;n)$ for each $i$?
fields.posedBy: Ruben Ascoli, Xiaoyu He, Jinyoung Park and Michel Talagrand (Conjecture 8.1, arXiv 2608.11183, August 2026)
fields.ageNote: Posed about two months before this manuscript.
fields.aiRole: The release README says every result in openai/math was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. This result is not one of the README's two exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The proof uses the family's discrete-convexity theorem (September 23, 2026) as an essential input; the manuscript says so.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against Conjecture 8.1 as the manuscript reports it; the manuscript notes that the conjecture's overlapping-edge-set form is equivalent to the partition form proved. The partition is fixed before sampling, and the embeddings of different pieces need not agree on shared vertices. The proof is conditional on the companion discrete-convexity theorem, itself unreviewed. No Lean formalization of this manuscript.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are absolute $k\ge2$ and $L\ge1$ such that for every $n\ge2$ and every graph $H$ on at most $n$ vertices, $E(H)=E(H_1)\sqcup\dots\sqcup E(H_k)$ with $p_c(H_i;n)\le Lq(H;n)$ for each $i$. Pieces may be empty or share vertices, and the partition depends only on $H$ and $n$. It does not give a single copy of $H$ at threshold $Lq(H;n)$ (the separate embeddings need not glue), and $k$, $L$ are not explicit.

fields.name: Is block sensitivity at most quadratic in sensitivity? (Nisan-Szegedy)
fields.field: Boolean function complexity; sensitivity
fields.statement: For a total Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, the sensitivity $s(f)$ is the largest number of single bits whose flip changes $f$ at some input, and the block sensitivity $\mathrm{bs}(f)$ the largest number of disjoint blocks of bits each of whose flip changes $f$ at some input. Nisan and Szegedy (1994) explicitly suggested $\mathrm{bs}(f)\le s(f)^2$. Rubinstein's functions give $\mathrm{bs}=s^2/2$, improved to $\frac23s^2-\frac13s$ by Ambainis and Sun (2011); Huang's 2019 proof of the Sensitivity Conjecture gives $\mathrm{bs}(f)\le s(f)^4$. Is there a universal constant $C$ with $\mathrm{bs}(f)\le C\,s(f)^2$ for every total Boolean function?
fields.posedBy: Noam Nisan and Mario Szegedy (Section 4, Computational Complexity 1994)
fields.aiRole: The release README says every result in openai/math was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. The manuscript is authored 'OpenAI' and names no human author. The manuscript adapts the gated-tournament architecture of Meiburg's 2026 spectral-sensitivity separation (arXiv 2608.00851), whose own attribution credits GPT-5.6-Sol with those ideas.

fields.name: The Erdos similarity conjecture for geometric progressions
fields.field: Real analysis; measure theory and affine copies
fields.statement: A set $A\subseteq\mathbb R$ is measure universal if every measurable set of positive Lebesgue measure contains an affine copy $x+sA$ with $s\ne0$. Every finite set is universal. Erdos (1974, Problem 4.33.7*) conjectured that no infinite set is. Falconer and Eigen proved it for sequences $a_n\to0$ with $a_{n+1}/a_n\to1$, and later criteria (Kolountzakis, Humke-Laczkovich, Chlebik) do not apply to geometric progressions, so even the dyadic sequence $\{2^{-n}\}$ remained open. Is it true that for every $q\in(0,1)$ the progression $\{q^n:n\ge1\}$ is not measure universal, that is, some set of positive measure contains no affine copy of it?
fields.posedBy: Paul Erdos (Problem 4.33.7*, Mathematica Balkanica 4, 1974)

The family's earlier manuscript, 'The dyadic case of the Erdos similarity conjecture' (September 25, 2026), proves the case $q=1/2$ and carries the release's Lean formalization.

For each $q\in(0,1)$ and $\eta\in(0,1)$ it gives a compact $E\subseteq[0,1]$ of measure $>1-\eta$ with no copy $x+sG_q$, either sign of $s$; the set may depend on $q$. It states only the dyadic case $q=1/2$ (from the companion manuscript), a special case of this entry's claim, so the entry stays Unreviewed under the tier rule. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $q\in(0,1)$ and $\eta\in(0,1)$ there is a compact $E_{q,\eta}\subseteq[0,1]$ with $m(E_{q,\eta})>1-\eta$ such that for all $x\in\mathbb R$, $s\ne0$, some $x+sq^n\notin E_{q,\eta}$. So no geometric progression is measure universal; the dyadic companion first proved $q=1/2$. The construction is probabilistic (random routing tables on a finite tree). It does not prove the conjecture for other infinite sets, and makes no claim of one set avoiding all ratios at once.

fields.name: Gaussian free field limit of the six-vertex height function throughout the regime a = b = 1, 0 < c <= 2
fields.field: Statistical mechanics; six-vertex model and random surfaces
fields.statement: In the square-lattice six-vertex model with weights $a=b=1$ and $c>0$, the ice rule makes the arrows a height function $h$ on faces. The Coulomb-gas picture predicts that in the critical range $|\Delta|\le1$, $\Delta=1-c^2/2$ (that is $0<c\le2$), the rescaled height converges to a multiple of the Gaussian free field; Di Francesco, Saleur and Zuber (1987) gave the Gaussian action for $1<c<2$ with squared multiplier $1/\arcsin(c/2)$ in unit height steps. Rigorous results covered the free-fermion point $c=\sqrt2$ (Kenyon), perturbations of it, logarithmic delocalization for $1\le c\le2$, and a GFF theorem for $\sqrt3\le c\le2$. Does the height function converge to $\sigma(c)$ times the Gaussian free field, with $\sigma(c)^2=1/\arcsin(c/2)$, for every $c\in(0,2]$?
fields.posedBy: Coulomb-gas prediction; the manuscript cites P. di Francesco, H. Saleur and J.-B. Zuber (J. Stat. Phys. 1987) for the Gaussian action and coupling
fields.ageNote: The Gaussian description belongs to the Coulomb-gas approach of the 1970s and 1980s; the manuscript cites DFSZ 1987 for the precise prediction in $1<c<2$ and states that its formula agrees with the proved multiplier. Physical predictions stated precisely in print count as posed.

At $c=2$ and for the amplitude on $1\le c<2$ it uses Duminil-Copin-Kozlowski-Lammers-Manolescu (2026), whose rotational-invariance input is cited as in preparation; the manuscript supplies its own endpoint rotation argument. fields.name: The Laughlin spectral gap conjecture for the V1 pseudopotential on the sphere
fields.field: Fractional quantum Hall effect; spectral gaps
fields.statement: On the sphere with $Q$ flux quanta, $N$ fermions in the lowest Landau level interact through Haldane's $V_1$ pseudopotential $H_{N,Q}=\sum_{i<j}P^{(1)}_{ij}$, which penalizes each pair in relative angular momentum one. At $Q=3(N-1)$ the Laughlin state $\prod_{i<j}(u_iv_j-u_jv_i)^3$ is its unique zero mode. Numerics since Haldane and Rezayi (1985) indicate a gap above it, and the folklore spectral-gap conjecture is recorded in Rougerie's survey (Conjecture A.1); uniform gaps were proved only for truncated pseudopotentials on thin cylinders and tori (Nachtergaele-Warzel-Young, Warzel-Young). Is there $\gamma>0$ with $H_{N,3(N-1)}\ge\gamma(1-P_{\mathrm L})$ for all sufficiently large $N$?
fields.posedBy: Folklore since Haldane (1983) and Haldane-Rezayi (1985); recorded as Conjecture A.1 in N. Rougerie's survey, as cited by the manuscript
fields.ageNote: The manuscript dates the gap question to Haldane and Rezayi's 1985 finite-size study, which distinguished the expected gap from a proof; the written conjecture it cites is in Rougerie's survey, whose year the manuscript's text does not give.

fields.name: The duality conjecture for metric entropy (Pietsch)
fields.field: Asymptotic geometric analysis; covering numbers
fields.statement: For convex bodies $A,B$ let $N(A,B)$ be the least number of translates of $B$ covering $A$, and let $K^\circ$ be the polar of $K$. The duality conjecture for metric entropy, originating in Pietsch's 1972 work on entropy numbers of operators and formulated geometrically by Artstein, Milman, Szarek and Tomczak-Jaegermann (2004, Conjecture 1), asks whether covering complexity is preserved under polarity up to universal changes of scale and constant factors. It was proved when one body is an ellipsoid (Artstein-Milman-Szarek 2004) and with logarithmic losses in general (E. Milman). Are there absolute constants $a,b\ge1$ such that $\frac1b\log N(L^\circ,aK^\circ)\le\log N(K,L)\le b\log N(L^\circ,a^{-1}K^\circ)$ for all dimensions and all origin-symmetric convex bodies $K,L$?
fields.posedBy: Albrecht Pietsch (1972, operator form); geometric form as Conjecture 1 of Artstein, Milman, Szarek and Tomczak-Jaegermann (GAFA 2004)
fields.aiRole: The release README says every result in openai/math was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. The statement MetricEntropyDuality.lean was read here; not rebuilt here. It defines the cube, polar, translate covers and covering numbers in $\mathbb R^n$, and states exactly Theorem 1.1 for a compact convex symmetric $K$ with nonempty interior, with both covers shown to exist. This states the headline disproof. Only one direction is refuted; the dimension grows with $a,b$. Permitted axioms: propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $a,b\ge1$ there exist $n$ and an origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ such that, with $L$ the cube, $\log N(K,L)>b\log N(L^\circ,a^{-1}K^\circ)$. fields.name: The least distortion of embedding edit distance into l1
fields.field: Metric embeddings; edit distance
fields.statement: Let $E_\Sigma(d)$ be the least distortion of an embedding into $\ell_1$ of the strings of length at most $d$ over an alphabet $\Sigma$, with unit-cost edit distance (insertions, deletions, substitutions). Ostrovsky and Rabani (2007) embedded binary strings with distortion $\exp(O(\sqrt{\log d\log\log d}))$. Lower bounds rose from $3/2$ (Andoni-Deza-Gupta-Indyk-Raskhodnikova 2003) to $(\log d)^{1/2-o(1)}$ (Khot-Naor 2006) and $\Omega(\log d)$ (Krauthgamer-Rabani 2009), leaving an exponential gap. What is the order of growth of $E_\Sigma(d)$; in particular, is the Ostrovsky-Rabani bound $\exp(O(\sqrt{\log d\log\log d}))$ optimal?

fields.ageNote: The manuscripts present the question through the gap between Ostrovsky-Rabani (2007) and Krauthgamer-Rabani (2009) and do not cite a paper that poses it, so no year is given.

fields.name: The entropy photon-number inequality (Guha-Erkmen-Shapiro)
fields.field: Quantum Shannon theory; bosonic channels
fields.statement: For an $n$-mode bosonic state $\rho$ let $N(\rho)=g^{-1}(S(\rho)/n)$, where $g(t)=(t+1)\log(t+1)-t\log t$ is the entropy per mode of a thermal state; $N$ is the mean photon number per mode of the product thermal state with the same entropy. Guha, Erkmen and Shapiro (2007) conjectured the entropy photon-number inequality, a quantum analogue of the entropy power inequality with consequences for minimum output entropy and broadcast capacities. Konig-Smith and De Palma-Mari-Giovannetti proved weaker entropy power inequalities. If independent $n$-mode states $\rho_A,\rho_B$ are mixed on a beam splitter of transmissivity $\eta\in[0,1]$ with output $\rho_C$, is $N(\rho_C)\ge\eta N(\rho_A)+(1-\eta)N(\rho_B)$?
fields.posedBy: Saikat Guha, Baris I. Erkmen and Jeffrey H. Shapiro ('The entropy photon-number inequality and its consequences', arXiv 0710.5666, 2007)
fields.aiRole: The release README says every result in openai/math was produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. The finite-energy hypothesis is a scope limit the paper states. The challenge is not in lean/formalization.yaml; lean/ComparatorChallenges/EntropyPhotonNumber.json exists with solution_module OAI.InformationTheory.PhotonNumber.Inequality, whose file exists at the pinned commit. It models states as positive trace-one operators on untruncated $\ell^2(\mathbb N^n)$, entropy by functional calculus, the beam-splitter output through explicit number-basis coefficients and a partial-trace HasSum condition, and states $\eta g^{-1}(S_A/n)+(1-\eta)g^{-1}(S_B/n)\le g^{-1}(S_C/n)$ for finite-energy inputs. This states the headline. Permitted axioms: propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for finite $n\ge1$, $\eta\in[0,1]$ and $n$-mode states $\rho_A,\rho_B$ of finite mean photon number, the output of passive mixing satisfies $g^{-1}(S(\rho_C)/n)\ge\eta g^{-1}(S(\rho_A)/n)+(1-\eta)g^{-1}(S(\rho_B)/n)$, with equality for product thermal inputs. Corollaries: the exact minimum output entropy at fixed input entropy for tensor powers of the thermal attenuator, and the capacity region of the degraded pure-loss bosonic broadcast channel. Not covered: infinite-energy finite-entropy inputs, amplifiers and additive-noise channels, and uniqueness of optimizers.

fields.name: The Kadison-Ringrose cohomology conjecture
fields.field: Operator algebras: bounded Hochschild cohomology
fields.statement: For a complex von Neumann algebra $M$, let $C_b^k(M,M)$ be the bounded complex $k$-linear maps $M^k\to M$ (operator-norm boundedness, no complete boundedness), with the Hochschild differential $d$, and let $H_b^k(M,M)=\ker d/\operatorname{im} d$, the image taken without closure. In degree one vanishing is the Kadison-Sakai theorem that every derivation of $M$ is inner. Kadison and Ringrose proved vanishing for type I and hyperfinite algebras, Christensen, Effros and Sinclair whenever the type $\mathrm{II}_1$ summand absorbs the hyperfinite $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor, and later work handled Cartan subalgebras and property $\Gamma$. Is $H_b^k(M,M)=0$ for every complex von Neumann algebra $M$ and every $k\ge1$?
fields.posedBy: Richard V. Kadison and John R. Ringrose (Cohomology of operator algebras I, II, 1971); Sinclair and Smith trace the self-coefficient formulation to 1967
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Sinclair and Smith (PNAS 1998, p. 3376), who trace the self-coefficient formulation to 1967; the first published papers on the problem are Kadison and Ringrose, Acta Math. 1971.
fields.aiRole: Produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model as part of an OpenAI evaluation on open research problems. The manuscript is authored as OpenAI with no human author named.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the abstract, introduction and Theorem 1.1, read against the conjecture as the manuscript states it (vanishing of $H_b^k(M,M)$ for all complex von Neumann algebras and all $k\ge1$). The proof was not refereed. Theorem 1.1 covers every degree $k\ge2$ with no separability or type restriction; degree one is the classical Kadison-Sakai inner-derivation theorem, which the paper cites rather than reproves. Lean-checked on the release's own Comparator challenge KadisonRingrose together with its solution module OAI.Analysis.BoundedHochschild.MainResult, both fetched at the pinned commit; the challenge is not listed in the release's formalization catalogue (lean/formalization.yaml), the statement was read here but not independently audited, and the development was not rebuilt here. The formal statement (OAI.BoundedHochschild.KadisonRingrose.main_result) takes any C*-algebra with a W*-algebra (predual) structure and says every bounded multilinear cocycle of degree n+2 with values in the algebra is the differential of a bounded cochain of degree n+1, which is the headline claim for all degrees at least two.
fields.resultNote: Claims Theorem 1.1: for every complex von Neumann algebra $M$ and every $k\ge2$, every bounded $k$-cocycle $f\in C_b^k(M,M)$ with $df=0$ equals $dg$ for some bounded $g\in C_b^{k-1}(M,M)$, so $H_b^k(M,M)=0$. Combined with the Kadison-Sakai theorem in degree one this is the full conjecture. The key new input is a Liouville theorem for harmonic maps under a single unitary random walk built from Popa's free-independent sequences in type $\mathrm{II}_1$ algebras. It concerns ordinary bounded cohomology with coefficients in $M$ itself; it says nothing new about coefficients in $B(H)$ or about completely bounded cohomology beyond what follows.

fields.name: The smooth realization problem: does finite entropy suffice for a smooth volume-preserving model?
fields.field: Ergodic theory; smooth realization of measure-preserving systems
fields.statement: A smooth positive-volume model of an invertible ergodic transformation $(X,\mu,T)$ of a standard nonatomic probability space is a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $S$ of a compact finite-dimensional manifold $M$ preserving a probability $\nu$ with strictly positive smooth density, together with a measurable isomorphism $F$ between invariant conull sets with $F\circ T=S\circ F$. Finite Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy is necessary (Ruelle's inequality), and Lind and Thouvenot realized every finite-entropy ergodic system by a homeomorphism of the two-torus, but a realization with a singular invariant measure does not give a smooth volume. The smooth realization problem, as discussed by Katok and Thouvenot, asks whether this entropy restriction is the only one. Does every ergodic invertible transformation with finite entropy admit a smooth positive-volume model?
fields.posedBy: The classical smooth realization problem, in the formulation discussed by Anatole Katok and Jean-Paul Thouvenot (Ann. IHP Probab. Stat. 1997, pp. 324-326)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Katok and Thouvenot (1997) for the classical formulation and Foreman and Weiss (2022) for a variant; it does not name an earlier originator, though the problem is commonly traced to Anosov and Katok (1970). Year taken from the cited source.

It does not exclude models whose invariant measure is only equivalent to volume, and it does not characterize which systems are smoothly realizable.

fields.name: Parity is not in QAC0 (Moore's parity conjecture)
fields.field: Quantum circuit complexity; constant-depth lower bounds
fields.statement: $\mathrm{QAC}^0$ is the class of constant-depth quantum circuits on polynomially many qubits built from arbitrary one-qubit unitaries and Toffoli gates with unboundedly many controls, gates in a layer acting on disjoint qubits. Classically parity is not in $\mathrm{AC}^0$ (Furst-Saxe-Sipser, Ajtai, Hastad). Moore introduced these quantum classes in 1999 and related coherent parity to unbounded fanout; he conjectured that parity cannot be computed in $\mathrm{QAC}^0$. Prior lower bounds needed restrictions on the number of ancillas or on the entangling depth. Can a constant-depth quantum circuit of this kind, with polynomially many zero-initialized ancillas, compute the parity of $n$ input bits with bounded error?
fields.posedBy: Cristopher Moore (Quantum circuits: fanout, parity, and counting, arXiv quant-ph/9903046, 1999)
fields.aiRole: Produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model as part of an OpenAI evaluation on open research problems. The manuscript is authored as OpenAI with no human author named. Two manuscripts dated the same day give two different proofs of the same bound.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. fields.resultNote: Claims: for every fixed depth $d$, every $c\ge1$ and every $0<\varepsilon\le1/2$, for all large $n$ no depth-$d$ circuit of one-qubit unitaries and unbounded-arity Toffoli gates on at most $n^c$ qubits, ancillas starting in $|0\rangle$ and one output qubit measured, computes parity with probability at least $1/2+\varepsilon$ on every input. Taking $\varepsilon=1/6$ gives bounded error $2/3$. The companion paper gives a second proof via regular trajectories and pruning; via Xu-Li reductions the same obstruction holds for strict majority. It does not cover circuits with intermediate measurements, postselection or primitive fanout gates, and gives no explicit size-depth tradeoff beyond polynomial size.

fields.name: The second Kahn-Kalai conjecture
fields.field: Random graphs; thresholds and expectation thresholds
fields.statement: For a graph $H$ with at least one edge and at most $n$ vertices, let $p_c(n,H)$ be the density at which $G(n,p)$ contains a copy of $H$ with probability $1/2$, and $p_E(n,H)$ the least density at which every subgraph $F\subseteq H$ has expected copy count at least one (or one half). Always $p_E\le p_c$, and perfect matchings and Hamilton cycles show a logarithmic gap can occur. Kahn and Kalai conjectured in 2007 that this elementary first-moment obstruction determines the threshold up to a logarithm, uniformly in $H$. The abstract (first) Kahn-Kalai conjecture was proved by Park and Pham; it does not give the graph statement, and the best prior general bound was $O(\log^2)$ loss. Is $p_c(n,H)=O(p_E(n,H)\log n)$ for every such $H$, with a universal constant?
fields.posedBy: Jeff Kahn and Gil Kalai (Thresholds and expectation thresholds, Combin. Probab. Comput. 16, 2007)
fields.aiRole: Produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model as part of an OpenAI evaluation on open research problems. The release README says the vast majority of results used one fixed procedure, averaging about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result; this result is not among the README's stated exceptions (the Riemann zeta zero-free region work and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties). The manuscript is authored as OpenAI with no human author named.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: abstract, introduction and Theorem 1.1, read against the Kahn-Kalai formulation as cited; the paper notes that normalising expected counts at one half instead of one changes $p_E$ by at most a factor two, so the conjecture is unchanged. The proof was not refereed. Lean-checked: the release's formalization catalogue lists ComparatorChallenges/SecondKahnKalai.json with declaration OAI.LeanBlast.SecondKahnKalai.secondKahnKalaiBounds. The statement was read here: for n >= 2 and any finite simple graph H with at least one edge and at most n vertices, the actual containment threshold (infimum over p of probability >= 1/2) is at most min(1, 2048 e^50 p_E (1 + log2 e(H))) and at most 6144 e^50 p_E log2 n, with p_E defined over all subgraphs of H. That is the headline claim. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Claims Theorem 1.1: for every $n\ge2$ and every finite simple graph $H$ with $h\ge1$ edges and at most $n$ vertices, $p_c(n,H)\le\min\{1,2048e^{50}p_E(n,H)(1+\log_2 h)\}$, hence $p_c(n,H)\le6144e^{50}p_E(n,H)\log_2 n$. The logarithm depends only on the number of edges of $H$, which is stronger than the conjectured $\log n$. The proof builds on Tran's spread-link cores and the Mossel-Niles-Weed-Sun-Zadik resampling, with a tree reduction replacing Tran's proposed coupling conjecture. Constants are explicit but huge; it says nothing about optimal constants or about hypergraph targets.

fields.name: The strong isotropic constant conjecture: simplices maximize the isotropic constant
fields.field: Convex geometry; isotropic constants and the slicing problem
fields.statement: For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ with covariance matrix $\Sigma_K$ of the uniform distribution, the isotropic constant is $L_K=(\det\Sigma_K/|K|^2)^{1/(2n)}$, an affine invariant. Bourgain's slicing problem asked for a dimension-free upper bound, recently obtained by Klartag and Lehec. The sharp (strong) form asks for the extremal body: Campi, Colesanti and Gronchi proved it in the plane, Saroglou proved uniqueness there, and Rademacher showed a simplicial polytope maximizer must be a simplex. Klartag showed the sharp bound implies the non-symmetric Mahler inequality, and Fradelizi and Marin Sola recast it as a sharp entropy bound for log-concave densities. Is it true in every dimension $n$ that $L_K\le L_{\Delta_n}$ for every convex body $K$, where $\Delta_n$ is a simplex, with equality only for simplices?
fields.posedBy: Sharp form of Bourgain's slicing problem (1986); no originator named in the manuscript, which cites Campi-Colesanti-Gronchi (1999, planar case) and Fradelizi-Marin Sola (entropy form)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript calls it the strong isotropic constant conjecture without naming who first stated it; the planar case was proved by Campi, Colesanti and Gronchi in 1999, so it predates that. Left null rather than guessed.
fields.aiRole: Produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model as part of an OpenAI evaluation on open research problems. The release README says the vast majority of results used one fixed procedure, averaging about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result; this result is not among the README's stated exceptions (the Riemann zeta zero-free region work and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties). The manuscript is authored as OpenAI with no human author named. The README also cautions that unformalized results could have issues.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: abstract, introduction, Theorems 1.1 and 1.2, read against the conjecture as the manuscript states it. The release ships a scalar certificate checker, verification/verify_scalar.py (exact rational arithmetic, standard library); it was run here on 7 October 2026 and ended with ALL CHECKS PASSED. That checker covers only the rational scalar inequalities used in the estimates, not the transport, chaos-decomposition or equality-case arguments, so it does not raise the tier.
fields.resultNote: Claims Theorem 1.1: for every $n\ge1$ and every convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $L_K\le(n!)^{1/n}/((n+1)^{(n+1)/(2n)}\sqrt{n+2})$, with equality if and only if $K$ is a simplex. Also claims the sharp entropy bound $h(f)\ge m+\tfrac12\log\det\mathrm{Cov}(f)$ for every log-concave density on $\mathbb R^m$, with equality exactly for affine images of products of one-sided exponentials, proved via Gaussian-to-target Brenier transport. Via Klartag (2018) it yields the non-symmetric Mahler inequality $|K||K^\circ|\ge(n+1)^{n+1}/(n!)^2$, already listed from a separate manuscript of the same release. It gives no new information on the symmetric slicing constant or on symmetric Mahler.

fields.significanceNote: The extremal form of the slicing problem, the organizing question of asymptotic convex geometry, and strong enough to imply the non-symmetric Mahler conjecture. fields.name: The satisfiability threshold conjecture: a limiting random k-SAT threshold for every k >= 3
fields.field: Random constraint satisfaction; random k-SAT phase transition
fields.statement: Fix $k\ge3$ and let $F_{n,m}$ be a conjunction of $m$ independent uniformly random $k$-clauses on $n$ Boolean variables (distinct variables in a clause, fair signs). Friedgut (with Bourgain) proved a sharp threshold: there is a sequence $c_k(n)$ around which the satisfiability probability drops from near one to near zero, but not that $c_k(n)$ converges. Ding, Sly and Sun proved convergence, with the predicted value, for all sufficiently large $k$; the case $k=2$ is classical. Chvatal and Reed conjectured that each fixed clause size has a limiting density. Is there, for every fixed $k\ge3$, a constant $\alpha_k$ such that $\Pr(F_{n,\lfloor cn\rfloor}\text{ satisfiable})\to1$ for $c<\alpha_k$ and $\to0$ for $c>\alpha_k$?
fields.posedBy: Vasek Chvatal and Bruce Reed (Mick gets some (the odds are on his side), FOCS 1992)
fields.aiRole: Produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model as part of an OpenAI evaluation on open research problems. The release README says the vast majority of results used one fixed procedure, averaging about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result; this result is not among the README's stated exceptions (the Riemann zeta zero-free region work and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties). The manuscript is authored as OpenAI with no human author named. The release itself credits Gaia Carenini (ECCC TR26-229, public 5 October 2026) with priority for the threshold-existence result and presents this family as an alternative proof plus sharper variance and computability results.

fields.name: The Euclidean-complete affine Bernstein problem in dimensions three through nine
fields.field: Geometric PDE; affine maximal hypersurfaces
fields.statement: Let $u$ be smooth with positive-definite Hessian on an open convex $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ and solve the affine maximal equation $U^{ij}w_{ij}=0$, $U^{ij}=\det(D^2u)(D^2u)^{-1}_{ij}$, $w=(\det D^2u)^{-(n+1)/(n+2)}$, the Euler equation of affine area. Chern asked whether an entire such surface ($n=2$) must be an elliptic paraboloid; Calabi proved it under Euclidean and affine completeness, and Trudinger and Wang proved the Euclidean-complete surface case in 2000, reduced higher dimensions to a uniform strict-convexity estimate, and exhibited a singular nonquadratic weak solution in dimension ten. For $n\ge3$, if the graph of $u$ is complete for the induced Euclidean metric, must $\Omega=\mathbb R^n$ and $u$ be quadratic, and in which dimensions?
fields.posedBy: Shiing-Shen Chern (Affine minimal hypersurfaces, 1977 seminar, published 1979) for surfaces; the higher-dimensional Euclidean-complete form follows Trudinger and Wang (Invent. Math. 2000)
fields.ageNote: Chern's question concerns surfaces and was posed at a 1977 seminar published in 1979. The manuscripts call the higher-dimensional statement the Euclidean-complete affine Bernstein conjecture without naming who first stated it for n >= 3.

fields.name: Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties
fields.field: Arithmetic geometry: Hodge classes, reduction and rational Tate classes
fields.statement: Let $A$ be an abelian variety of dimension $d$ over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ with good reduction $A_0$ at a $p$-adic place, and $\gamma$ a rational Hodge class in $H^{2r}(A(\mathbb C),\mathbb Q(r))$. Deligne's absolute-Hodge theorem gives compatible specializations of $\gamma$ to $\ell$-adic cohomology of $A_0$ for $\ell\ne p$ and to crystalline cohomology, but the reduction may acquire divisors that do not lift. Milne conjectured that the specialized class nevertheless behaves rationally, which he showed equivalent (for CM abelian varieties) to the existence of a good theory of rational Tate classes. For every list of divisors $D_1,\dots,D_{d-r}$ on $A_0$, is the intersection number of the specialized $\gamma$ with $D_1\cdots D_{d-r}$ one and the same rational number in every $\ell$-adic and in the crystalline realization?
fields.posedBy: J. S. Milne (weak form in his 2000 Langlands-Rapoport notes; pairing form in 2007 AIM notes and Conjecture 4.1 of Rational Tate classes, Mosc. Math. J. 2009)

fields.name: The Kannan-Tetali-Vempala conjecture for simple undirected graphs
fields.field: Markov chain mixing time; sampling graphs with given degrees
fields.statement: For a graphical degree vector $d=(d_1,\dots,d_n)$, let $\Omega_d$ be the simple undirected graphs on $\{1,\dots,n\}$ with degrees $d$. The switch chain removes two disjoint edges and inserts a different perfect matching on their four endpoints when both new edges are absent. Kannan, Tetali and Vempala began this program for bipartite graphs and suggested broad applicability; rapid mixing was then proved for regular sequences (Cooper-Dyer-Greenhill) and for P-stable families, and the bipartite case was settled in 2026. The modern form of the conjecture (Erdos, Greenhill, Mezei, Miklos, Soltesz and Soukup, Conjecture 1.1) asks for rapid mixing for every realizable degree sequence in the bipartite, directed and simple undirected models. Does the switch chain on $\Omega_d$ mix in time polynomial in $n$ for every graphical $d$?

fields.name: The CKLW strong-locality conjecture for strongly rational unitary vertex operator algebras
fields.field: Chiral conformal field theory: vertex operator algebras and conformal nets
fields.statement: A simple unitary vertex operator algebra $V$ is CKLW-strongly local if its fields satisfy polynomial energy bounds and the von Neumann algebras $A_V(I)$ generated by the closed smeared fields $\overline{Y(a,f)}$ with $\operatorname{supp}f\subset I$ commute for disjoint intervals of the circle, so that $V$ generates a conformal net. Carpi, Kawahigashi, Longo and Weiner proved this for unitary affine, Virasoro and moonshine VOAs and conjectured it for every simple unitary VOA (Conjecture 8.18). Commuting unbounded fields need not give commuting von Neumann algebras, so the point is analytic. Is every simple unitary vertex operator algebra strongly local?

fields.name: The purely cosmetic surgery conjecture for knots in the three-sphere
fields.field: Low-dimensional topology: Dehn surgery on knots
fields.statement: For a knot $K\subset S^3$ and a slope $r\in\mathbb{Q}\cup\{\infty\}$, let $S^3_r(K)$ be the oriented manifold obtained by Dehn surgery. Two distinct slopes $r\ne s$ are purely cosmetic if $S^3_r(K)$ and $S^3_s(K)$ are orientation-preservingly homeomorphic. Gordon conjectured (as part of his cosmetic filling conjecture) that this never happens for a nontrivial knot; the question is Bleiler's Problem 1.81(A) in Kirby's list. Known before this work: the meridional case (Gordon-Luecke), same-sign pairs (Wu), the reduction to opposite slopes $\pm 2$ or $\pm 1/q$ (Ni-Wu, Hanselman), exclusion of $\pm 1/q$ (Daemi-Lidman-Miller Eismeier), and verification for many families and all knots up to about 19 crossings. Does every nontrivial knot $K\subset S^3$ satisfy: $S^3_r(K)\cong S^3_s(K)$ orientation-preservingly implies $r=s$?

fields.name: The logarithmic exponent of the off-diagonal Ramsey numbers r(s,t) for fixed s at least 5
fields.field: Extremal and probabilistic combinatorics: Ramsey numbers
fields.statement: For fixed $s$, the Ramsey number $r(s,t)$ is the least $N$ such that every graph on $N$ vertices contains $K_s$ or an independent set of size $t$. Ajtai, Komlos and Szemeredi (1980) proved $r(s,t)=O_s(t^{s-1}/(\log t)^{s-2})$, and Erdos asked for the true order of growth: for $s=3$ it is $t^2/\log t$ (Kim 1995), Erdos Problem #166 asked for $r(4,t)\gg t^3/(\log t)^{O(1)}$ (Mattheus-Verstraete), and Erdos Problem #986 asked for $r(s,t)\gg t^{s-1}/(\log t)^{c(s)}$, which Bradac proved in 2026 with $c=2s-4$. That left the power of $\log t$ between $s-2$ and $2s-4$. For fixed $s\ge5$, what is the exponent $\theta_s$ with $r(s,t)=t^{s-1}/(\log t)^{\theta_s+o(1)}$; in particular, is the Ajtai-Komlos-Szemeredi upper bound sharp up to $(\log t)^{o(1)}$?
fields.posedBy: Classical problem of P. Erdos on the order of r(s,t) for fixed s (Erdos Problems #165, #166, #986; general case per Chung and Graham, 1998); upper bound by Ajtai, Komlos and Szemeredi (1980)
fields.ageNote: erdosproblems.com, citing Chung and Graham, dates Erdos's general conjecture on the polynomial order of r(s,t) to 1947. The sharper question of the exact logarithmic exponent is a natural refinement left open by Bradac (2026); the manuscripts give no source posing it as stated, so yearPosed is left empty.

fields.name: Hopkins' chromatic splitting conjecture (weak and odd-prime strong forms)
fields.field: Stable homotopy theory: chromatic homotopy
fields.statement: Fix a prime $p$, let $L_{n-1}$ be localization at $E(n-1)$ and $L_{K(n)}$ localization at Morava $K$-theory. Hopkins' chromatic splitting conjecture, recorded by Hovey (1995, Conjecture 4.2), describes the chromatic overlap $L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge$. Its weak form asserts that for the $p$-completion $X$ of a finite spectrum the canonical map $L_{n-1}X\to L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}X$ has a homotopy retraction (finite-input form: Beaudry-Goerss-Henn, Conjecture 1.1.11). Its strong form prescribes an explicit splitting of $L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge$ into suspended localized spheres indexed by an exterior algebra; Beaudry disproved this at $n=p=2$, and Barthel-Beaudry (2019, Conjecture 6.3) retain it at odd primes. Both forms were known through height two at odd primes. Does the canonical map split for all $n$ and $p$, and does the overlap decompose as predicted at odd primes?
fields.posedBy: M. J. Hopkins, recorded by M. Hovey, Bousfield localization functors and Hopkins' chromatic splitting conjecture (1995), Conjecture 4.2; refined by Barthel-Beaudry (2019) and Beaudry-Goerss-Henn

fields.name: The Ajtai-Erdos-Komlos-Szemeredi conjecture on independent sets in K_r-free graphs
fields.field: Extremal graph theory: independence number
fields.statement: Every graph with $n$ vertices and average degree $d$ has an independent set of size at least $n/(d+1)$, and disjoint cliques show this is sharp. Ajtai, Komlos and Szemeredi (1980) proved that triangle-free graphs have $\alpha(G)\gg n\log d/d$, and Shearer sharpened the constant to $1-o(1)$. For fixed $r\ge4$, does every $K_r$-free graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $d$ have an independent set of size $\Omega_r(n\log d/d)$?

fields.name: The Alon-Krivelevich-Sudakov conjecture: graphs with a fixed forbidden subgraph have chromatic number O(Delta/log Delta)
fields.field: Graph coloring: sparse and F-free graphs
fields.statement: Every graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ has $\chi(G)\le\Delta+1$. Johansson (1996) proved $\chi(G)=O(\Delta/\log\Delta)$ for triangle-free graphs, and Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov (1999) extended this to graphs with sparse neighborhoods. For general fixed $F$, and already for $F=K_4$, the best bounds carried an extra $\log\log\Delta$ factor. Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov (1999, Conjecture 3.1) conjectured: for every fixed graph $F$ there is $C_F$ such that every $F$-free graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ has chromatic number at most $C_F\Delta/\log\Delta$. fields.name: Polynomial-time approximate counting and uniform sampling of contingency tables with arbitrary margins
fields.field: Approximate counting and sampling (FPRAS, Markov chains)
fields.statement: For margins $r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}^m$, $c\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}^n$ with equal totals, let $\Omega(r,c)$ be the nonnegative integer $m\times n$ matrices with these row and column sums (optionally with individual cell bounds $b_{ij}$, zero bounds allowed). Exact counting is #P-complete even for two rows (Dyer-Kannan-Mount 1997). Polynomial approximate counting and sampling were known for two rows, for a fixed number of rows, for sufficiently large or dense margins, and for sparse margins, but not jointly polynomial in both dimensions and the binary length of the margins; Cryan, Dyer and Randall (2010) named unrestricted cell-bounded counting as open. Is there a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for $|\Omega|$, and a polynomial-time almost-uniform sampler, for arbitrary binary-encoded margins (and cell bounds) with both dimensions part of the input?

fields.ageNote: No single paper is cited as posing the problem in full generality. fields.name: Quasi-isometric rigidity of virtually polycyclic groups (the Eskin-Fisher-Whyte lattice-recognition conjecture)
fields.field: Geometric group theory: quasi-isometric rigidity
fields.statement: Gromov's polynomial growth theorem implies that a finitely generated group quasi-isometric to a virtually nilpotent group is virtually nilpotent. For solvable groups of exponential growth, quasi-isometric rigidity was known only for special classes: Sol and lamplighters (Eskin-Fisher-Whyte), nondegenerate abelian-by-abelian groups (Peng), SOL-like groups (Dymarz; Dymarz-Fisher-Xie), and under stronger hypotheses such as commability (Le Boudec). Shalom showed such a group virtually has infinite abelianization. Eskin, Fisher and Whyte (2007) conjectured that a finitely generated group quasi-isometric to a lattice in a connected simply connected solvable Lie group is virtually a lattice in a possibly different such Lie group; equivalently: if a finitely generated group $H$ is quasi-isometric to a finitely generated virtually polycyclic group, must $H$ be virtually polycyclic?

fields.name: Jacobsthal's quadratic-bound question: is h(k) = O(k^2)?
fields.field: Sieve theory: Jacobsthal's function
fields.statement: Let $h(k)$ be the least $m$ such that every interval of $m$ consecutive integers contains an integer coprime to any prescribed positive integer with at most $k$ distinct prime factors. Brun's sieve gives $h(k)\ll k^{C}$; Iwaniec's linear-sieve work gave $h(k)\ll k^2\log^2k$ (1978), improving Vaughan's $k^2\log^4k$; the best lower bound, from Ford, Green, Konyagin, Maynard and Tao, is about $k(\log k)^2\log\log\log k/\log\log k$. Jacobsthal asked, and Erdos recorded (1962; Erdos Problem #970), whether the upper bound is quadratic. Is $h(k)\ll k^2$?
fields.posedBy: E. Jacobsthal (papers from 1960); recorded by P. Erdos (1962, p. 163) and as Erdos Problem #970
fields.ageNote: Jacobsthal studied the function in papers beginning in 1960; the manuscript cites Erdos (1962) as the record of Jacobsthal's question, and erdosproblems.com lists it as #970 citing Erdos (1965).

Its statement was read here: there is C > 0 such that for every k >= 1 some m <= C k^2 has the property that, for every positive n with at most k distinct prime factors and every integer start a, one of a, a+1, ..., a+m-1 is coprime to n. That is exactly Jacobsthal's question. The separate challenge JacobsthalImproved (erdos_970_iterated_log, same solution module, not in the formalization catalogue) states the paper's stronger bound C k^2/(log log 3k)^2. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: $h(k)\le Ck^2/(\log\log(3k))^2$ for an absolute constant $C$ and every $k\ge1$, uniformly over prime sets and interval positions; in particular $h(k)\ll k^2$, answering Jacobsthal's question and improving Iwaniec's $k^2\log^2k$. The proof pushes the linear sieve to its limiting parameter, keeping a boundary term, and controls the discrepancy with the actual residue classes through an inverse estimate and stopped counts. The constant is not explicit, and the true order of $h(k)$ (Erdos #970's broader ask) is not determined: the gap to the lower bound near $k(\log k)^2$ remains.

fields.name: The weak inhomogeneous Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture
fields.field: Metric Diophantine approximation
fields.statement: Koukoulopoulos and Maynard (2020) proved the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture: for $\psi:\mathbb{N}\to[0,\infty)$ with $\sum_q\phi(q)\psi(q)/q=\infty$, almost every $x$ has infinitely many reduced fractions $a/q$ with $|x-a/q|<\psi(q)/q$. For a fixed shift $\gamma$, unweighted divergence does not suffice without monotonicity (Ramirez; Chow-Hauke-Pollington-Ramirez), and the coprime-numerator inhomogeneous version is false. The weak inhomogeneous conjecture (Yu 2021, Question 1.2; Chow-Technau 2024, Conjecture 1.22; Beresnevich-Hauke-Velani 2024, Conjecture 2), proved for rational shifts by Beresnevich-Hauke-Velani, asks: for every fixed $\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$ and every $\psi$ with $\sum_q\phi(q)\psi(q)/q=\infty$, does $\|qx-\gamma\|<\psi(q)$ hold for infinitely many $q$, for almost every $x$?

fields.name: Existence of bounded-degree F2 coboundary expanders in every dimension
fields.field: High-dimensional expanders: coboundary expansion
fields.statement: A finite pure $d$-dimensional simplicial complex $X$ is an $\varepsilon$-coboundary expander over $\mathbb{F}_2$ if, with the standard weighted norms, $\|\delta f\|\ge\varepsilon\,\mathrm{dist}(f,B^i(X))$ for every $i$-cochain $f$ and all $i<d$; this forces vanishing cohomology below $d$. Linial-Meshulam random complexes, Latin-square complexes (Lubotzky-Meshulam) and Steiner-system complexes (Lubotzky-Luria-Rosenthal) are coboundary expanders, but their vertex degrees grow. Bounded-degree cosystolic expanders exist in every dimension (Kaufman-Kazhdan-Lubotzky; Evra-Kaufman), and Chapman-Lubotzky (2025) built bounded-degree two-dimensional coboundary expanders. Gromov (2010) asked for large complexes with bounded degree and uniform filling, and Chapman-Lubotzky posed the problem in general: for every $d\ge3$, are there arbitrarily large bounded-degree $d$-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_2$ coboundary expanders with uniform constant?

fields.name: Scale invariance implies local conformal invariance for a class of four-dimensional unitary QFTs
fields.field: Axiomatic quantum field theory: scale and conformal symmetry
fields.statement:
In a scale-invariant QFT with symmetric conserved stress tensor $T_{\mu
u}$, the dilatation current is $D_\mu=x^
u T_{\mu
u}-V_\mu$ with $T^\mu{}_\mu=\partial^\mu V_\mu$; the theory is conformal if $T$ can be improved to a traceless tensor, for instance when $\partial^\mu V_\mu=\Box L$ for a local scalar $L$. Zamolodchikov and Polchinski (1988) proved that scale implies conformal invariance in two-dimensional unitary theories under mild assumptions, and Polchinski raised the four-dimensional case. Perturbative results (Fortin-Grinstein-Stergiou, Jack-Osborn) and dilaton-based arguments (Luty-Polchinski-Rattazzi; Dymarsky-Komargodski-Schwimmer-Theisen) support it but leave gaps. In a four-dimensional unitary, positive-energy QFT with a Poincare- and scale-invariant vacuum, does scale invariance imply conformal invariance?

fields.ageNote: Polchinski's 1988 paper proved the two-dimensional case and discussed the four-dimensional question; the manuscript cites it with Zamolodchikov (1986) for the history. The question is also linked to earlier improvement work of Callan, Coleman and Jackiw (1970).

fields.name: Quillen's conjecture on the poset of elementary abelian p-subgroups
fields.field: Finite group theory; subgroup complexes and homotopy
fields.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group, $p$ a prime, and $\mathcal A_p(G)$ the poset of nontrivial elementary abelian $p$-subgroups of $G$. Quillen showed that a nontrivial normal $p$-subgroup ($O_p(G)\ne1$) makes $\mathcal A_p(G)$ contractible, and proved the converse for solvable groups, $p$-rank at most two and groups of Lie type in defining characteristic. Aschbacher and Smith reduced the problem for $p>5$ to unitary-group cases and later work (Piterman, Smith, Diaz Ramos) narrowed it further, settling the rational form for odd primes, but the prime $2$ remained open. Conjecture: if $\mathcal A_p(G)$ is contractible, must $O_p(G)\ne1$?

The proof relies on published and preprint reductions (Aschbacher-Smith, Piterman-Smith, Piterman 2026 arXiv:2607.27500, Diaz Ramos 2026 arXiv:2303.15613v6) plus new frame-cycle constructions; it uses the classification of finite simple groups through those reductions. fields.field: Discrete and computational geometry; k-sets
fields.statement: For a set $P$ of $n$ points in the plane in general position ($n$ even), a halving line passes through two points of $P$ and leaves $(n-2)/2$ points on each side. Lovasz (1971) and Erdos, Lovasz, Simmons and Straus (1973) introduced the problem of determining the maximum number $h(n)$ of halving lines (and more generally of $k$-sets), proving $O(n^{3/2})$ and constructing $\Omega(n\log n)$. Dey (1998) proved $h(n)=O(n^{4/3})$; the best lower bound is $n e^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log n})}$ (Toth, Nivasch). What is the true order of $h(n)$; in particular, can Dey's exponent $4/3$ be improved?
fields.posedBy: L. Lovasz, On the number of halving lines (1971); P. Erdos, L. Lovasz, A. Simmons and E. G. Straus, Dissection graphs of planar point sets (1973)
fields.ageNote: The halving-line count goes back to Lovasz (1971) and the k-set problem to Erdos, Lovasz, Simmons and Straus (1973). The specific target of beating Dey's 1998 exponent 4/3 is the open part addressed here.

The constants and exponent are ineffective; no numerical value of $\varepsilon$ is given. It does not determine the order of $h(n)$, which could still lie anywhere between $n e^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log n})}$ and $n^{4/3-\varepsilon}$.

fields.name: The Gromov-Lawson conjecture: closed aspherical manifolds admit no metric of positive scalar curvature
fields.field: Scalar curvature; topology of manifolds
fields.statement: A closed manifold is aspherical if its universal cover is contractible. Gromov and Lawson (1983), with Dirac-operator methods, and Schoen and Yau, with minimal hypersurfaces, obstructed positive scalar curvature on tori and enlargeable manifolds; the conjecture that no closed aspherical manifold carries a metric of positive scalar curvature was open beyond dimension five (Chodosh-Li, Gromov). Hanke (2011, Conjecture 2.9) formulated the stronger homological form: if a closed oriented $n$-manifold $M$ admits positive scalar curvature, the classifying map sends its rational fundamental class to zero in $H_n(B\pi_1(M);\mathbb Q)$. Does any closed aspherical manifold admit a metric of positive scalar curvature, and are positive-scalar-curvature manifolds always rationally inessential?
fields.posedBy: M. Gromov and H. B. Lawson, Positive scalar curvature and the Dirac operator on complete Riemannian manifolds, Publ. Math. IHES 58 (1983); homological form: B. Hanke (2011), Conjecture 2.9
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Gromov-Lawson 1983 for the obstruction programme and names the corollary the Gromov-Lawson aspherical conjecture; the homological form is Hanke 2011, Conjecture 2.9, also stated by Yau (2000) and Gromov (2023).

Placed level with the Borel conjecture in dimension four (60), below Cannon's conjecture (62) and above the Eilenberg-Ganea conjecture (55).

fields.name: Gromov's integral scalar-curvature bound for simplicial volume
fields.shortName: Gromov's scalar curvature vs simplicial volume
fields.field: Scalar curvature; simplicial volume and bounded cohomology
fields.statement: For a closed connected oriented $n$-manifold $M$ let $\|M\|$ be its real simplicial volume, and for a Riemannian metric $g$ let $\mathrm{Scal}_g^-=\max\{0,-\mathrm{Scal}_g\}$. In 1986 Gromov (Large Riemannian manifolds, Conjecture 3.A, Remark (B), Equation (8')) proposed bounding simplicial volume by the scale-invariant integral $\int_M(\mathrm{Scal}_g^-)^{n/2}dV_g$; equivalently, $\mathrm{Scal}_g\ge-\kappa^2$ should force $\|M\|\le C_n\kappa^n\mathrm{Vol}_g(M)$. Partial results covered bounded unit-ball volumes in the universal cover (Braun-Sauer), Kahler surfaces (Min-Zheng-Zhu) and qualitative vanishing for spin universal covers. Is there $a_n>0$ with $\int_M(\mathrm{Scal}_g^-)^{n/2}dV_g\ge a_n\|M\|$ for every closed $n$-manifold and every metric?
fields.posedBy: M. Gromov, Large Riemannian manifolds, in Curvature and Topology of Riemannian Manifolds (1986), Conjecture 3.A, Remark (B), Equation (8')

fields.name: The Bass trace conjecture for complex group rings of all discrete groups
fields.field: K-theory of group rings; Hattori-Stallings traces
fields.statement: For a discrete group $G$ and an idempotent matrix $e$ over the group ring $\mathbb CG$, the Hattori-Stallings trace assigns to each conjugacy class $C$ the coefficient $\sum_{g\in C}\sum_i e_{ii}(g)$, giving a map $K_0(\mathbb CG)\to\bigoplus_{C}\mathbb C\,C$. Bass (1976) conjectured that for the integral group ring the trace is supported at the identity; the complex form asks that it vanish on every conjugacy class of infinite-order elements. Berrick, Chatterji and Mislin (2004) also stated an $\ell^1$ form (finite support on finite-order classes for idempotents over $\ell^1(G)$), proved when the Bost assembly map is rationally surjective. Known for many classes of groups but open in general. Does the Hattori-Stallings trace of every finitely generated projective $\mathbb CG$-module vanish on infinite-order conjugacy classes, for every group $G$?
fields.posedBy: H. Bass, Euler characteristics and characters of discrete groups (Inventiones 1976); complex and l1 forms: Berrick, Chatterji and Mislin, Math. Annalen (2004), Conjectures 2.1 and 2.2
fields.aiRole: Produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model as part of the openai/math release (pinned commit adc7f12). The manuscript is authored as OpenAI with no human author named. A Lean formalization of the complex group-ring theorem accompanies it (Comparator challenge BassTrace, listed in lean/formalization.yaml). The l1 strengthening is a separate 5 October manuscript without Lean.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Its statement was read here: for every group $G$ and every class $x$ in a module-level $K_0(\mathbb C[G])$, the Hattori-Stallings trace vanishes at every infinite-order conjugacy class and its support lies in finite-order classes. That is the complex headline. Not rebuilt here. The $\ell^1$-Bass theorem of the 5 October companion is stronger and is NOT formalized; the manuscript says its proof does not use the complex theorem as input.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 (24 September): for every discrete group $G$, every $x\in K_0(\mathbb CG)$ and every infinite-order $g$, $\mathrm{HS}_G(x)([g])=0$; the integral (identity-support) form for $\mathbb ZG$ is deduced in Section 9. The 5 October companion proves the $\ell^1$-Bass conjecture (BCM 2004, Conjecture 2.2): the trace of every idempotent over $\ell^1(G)$ is supported on finitely many finite-order classes, with no assembly hypothesis, which implies the complex form. Neither manuscript addresses the reduced $C^*$-algebra (the Kadison-Kaplansky question), where this release separately claims a counterexample.

fields.name: Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture for torsion-free groups in characteristic zero
fields.field: Group rings; idempotents
fields.statement: Let $G$ be a torsion-free group and $k$ a field. The idempotent conjecture, commonly attributed to Kaplansky, asserts that the group ring $kG$ has no idempotents other than $0$ and $1$. For $k=\mathbb C$ it follows from the Bass conjecture or from Baum-Connes for $G$, and it was known for many classes of groups but not in general; it would also follow from Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture. In characteristic zero: if $G$ is torsion-free and $R$ a field (or domain) of characteristic zero, is every $e\in RG$ with $e^2=e$ equal to $0$ or $1$?
fields.posedBy: Attributed to I. Kaplansky; the manuscript cites the formulation in Oinert and Wagner (2023), Problem 3
fields.ageNote: The manuscript calls it the idempotent conjecture commonly attributed to Kaplansky and cites only a 2023 paper (Oinert-Wagner, Problem 3), so it gives no posing date. It is usually traced to Kaplansky's problem lists of the 1950s to 1970; the curator should confirm and set yearPosed.

fields.name: Maximum-cardinality matching in general graphs in almost-linear time
fields.field: Graph algorithms; matching
fields.statement: Given a simple undirected graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, find a maximum-cardinality matching. Edmonds' blossom algorithm gave polynomial time; Micali and Vazirani (1980) achieved $O(m\sqrt n)$, which remained the best combinatorial bound for sparse general graphs, while algebraic methods give $O(n^\omega)$. After almost-linear-time exact max flow (Chen, Kyng, Liu, Peng, Probst Gutenberg and Sachdeva, 2022) gave almost-linear bipartite matching, the general-graph case, where odd cycles (blossoms) defeat the flow formulation, remained open. Can a maximum matching in a general graph be found in $m^{1+o(1)}$ time?
fields.posedBy: Long-standing open algorithmic question (no single poser cited in the manuscript); benchmark bound Micali and Vazirani (1980), bipartite case settled by Chen et al. (2022)
fields.ageNote: The manuscript gives no reference that poses the question; it describes the history from Edmonds through Micali-Vazirani (1980) to almost-linear bipartite matching (2022). Beating O(m sqrt n) for sparse general graphs has been open since 1980, so yearPosed could defensibly be 1980; left null pending a citable statement.

fields.name: The threshold bound state conjecture for SU(N) supersymmetric matrix quantum mechanics
fields.field: Supersymmetric matrix quantum mechanics; spectral theory
fields.statement: The $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ BFSS model is the maximally supersymmetric matrix quantum mechanics with nine Hermitian $N\times N$ matrices and sixteen fermionic partners, obtained by reducing ten-dimensional super Yang-Mills to one dimension. De Wit, Luscher and Nicolai (1989) showed its spectrum is $[0,\infty)$. Witten (1996) predicted that, after removing the center of mass, there is exactly one normalizable zero-energy state for every $N$ (the D0-brane bound state), a prediction central to the BFSS matrix-theory conjecture. Index computations (Yi, Sethi-Stern, Moore-Nekrasov-Shatashvili) supported it, but a rigorous proof of existence and uniqueness was open. For every $N\ge2$, does the relative $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Hamiltonian have a kernel of dimension exactly one?
fields.posedBy: E. Witten, Bound states of strings and p-branes, Nuclear Physics B (1996), Section 4.2; central to Banks, Fischler, Shenker and Susskind (1997)
fields.aiRole: Produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model as part of the openai/math release (pinned commit adc7f12). fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: abstract, introduction and Theorem 1.1 of the TeX source, read against Witten's prediction as cited. Theorem 1.1 states $\dim\ker H_N=1$ for every $N\ge2$, with $H_N$ the self-adjoint operator of the closed supercharge quadratic form on the gauge-invariant smooth compactly supported core; the kernel is $\mathrm{Spin}(9)$-invariant and even. The result is for that specific operator realization; the paper contrasts it with other realizations (Boulton et al.). The proof passes from a BMN mass-deformed Fredholm index to the undeformed kernel with cluster estimates. Not refereed here. No Lean formalization.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every integer $N\ge2$, the relative undeformed $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ BFSS Hamiltonian (closure of $\frac1{16}\sum_\alpha\|Q_\alpha\Psi\|^2$ on gauge-invariant states in $L^2(\mathbb R^{9(N^2-1)})$ tensor a Clifford module) has a one-dimensional kernel, consisting of $\mathrm{Spin}(9)$-invariant even states. This gives both existence and uniqueness of the threshold bound state at each finite $N$. Constants depend on $N$; nothing is claimed about large-$N$ limits or the matrix-theory conjecture itself.

fields.significanceNote: The existence and uniqueness of the D0-brane threshold bound state is a well-known open problem at the interface of string theory and rigorous spectral theory, open for three decades despite strong index evidence. fields.name: The BFSS exclusion of positive-energy normalizable states in the relative SU(2) model
fields.field: Supersymmetric matrix quantum mechanics; embedded eigenvalues
fields.statement: For the relative $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ BFSS Hamiltonian (supersymmetric quantum mechanics of three $9$-vectors with quartic potential $\sum_{a<b}|x^a\wedge x^b|^2$ and sixteen fermions per color), de Wit, Luscher and Nicolai (1989) proved the spectrum is $[0,\infty)$ and left open whether normalizable eigenstates lie inside it. Banks, Fischler, Shenker and Susskind (1997, Section 5, after Equation (5.4)) stated that besides the zero-energy threshold states 'No other normalizable bound states can occur'. Danielsson, Ferretti and Sundborg had found metastable excited states in a Born-Oppenheimer approximation. Does the relative $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Hamiltonian have normalizable eigenstates of positive energy?
fields.posedBy: T. Banks, W. Fischler, S. H. Shenker and L. Susskind, M theory as a matrix model: a conjecture, Phys. Rev. D (1997), Section 5; open question in de Wit, Luscher and Nicolai (1989)
