fields.name: Beauville's splitting conjecture for two integrable summands
fields.field: Complex and Kahler geometry; split tangent bundles and foliations
fields.statement: Let $X$ be a compact Kahler manifold with a holomorphic splitting $T_X=\bigoplus_i E_i$ such that partial sums of the summands are integrable. Beauville (2000, Section 2.3) conjectured that the universal cover of $X$ then splits as a product $\prod Y_i$ compatibly with the decomposition, and proved it for Kahler-Einstein manifolds and surfaces. Later work covered line-bundle summands with integrable complement (Brunella-Pereira-Touzet), Hermitian-flat summands (Pereira-Touzet, Druel-Pereira-Pym-Touzet) and foliations with a compact leaf of finite holonomy. For two summands the hypothesis is that both are integrable. If $T_X=E_1\oplus E_2$ with both summands integrable of positive rank, is the universal cover a compatible product $Y_1\times Y_2$?

fields.name: Hoering's conjecture: tangent-bundle summands on rationally connected manifolds are integrable
fields.field: Algebraic geometry; rationally connected varieties, foliations
fields.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth rationally connected projective complex manifold with a holomorphic splitting $T_X=E_1\oplus E_2$ into positive-rank subbundles. Hoering (2007) proved that if one summand is integrable then $X\cong X_1\times X_2$ compatibly, and conjectured (2008, Conjecture 1.2) that at least one summand is always integrable; Campana-Peternell had settled small ranks on Fano manifolds, and Hoering (2026, Conjecture 1.5) states that both summands are integrable in the smooth rationally connected case, after proving it for Fano type. Is every summand of such a splitting integrable, so that $X$ is a compatible product?

fields.name: Patterson's conjecture on the first moment of cubic Gauss sums over primes
fields.field: Analytic number theory; cubic Gauss sums and metaplectic forms
fields.statement: For a rational prime $p\equiv1\pmod 3$, Kummer studied the cubic sum $S_p=\sum_{x\bmod p}e(x^3/p)$ and observed a bias toward positive values. Heath-Brown and Patterson (1979) proved that the normalized sums are equidistributed on the circle, so any bias lives below the prime-counting scale. Patterson (1978) predicted a bias of exact order $X^{5/6}/\log X$; Heath-Brown's cubic large sieve gave $O(X^{5/6+\epsilon})$ and Dunn-Radziwill (2024) proved a smoothed asymptotic under GRH. With $G(\pi)$ the normalized cubic Gauss sum at a primary Eisenstein prime and $c_*=(2\pi)^{2/3}/(3\Gamma(2/3))$, is $\sum_{N\pi\le X}G(\pi)\sim\frac65c_*X^{5/6}/\log X$ unconditionally?
fields.posedBy: S. J. Patterson (1978); first-moment normalization as stated by Dunn and Radziwill (2024, display after Equation (1.8)) and Wan (2021, Conjecture 4.13)
fields.aiRole: Produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model as part of the openai/math release (pinned commit adc7f12). Its statement was read here: with Gauss sums at primary primes of $\mathbb Z[\omega]$ built from the cubic residue symbol and $e(\mathrm{Tr}(v/p))$, the sharp-cutoff sum over primary primes of norm at most $X$ minus $\frac65c_*X^{5/6}/\log X$ is $o(X^{5/6}/\log X)$; also the angular statements. That is the headline. Not rebuilt here. The manuscript notes that Dunn-Radziwill print the same constant in two inequivalent normalizations and identifies which one it proves.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: unconditionally, $\sum_{N\pi\le X,\ \pi\equiv1(3)\text{ prime}}G(\pi)=\frac65c_*X^{5/6}/\log X+o(X^{5/6}/\log X)$, over all primary Eisenstein primes; equivalently $\sum_{p\le X}S_p/(2\sqrt p)\sim\frac35c_*X^{5/6}/\log X$, matching Wan's Conjecture 4.13. Also cancellation in every fixed nonzero angular mode and for fixed powers $G(\pi)^k$ with $3\nmid k$, $|k|>1$. The error term is only little-oh, with no rate; powers $k$ divisible by 3 (part of Patterson's complementary conjecture) remain open. Uses the unconditional Dunn-Radziwill Voronoi formula, not their GRH estimates.

fields.name: A power saving in the Furstenberg-Sarkozy theorem (square-difference-free sets)
fields.field: Additive combinatorics; Furstenberg-Sarkozy theorem
fields.statement: Let $s(N)$ be the largest size of a set $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no two elements differing by a nonzero perfect square. Answering a question of Lovasz, Furstenberg and Sarkozy proved $s(N)=o(N)$. Quantitative bounds improved through Pintz-Steiger-Szemeredi and Bloom-Maynard to Green and Sawhney's $s(N)\ll N\exp(-c\sqrt{\log N})$, while Ruzsa-type constructions give $s(N)\gg N^{0.7334}$. Green and Sawhney asked whether a fixed power saving holds. Is there an absolute $c>0$ with $s(N)\ll N^{1-c}$?
fields.posedBy: B. Green and M. Sawhney, New bounds for the Furstenberg-Sarkozy theorem (arXiv:2411.17448), Section 1.1; the underlying problem originates with Lovasz
fields.ageNote: Green and Sawhney's arXiv preprint (2411.17448) dates from November 2024; the manuscript's bibliography lists it as 2025. The underlying density question goes back to Lovasz, answered qualitatively by Furstenberg (1977) and Sarkozy (1978).

The exponent is tiny and not computed, far from Ruzsa's lower-bound exponent $0.733$; the true exponent is not addressed.

fields.name: The Aaronson-Kuperberg unitary synthesis problem at constant diamond-norm error
fields.field: Quantum query complexity; oracle synthesis of unitaries
fields.statement: Aaronson and Kuperberg (2007) asked whether, for every $n$-qubit unitary $U$, there is a Boolean oracle $A$ such that a polynomial-time quantum algorithm with access to $A$ implements $U$. Aaronson (2021, Problem 6) named it the Unitary Synthesis Problem, called it wide open and conjectured a negative answer. Known results: state synthesis with one query (Irani et al., Rosenthal), a $2^{n/2}$-time upper bound for unitaries (Rosenthal), and one-query and parallel-query lower bounds (Lombardi-Ma-Wright). Is there a polynomial-size quantum oracle circuit family which, for every $n$-qubit $U$ and a suitable Boolean oracle depending on $U$, implements $U$ approximately?
fields.posedBy: S. Aaronson and G. Kuperberg, Quantum versus classical proofs and advice, Theory of Computing 3 (2007), Section 7, Problem (4); restated in Aaronson (2021), Problem 6
fields.aiRole: Produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model as part of the openai/math release (pinned commit adc7f12). The release README says results were produced by one fixed procedure averaging about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute each; this result is not among the README exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscript is authored as OpenAI with no human author named. No Lean formalization accompanies it.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: abstract, introduction and Theorem 1.1 of the TeX source, read against Aaronson's 2021 statement of Problem 6 (fetched for this check). Theorem 1.1 gives a circuit family generated in time polynomial in $n$ from $1^n$ (gates $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$; polynomial qubits, gates, queries and query length) such that for every $U$ some Boolean oracle yields full diamond-norm error at most $1/2$ (no factor $1/2$ in the norm). The paper calls this the constant-error formulation; Aaronson's statement does not fix the error, and smaller-error versions are not addressed. The oracle is existential with no efficient construction. Not refereed here. No Lean formalization.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are a polynomial $p$ and a deterministic algorithm outputting, on $1^n$, an oracle circuit $A_n$ with at most $p(n)$ qubits, gates and oracle calls and oracle input length at most $p(n)$, such that for every $U\in U(2^n)$ some $f$ gives $\|\Phi_{n,f}-\mathcal U\|_\diamond\le1/2$. The method is a recursive dimension reduction using one coherently controlled smaller synthesis per step. It does not achieve arbitrarily small error, does not give an efficient classical procedure for the oracle, and answers positively a question on which Aaronson (2021) had conjectured a negative answer.
fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: Polynomial-Time Unitary Synthesis from a Boolean Oracle
fields.significanceNote: The unitary synthesis problem is a well-known open question in quantum complexity, highlighted by Aaronson as wide open and tied to quantum circuit lower bounds; a positive answer even at a fixed constant error would surprise specialists, but the error level leaves part of the question open. Placed below mutually unbiased bases in dimension six (45) and the Sakoda-Sipser problem (45), above the approximation ratio for Boolean Max-k-CSP (15).

fields.name: Curtis's conjecture: the mod-2 stable Hurewicz image of the sphere is spanned by the Hopf- and Kervaire-invariant-one classes
fields.field: Stable homotopy theory
fields.statement: For $d>0$ let $h_d:\pi_d^S\to H_d(Q_0S^0;\mathbb F_2)$ be the mod-2 Hurewicz homomorphism into the homology of the basepoint component of $QS^0=\mathrm{colim}_r\Omega^rS^r$. The obvious elements with nonzero image are the Hopf-invariant-one classes $\eta,\nu,\sigma$ in degrees 1, 3, 7 and the Kervaire-invariant-one classes $\theta_j$ in degrees $2^{j+1}-2$, when they exist. Curtis (1975), in his study of the Dyer-Lashof and lambda algebras, conjectured that nothing else is detected; May (1977) recorded a gap, found by Wellington, in the proposed proof. The conjecture implies Eccles's conjecture for spheres. Is the image of $\bigoplus_{d>0}h_d$ spanned over $\mathbb F_2$ by the Hurewicz images of $\eta,\nu,\sigma$ and of the Kervaire-invariant-one classes that exist?
fields.posedBy: Edward B. Curtis
fields.ageNote: Curtis, The Dyer-Lashof algebra and the Lambda-algebra, Illinois J. Math. 19 (1975); May, Infinite loop space theory, Bull. AMS 83 (1977), p. 484, footnote 3, records the gap found by Wellington.

This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The single manuscript (September 25, 2026) is the whole family.

The proof (last nonzero homology suspension, weight decomposition through Dickson-algebra modules, a Steenrod-module obstruction, Kuhn's lifting theorem and Browder's identification of Kervaire classes) was not refereed. No Lean formalization accompanies this manuscript. The paper says its exclusion of fourth powers (Section 4) is already present in Eccles-Zare, and Corollary 1.3 uses the Hill-Hopkins-Ravenel nonexistence theorem as an input.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: the image of $\bigoplus_{d>0}h_d$ is spanned over $\mathbb F_2$ by the Hurewicz images of $\eta,\nu,\sigma$ and of the Kervaire-invariant-one classes $\theta_j$ (degree $2^{j+1}-2$) whenever they exist; no existence is posited. fields.name: The spacetime Penrose inequality: invariant ADM mass bounds the minimal area enclosing a trapped boundary, for general asymptotically flat initial data
fields.field: Mathematical general relativity
fields.statement: Penrose (1973), as a test of weak cosmic censorship, argued that a black hole of horizon area $A$ requires total mass at least $\sqrt{A/16\pi}$. The time-symmetric (Riemannian) case was proved in dimension three by Huisken-Ilmanen and Bray, and in higher dimensions by Bray-Lee and Bi-Zhu. For initial data $(M^n,g,K)$ with nonzero second fundamental form the bound with the apparent horizon's own area fails (Ben-Dov; Carrasco-Mars), and the accepted formulation, following Bray and Khuri, uses the least area $A_{\min}$ of surfaces enclosing the trapped boundary. It was known in spherical symmetry, for some cohomogeneity-one data, and with a non-sharp constant (Allen-Bryden-Kazaras-Khuri, 2025). Does every asymptotically flat initial-data set obeying the dominant energy condition, with weakly trapped boundary, satisfy $m\ge\frac12(A_{\min}/\omega_{n-1})^{(n-2)/(n-1)}$ for the invariant ADM mass $m$, with equality only for Schwarzschild?
fields.posedBy: Roger Penrose (heuristic inequality); enclosing-area initial-data formulation following Hubert Bray and Marcus Khuri
fields.ageNote: Penrose, Naked singularities, Ann. N.Y. Acad. Sci. 224 (1973). The enclosing-area form for non-time-symmetric data follows Bray-Khuri (2010, 2011) and the Ben-Dov (2004) and Carrasco-Mars (2010) counterexamples to apparent-horizon formulations.

fields.name: The charged spacetime Penrose inequality in upper-area form for Einstein-Maxwell initial data
fields.field: Mathematical general relativity
fields.statement: With electric and magnetic charge, $Q^2=Q_E^2+Q_B^2$, Penrose's heuristic suggests that a black hole of given area cannot have less mass than the Reissner-Nordstrom black hole of that area and charge. Does the upper-area inequality hold for general asymptotically flat initial data with arbitrary second fundamental form satisfying the charged dominant energy condition, with $A$ the least area enclosing a weakly trapped boundary, and is equality attained only by Reissner-Nordstrom?

fields.name: The asymptotically anti-de Sitter Penrose inequality for three-dimensional initial data with spherical conformal infinity
fields.field: Mathematical general relativity
fields.statement: With cosmological constant $-3$, the Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter relation $M=(r_h+r_h^3)/2$ and Penrose's 1973 argument suggest that asymptotically hyperbolic initial data with a trapped boundary of area $A$ have mass, in the sense of Wang and Chrusciel-Herzlich, at least $\frac12(r_A+r_A^3)$ with $r_A=\sqrt{A/4\pi}$. Even the time-symmetric case was known only for special classes: graphs (Dahl-Gicquaud-Sakovich, de Lima-Girao), small perturbations of Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter (Ambrozio; Khuri-Kopinski), and Neves showed inverse mean curvature flow cannot be used directly. Does every three-dimensional asymptotically anti-de Sitter initial-data set with spherical conformal infinity, the dominant energy condition and a weakly trapped boundary satisfy $m\ge\frac12(r_A+r_A^3)$ with $A$ the minimal enclosing area, with equality only for Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter?
fields.posedBy: Penrose's 1973 heuristic in the asymptotically anti-de Sitter setting; studied as a conjecture by Dahl, Gicquaud and Sakovich, Ambrozio, and Khuri and Kopinski, among others
fields.ageNote: The manuscript traces the inequality to Penrose (1973) and the mass of Wang and Chrusciel-Herzlich but cites no single source stating the asymptotically hyperbolic conjecture, so no year is set.

The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The family has thirteen manuscripts (September 27 and October 5, 2026); the October papers cite the September neutral theorem as an input, consistent with the README's note that some results build on earlier model results.

The paper says it makes no evolution or cosmic-censorship claim. No Lean formalization.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 (principal): under those hypotheses $m_{AH}\ge\frac12(r_A+r_A^3)$ with $A$ the full enclosing-area infimum, sharp; no maximality, compact topology or connectedness assumption. Equality on the stated horizon subclass identifies the original data as a spacelike hypersurface in Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter with the same mass. Companions: the maximal case with possibly disconnected boundary, and a local inequality for small maximal vacuum conformal perturbations of Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter using the horizon's own area. Not shown: higher dimensions, toroidal or higher-genus conformal infinity (the Lee-Neves regime), or timelikeness of the mass as a conclusion.

fields.name: Squarefree values of irreducible quartic polynomials, and (d-2)-power-free values in every degree d at least 4
fields.field: Analytic number theory, sieve methods
fields.statement: Let $f\in\mathbb Z[x]$ be irreducible of degree $d$ and $k\ge2$. If no prime $k$th power divides every value of $f$, one expects $f(n)$ to be $k$-free for a proportion $c_{f,k}=\prod_p(1-\rho_f(p^k)/p^k)>0$ of $n\le X$, where $\rho_f(q)$ counts roots mod $q$. Ricci proved this for $k\ge d$; Erdos (1953) and Hooley (1967) handled $k=d-1$, which includes squarefree values of cubics; Nair, Heath-Brown and Browning reached $k=d-2$ only for $d\ge9$. Erdos singled out the squarefreeness of $n^4+2$ in 1953 and returned to the $k=d-2$ obstacle in 1965. Does every irreducible integer quartic with no fixed prime-square divisor take squarefree values with the predicted density, and more generally does the $(d-2)$-free density hold in every degree $d\ge4$?
fields.posedBy: Paul Erdos (the case n^4 + 2 and the exponent d - 2 barrier)
fields.ageNote: Erdos, Arithmetical properties of polynomials, J. London Math. Soc. 28 (1953), p. 425, and Some recent advances and current problems in number theory (1965). The general squarefree-values conjecture is folklore; Granville derived it from abc.

With Browning's theorem for $d\ge9$ (Corollary 1.2) the $(d-2)$-free density holds for all $d\ge4$; Corollary 1.3 treats separable products. Not shown: a power-saving error term, uniformity in $f$, or squarefree values in degree five and above. Priority: Carella's preprint claims $n^4+1$ and $n^4+2$, and Zapata Ceballos-Jalalvand claim positive density for a class including $n^4+1$; the manuscript uses neither.

fields.name: The directional zero-one law for random walks in iid random environments in dimension at least three
fields.field: Random walks in random environment
fields.statement: Consider nearest-neighbour random walk on $\mathbb Z^d$ in an environment of iid transition rows, and for a direction $\ell\ne0$ let $A_\ell=\{X_n\cdot\ell\to+\infty\}$. Kalikow (1981) proved $P_0(A_\ell\cup A_{-\ell})\in\{0,1\}$ for the annealed law, and the question whether $P_0(A_\ell)$ itself must be 0 or 1 goes back to him. Zerner and Merkl (2001) proved it in dimension two for iid strictly elliptic environments; Bramson, Zeitouni and Zerner (2006) showed it fails for some stationary mixing environments in $d\ge3$ and posed the iid case as Open Problem 3. Is the annealed escape probability $P_0(A_\ell)$ always 0 or 1 for iid elliptic environments in every dimension $d\ge3$?
fields.posedBy: Steven A. Kalikow; the iid higher-dimensional case stated as Open Problem 3 by Maury Bramson, Ofer Zeitouni and Martin Zerner
fields.ageNote: Kalikow, Generalized random walk in a random environment, Ann. Probab. 9 (1981); Bramson-Zeitouni-Zerner (Ann. Probab. 34, 2006), Open Problem 3, for iid uniformly elliptic environments in d >= 3.

fields.name: The ballisticity conjecture: directional transience implies ballisticity for random walks in iid uniformly elliptic environments
fields.field: Random walks in random environment
fields.statement: For nearest-neighbour random walk on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge2$, in an iid uniformly elliptic environment, call the walk transient in direction $\ell$ if $P_0(X_n\cdot\ell\to\infty)=1$ and ballistic if $\liminf X_n\cdot\ell/n>0$ almost surely. In one dimension transient walks can have zero speed (Solomon). Sznitman's conditions $(T)$ and $(T')$ and his effective criterion give ballisticity from quantitative slab-exit bounds, and Guerra and Ramirez proved that the polynomial condition implies $(T')$, but all such results start from quantitative assumptions. Fribergh and Kious (2016, Conjecture 1.1) formulated the conjecture with the bare one-direction transience hypothesis. In dimension $d\ge2$, does almost-sure transience in a fixed direction $\ell$ imply a deterministic limiting velocity $v$ with $v\cdot\ell>0$?
fields.posedBy: Folklore of Sznitman's ballisticity programme; stated as Conjecture 1.1 by Alexander Fribergh and Daniel Kious
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Fribergh-Kious, Probab. Theory Related Fields 165 (2016), Conjecture 1.1, for the formulation. The question is older, implicit in Sznitman's work on conditions (T) and (T') around 2001-2002, but the manuscript gives no earlier statement.

fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for $d\ge2$, iid uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbour rows (no independence within a row needed) and a fixed unit $\ell$ with $P_0(A_\ell)=1$, there is a deterministic $v$ with $v\cdot\ell>0$ and $X_n/n\to v$ almost surely, so the walk is ballistic in direction $\ell$. For $d\ge3$ positive probability of $A_\ell$ suffices, the velocity is unique, and the directions with positive transience probability are exactly the open hemisphere $\{u:u\cdot v>0\}$, with probability one there and zero elsewhere. Not shown: the strictly (not uniformly) elliptic case, non-iid environments, or central limit theorems and slowdown estimates.

fields.name: A (1+epsilon)-approximation of edit distance in almost-linear time
fields.field: Fine-grained and string algorithms
fields.statement: Edit distance between strings of total length $N$ is computable in quadratic time, and Backurs and Indyk showed that a strongly subquadratic exact algorithm would refute SETH. Approximation algorithms reached polylogarithmic factors in time $N^{1+\delta}$ (Andoni-Krauthgamer-Onak), a constant factor in subquadratic time (Chakraborty-Das-Goldenberg-Koucky-Saks), and constant factors depending on $\delta$ in time $N^{1+\delta}$ (Andoni-Nosatzki 2020). For accuracy $1+\varepsilon$ the best known time saved only a quasi-polynomial factor, $N^2/2^{\log^{\Omega(1)}N}$ (Mao-Rubinstein 2026). For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, is there a randomized $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation of edit distance running in time $N^{1+o(1)}$?
fields.posedBy: Open question of the edit-distance approximation line (Andoni, Krauthgamer and Onak; Andoni and Nosatzki; Mao and Rubinstein); no single poser cited
fields.ageNote: The manuscript recounts the history of approximation algorithms but cites no paper that poses the question, and none was located here, so no year is set; it has been an open target at least since near-linear constant-factor algorithms appeared (2020).

This result is not among the README's exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region). The manuscripts are authored 'OpenAI' and name no human author. The single manuscript (September 24, 2026) is the whole family.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the abstract, introduction and main theorem were read against the question as framed. Its main theorem was read here: for every binary fraction $0<\varepsilon<1$, on integer lists of total length at most $N$ the output lies in $[\mathrm{ed},(1+\varepsilon)\mathrm{ed}]$ with probability at least 2/3, equal strings give 0, and for symbols bounded by $(N+2)^C$ the expected work is at most $(N+2)^{1+\eta}$ for every $\eta>0$ and large $N$, with polynomial space. The algorithm and its work and space accounting are defined inside the roughly 19,000-line challenge file itself; whether that accounting matches word-RAM time was not audited here. Not rebuilt here. Permitted axioms: propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice.
fields.resultNote: Main theorem: one randomized algorithm, uniform in a rational accuracy input $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, returns for explicitly stored strings with polynomially bounded integer symbols an estimate within factor $1+\varepsilon$ of unit-cost edit distance with probability at least 2/3, in worst-case expected time $N^{1+o(1)}$ on a logarithmic-word RAM; equal strings give 0 deterministically. The bound is pointwise in fixed $\varepsilon$: no polynomial dependence on $1/\varepsilon$ is claimed, and exact computation is used below very large accuracy-dependent thresholds, so it is an asymptotic scheme. Not shown: an alignment or edit script, weighted costs, a deterministic algorithm, or bounds when $\varepsilon$ shrinks with $N$.

fields.significanceNote: Whether edit distance can be approximated within 1+epsilon in near-linear time is a headline question of fine-grained algorithms; the best prior scheme, from March 2026, saved only a quasi-polynomial factor over quadratic time. Placed level with Randomized k-server polylogarithmic in k (45), just below Worst-case Subset Sum below meet-in-the-middle (46) and well below The APSP hypothesis (55).

fields.name: Smooth isometric immersion of every closed Riemannian surface into R^4
fields.field: Isometric immersions, geometric PDE
fields.statement: Nash's theorem places a compact Riemannian $n$-manifold smoothly and isometrically in Euclidean space of high dimension (17 for surfaces), and Gromov's methods give smooth isometric immersions of closed surfaces into $\mathbb R^5$. In $\mathbb R^3$ the topology and curvature obstruct global immersion and even local smooth immersion is delicate; $C^1$ immersions exist by Nash-Kuiper, and Poznyak treated compact planar domains in $\mathbb R^4$. Gromov recorded the question of smooth isometric immersion of arbitrary Riemannian surfaces into $\mathbb R^4$ (2000) and later attributed it to Chern around 1950. Does every closed smooth Riemannian surface, orientable or not and of any curvature, admit a $C^\infty$ isometric immersion into $\mathbb R^4$?
fields.posedBy: Mikhael Gromov (attributing the question to Shiing-Shen Chern)
fields.ageNote: Gromov, Spaces and questions, GAFA Special Volume (2000), Section I Remark (d). In a 2015 manuscript Gromov attributed the four-space surface question to Chern around 1950, while expressing uncertainty about the compactness qualification.

fields.name: Naor's sublinear-dimension question for finite subsets of Lp, 1 < p < infinity, p not 2
fields.field: Metric embeddings, Banach space geometry
fields.statement: The Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma embeds every $n$-point subset of Hilbert space into $O(\log n)$ dimensions with distortion $1+\varepsilon$, and Johnson and Lindenstrauss (1984, Problem 3) asked what analogues hold in other Banach spaces. In $L_1$ polynomial dimension is necessary (Brinkman-Charikar), and Ball's exact bound for $L_p$ is $\binom n2$ coordinates. Naor (ICM 2018) remarked that for no fixed $p\in[1,\infty)\setminus\{2\}$ was it even known whether every $n$-point subset of $\ell_p$ embeds with bounded distortion into a normed space of dimension $o(n)$. For fixed $p\ne2$ and distortion $D$, can every $n$-point subset of $L_p$ be embedded with distortion $D$ in dimension $o(n)$?
fields.posedBy: Assaf Naor (after William B. Johnson and Joram Lindenstrauss)
fields.ageNote: Naor, Metric dimension reduction: a snapshot of the Ribe program, Proc. ICM 2018, remark after Question 13; the underlying question is Johnson-Lindenstrauss (1984), Problem 3.

fields.name: The ordinary-double-point gap conjecture for normalized volumes of klt singularities
fields.field: Birational geometry, K-stability
fields.statement: For a klt germ $x\in X$ of dimension $n$ with zero boundary, the normalized volume $\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(x,X)=\inf_vA_X(v)^n\mathrm{vol}(v)$ over valuations centred at $x$ is at most $n^n$, with equality exactly at smooth points (Liu-Xu). Spotti and Sun, motivated by volume densities of tangent cones of Kahler-Einstein limits, conjectured that the ordinary double point comes next. It was known for surfaces (Li-Liu), threefolds (Liu-Xu) and local complete intersections (Liu), with a different sharp bound for toric germs (Moraga-Suss). Does every singular $n$-dimensional klt germ satisfy $\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(x,X)\le2(n-1)^n$, with equality exactly for an ordinary double point?

fields.name: The Friedgut-Kalai sharp-threshold conjecture: threshold width O(1/log^2 n) for monotone graph properties
fields.field: Random graphs, analysis of Boolean functions
fields.statement: For a nontrivial increasing graph property $P$ on $n$ vertices and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, let $p_a$ be the edge probability at which $G(n,p)$ has $P$ with probability $a$. Friedgut and Kalai (1996), combining the KKL and BKKKL influence theorems with Russo's formula, proved $p_{1-\varepsilon}-p_\varepsilon\le C\log(1/2\varepsilon)/\log n$, observed that containing a clique of size about $\log n$ has width of order $(\log n)^{-2}$, and conjectured that this is the truth (Conjecture 1.2). fields.name: The Friedgut-Kalai threshold-width conjecture for r-uniform hypergraph properties
fields.field: Random hypergraphs, analysis of Boolean functions
fields.statement: For a nontrivial increasing property of $r$-uniform hypergraphs on $n$ vertices invariant under relabelling, the transitive symmetry of the $\binom nr$ edge coordinates gives threshold width $O(1/\log n)$ by the Friedgut-Kalai method. fields.name: Randomized versus quantum query complexity of total Boolean functions: is R(f) = O(Q(f)^3)?
fields.field: Query complexity
fields.statement: For total Boolean functions the bounded-error randomized query complexity $R$ and quantum query complexity $Q$ are polynomially related: Beals et al. proved $D=O(Q^6)$, and after Huang's sensitivity theorem Aaronson, Ben-David, Kothari, Rao and Tal proved $D(f)=O(Q(f)^4)$, hence $R=O(Q^4)$. The best separations were power $5/2$ (cheat sheets), then $8/3-o(1)$ (Tal) and $3-o(1)$ (Bansal-Sinha; Sherstov-Storozhenko-Wu). Aaronson, Ben-David, Kothari, Rao and Tal conjectured that the cubic relation holds. Is $R(f)=O(Q(f)^3)$ for every total Boolean function, or is the quartic exponent optimal?
fields.posedBy: Scott Aaronson, Shalev Ben-David, Robin Kothari, Shravas Rao and Avishay Tal
fields.ageNote: Conjecture 2 of their STOC 2021 paper, as cited by the manuscript; the preprint appeared on arXiv in October 2020 (2010.12629).
fields.aiRole: The release README says the results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model with a fixed procedure, on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result, and that some outputs build on earlier model results. fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the abstract, introduction, Theorem 1.1 and the quantum upper-bound proposition were read against Conjecture 2 as the manuscript states it. The construction and its analyses (a quantum tournament lemma for candidate comparisons, an adaptive direct-product lower bound) were not refereed. No Lean formalization accompanies this manuscript. Both measures are worst-case bit-query counts with error at most 1/3 and unrestricted computation between queries, as the paper states.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for each fixed $k\ge2$ there are total Boolean functions $F_{k,m}$ with $Q(F_{k,m})\le C_k\sqrt m(\log m)^{b_k}$ and $R(F_{k,m})\ge c_km^{2-1/k}/(\log m)^2$, a power $4-2/k$ separation up to logarithms, so no bound $R=O((1+Q)^\alpha)$ holds with $\alpha<4$. With the known $R=O(Q^4)$ the optimal exponent is exactly 4, and the cubic conjecture is false. The functions are cheat-sheet-style columns whose certificate cells are addressed by answers to partial-function instances. Not shown: a separation with exponent exactly 4 for a single family, or new results for partial functions.

fields.name: Petty's projection conjecture in dimensions at least four
fields.field: Convex geometry; affine isoperimetric inequalities, projection bodies
fields.statement: For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ the projection body $\Pi K$ has support function $h_{\Pi K}(u)=\mathrm{vol}_{n-1}(\mathrm{proj}_{u^\perp}K)$. The ratio $|\Pi K|/|K|^{n-1}$ is affine invariant. Petty (1971) conjectured that for $n\ge3$ it is minimized exactly by ellipsoids, i.e. $|\Pi K|/|K|^{n-1}\ge\kappa_{n-1}^n\kappa_n^{2-n}$ with equality only for ellipsoids. Local versions were proved by Saroglou-Zvavitch and Ivaki, and in August 2026 Chen, Feng, Li, Xi and Xu proved the case $n=3$. Does Petty's inequality, with its ellipsoid equality case, hold for every convex body in every dimension $n\ge4$?
fields.posedBy: C. M. Petty, Isoperimetric problems, Proc. Conf. Convexity and Combinatorial Geometry, Univ. of Oklahoma (1971)
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1 of the manuscript was read against Petty's conjecture as the paper states it with the 1971 reference; it claims the inequality and the ellipsoid-only equality case for every convex body in every dimension $n\ge4$. The proof was not refereed. The Lean challenge ComparatorChallenges/PettyProjectionVolume.lean (listed in lean/formalization.yaml, declaration OAI.PettyProjection.petty_projection_volume) was read here: for $n\ge4$ and every compact convex $K$ with nonempty interior it asserts pettyConstant $n\le|\Pi K|/|K|^{n-1}$ and equality iff $K$ is an affine image of the unit ball, with $\Pi K$ defined through orthogonal shadow volumes. This states the headline claim. Not rebuilt here. The three-dimensional case is not part of this work and rests on the human preprint of Chen et al.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1: for every $n\ge4$ and every convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $|\Pi K|/|K|^{n-1}\ge\kappa_{n-1}^n\kappa_n^{2-n}$, with equality iff $K$ is an ellipsoid; no symmetry or regularity is assumed. The proof bounds a bilinear pairing $\iint|x\cdot y|\,d\eta\,d\zeta$ via a strict spherical-harmonic estimate for norms and a fixed-point choice of affine position. It does not treat $n=3$, which Chen, Feng, Li, Xi and Xu proved in August 2026; the paper notes that the two together give the full conjecture for $n\ge3$. As corollaries (via Lutwak's known implication) it states the Lutwak-Petty lower-degree inequalities for $2\le i\le n-2$, without equality cases, and a sharp Holmes-Thompson isoperimetric inequality.

fields.name: Brannen's simplex conjecture for projection-body volume
fields.field: Convex geometry; projection bodies, reverse affine isoperimetric inequalities
fields.statement: For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ with projection body $\Pi K$ (support function $h_{\Pi K}(u)=\mathrm{vol}_{d-1}(\mathrm{proj}_{u^\perp}K)$), the ratio $R_d(K)=|\Pi K|/|K|^{d-1}$ is affine invariant. The simplex has $R_d=c_d=(d+1)d^d/d!$. Brannen (1996) conjectured that simplices maximize $R_d$ among all convex bodies, i.e. $|\Pi K|\le c_d|K|^{d-1}$. Is the simplex the maximizer of normalized projection-body volume in every dimension?
fields.posedBy: N. S. Brannen, Volumes of projection bodies, Mathematika 43 (1996)
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. fields.name: Marrakchi's relative bicentralizer conjecture
fields.field: Operator algebras; type III von Neumann algebras, bicentralizers
fields.statement: Connes asked whether the bicentralizer of a faithful normal state on a type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor with separable predual is always trivial; Haagerup settled the amenable case. Ando, Haagerup, Houdayer and Marrakchi built a relative bicentralizer and its flow for expected inclusions. Marrakchi formulated the relative bicentralizer conjecture and proved that, for separable preduals, it is equivalent to: for every inclusion $N\subset M$ of von Neumann algebras with separable preduals and a faithful normal conditional expectation, there is an expected amenable subalgebra $P\subset N$ with $P'\cap c(M)=N'\cap c(M)$, where $c(M)$ is the continuous core. Is the relative bicentralizer conjecture true?
fields.posedBy: A. Marrakchi, Kadison's problem for type III subfactors and the bicentralizer conjecture, Invent. Math. 239 (2025), Conjecture C (arXiv 2308.15163)
fields.ageNote: Posed in the arXiv preprint 2308.15163 (2023), published in Invent. Math. in 2025. The absolute problem it generalizes goes back to Connes (1980s).
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against Marrakchi's Conjecture C via his Theorem D equivalence, as the paper states it. The argument uses as inputs Marrakchi's Theorem D equivalence and his 2026 binormal-state lemmas.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every unital inclusion $N\subset M$ with separable preduals and a faithful normal conditional expectation there are an amenable $P\subset N$ and an expectation $N\to P$ with $P'\cap c(M)=N'\cap c(M)$; with Marrakchi's Theorem D this is the relative bicentralizer conjecture, including arbitrary centers and types, and gives an expected MASA corollary relevant to Kadison's problem for subfactors. Along the way it reproves Connes' bicentralizer conjecture for separable type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factors; priority for that absolute case belongs to Houdayer and Marrakchi (arXiv 2609.11462, 10 Sep 2026), whose statement has no separability assumption. The companion gives a second absolute proof via bounded recovery. Non-separable preduals are not treated.

fields.name: Is the worst-case translative covering density of convex bodies linear in the dimension?
fields.field: Discrete and convex geometry; translative and lattice coverings
fields.statement: For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ let $\theta_T(K)$ be the least density of a covering of $\mathbb R^n$ by translates of $K$. Rogers (1957) proved $\theta_T(K)\le n\log n+n\log\log n+5n$ for every convex body, and lower bounds of order $n$ are known for balls. Naszodi recorded the question whether a universal linear bound holds: is there an absolute constant $C$ with $\theta_T(K)\le Cn$ for every convex body in every dimension? Equivalently, what is the order of the worst-case covering density in dimension $n$?
fields.posedBy: M. Naszodi, Flavors of Translative Coverings, New Trends in Intuitive Geometry, Bolyai Soc. Math. Stud. 27 (2018), Section 3 (arXiv 1603.04481)
fields.ageNote: Recorded in Naszodi's survey, arXiv 1603.04481 (2016), published 2018; the manuscript does not say who first asked it. Rogers' n log n upper bound dates from 1957.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. The challenge ComparatorChallenges/CoveringDensity.lean is not in lean/formalization.yaml; it is found through lean/docs/092.md and its solution module OAI.Geometry.CoveringDensity.Main exists at the pinned commit. Its statement was read here: absolute $0<c<C$ and $n_0$ such that for $n\ge n_0$ the suprema of translative and of lattice covering density, over all convex bodies and over centrally symmetric ones, lie between $cn\log n$ and $Cn\log n$, with coverings defined from scratch. This states the headline. Not rebuilt here. SingleLatticeCovering.lean (in the catalogue) states the companion's lattice upper bound.
fields.resultNote: Translative paper, Theorem 1.1: for absolute $c>0$ and all large $n$ there is a centrally symmetric convex body (even a rational polytope) with $\theta_T(K_n)>cn\log n$, so no universal linear bound exists; with Rogers' bound the worst-case order is $n\log n$. It extends the lattice lower bound of Li and Liu (2026) to arbitrary translative coverings. The companion proves every convex body has a single-lattice covering of density at most $Cn\log n$, removing the $(\log\log n)^{O(1)}$ loss of Li-Liu, so the lattice supremum also has order $n\log n$. Constants are not optimized; Euclidean balls are not treated.

fields.name: The degenerate Arnold conjecture: critical-number and rational cup-length lower bounds for Hamiltonian fixed points
fields.field: Symplectic topology; Hamiltonian fixed points, Arnold conjecture
fields.statement: Arnold asked whether a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism $\phi$ of a closed symplectic manifold $M$ must have at least as many geometrically distinct fixed points as a smooth function on $M$ has critical points. Without nondegeneracy assumptions this is the critical-number bound $\#\mathrm{Fix}(\phi)\ge\mathrm{Crit}(M)$, with the weaker rational cup-length form $\#\mathrm{Fix}(\phi)\ge\mathrm{cuplength}(M;\mathbb Q)$ (unit included). These are known on tori and $\mathbb{CP}^n$, and when $[\omega]$ and $c_1$ vanish on $\pi_2(M)$ (Rudyak-Oprea). Do the critical-number and cup-length bounds hold for every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of every closed symplectic manifold?
fields.posedBy: V. I. Arnold, First steps in symplectic topology, Russian Math. Surveys 41 (1986); recorded as Conjectures 1.4 and 1.6 in R. Golovko, On variants of Arnold conjecture, Arch. Math. (Brno) 56 (2020)
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the conjectures as the paper states them (Arnold 1986, Golovko 2020). It claims a smooth Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of the quadric $Q^3$ with exactly 3 fixed points while $\mathrm{Crit}(Q^3)=\mathrm{cuplength}(Q^3;\mathbb Q)=4$. The proof was not refereed. Lean: ComparatorChallenges/ArnoldCounterexample.lean (OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.main, in lean/formalization.yaml) was read here; it states a Hamiltonian $\phi$ of the literal quadric with fixed set of size 3, $4\le$ the minimum critical number over all smooth functions, and a degenerate fixed point. It covers the critical-number form; the cup-length value is not formalized. Not rebuilt here. Graded contested because an earlier preprint (Ma) claims the opposite; see the claim note.
fields.claimIssueNote: The release says: 'Ma [Theorem 1.5] asserted that the minimum number of fixed points over all Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms always equals Crit(M). Theorem 1.1 contradicts that assertion' (degenerate paper) and 'Ma's preprint asserts that the minimum number of fixed points of a nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism always equals the ordinary Morse number ... Theorem 1.1 contradicts that unrestricted assertion' (Morse-number paper). The other side: R. Ma, Proofs on Arnold conjectures, arXiv 0808.0613v7 (2013), Theorem 1.5, claims these lower bounds hold in general. Ma's preprint is unpublished; no referee has ruled between them.

fields.name: The Morse-number Arnold conjecture for nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms
fields.field: Symplectic topology; Hamiltonian fixed points, Morse theory
fields.statement: For a closed connected symplectic manifold $(M,\omega)$ let $\mathrm{Morse}(M)$ be the least number of critical points of a Morse function on $M$. Floer theory and its virtual extensions show that a nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism has at least the sum of the Betti numbers many fixed points, but the Morse number can be larger. The Morse-number form of the Arnold conjecture asks: if $H$ is a one-periodic Hamiltonian whose time-one map is nondegenerate, is the number of fixed points with contractible orbits at least $\mathrm{Morse}(M)$?
fields.posedBy: V. I. Arnold, First steps in symplectic topology (1986); recorded as Conjecture 1.1 in R. Golovko, On variants of Arnold conjecture, Arch. Math. (Brno) 56 (2020)
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 were read against Golovko's Conjecture 1.1 as the paper states it. The proof was not refereed and is not formalized. Graded contested because Ma's 2013 preprint claims the opposite; see the claim note.
fields.claimIssueNote: The release says: 'Ma [Theorem 1.5] asserted that the minimum number of fixed points over all Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms always equals Crit(M). Theorem 1.1 contradicts that assertion' (degenerate paper) and 'Ma's preprint asserts that the minimum number of fixed points of a nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism always equals the ordinary Morse number ... Theorem 1.1 contradicts that unrestricted assertion' (Morse-number paper). The other side: R. Ma, Proofs on Arnold conjectures, arXiv 0808.0613v7 (2013), Theorem 1.5, claims these lower bounds hold in general. Ma's preprint is unpublished; no referee has ruled between them.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are a closed symplectic 12-manifold and a one-periodic Hamiltonian with all fixed points nondegenerate and contractible and $\#\mathrm{Fix}=\chi(M)+128<\mathrm{Morse}(M)$; Corollary 1.2 makes $\mathrm{Morse}(M)-\#\mathrm{Fix}$ arbitrarily large (the manifold depends on the deficit). The mechanism: the augmentation ideal of $A_5^k$ needs two generators while $d(A_5^k)$ is unbounded, realized by relative handle cancellation on $X\times\mathbb R^8$. The fixed-point count still exceeds the homological (Floer) bounds. The examples are not simply connected; the October 5 companions give simply connected Kahler examples below the stable Morse number.

fields.name: The stable Morse number as a lower bound for nondegenerate Hamiltonian fixed points
fields.field: Symplectic topology; Hamiltonian fixed points, stable Morse theory
fields.statement: The stable Morse number $\mathrm{SM}(W)$ of a closed manifold is the least number of critical points of a Morse function $F:W\times\mathbb R^k\to\mathbb R$ equal to a nondegenerate quadratic form outside a compact set ($k\ge0$ varying); $\mathrm{SM}(W)\le\mathrm{Morse}(W)$. Dimitroglou Rizell and Golovko proved $\#\mathrm{Fix}_0\ge\mathrm{SM}(M)$ for nondegenerate Hamiltonians when $[\omega]$ and $c_1$ vanish on $\pi_2(M)$. Does the stable Morse bound $\#\mathrm{Fix}_0(\phi_H^1;H)\ge\mathrm{SM}(M)$ hold for every nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of every closed symplectic manifold?
fields.posedBy: Recorded as Conjecture 1.2 in R. Golovko, On variants of Arnold conjecture, Arch. Math. (Brno) 56 (2020); background in Arnold (1986)
fields.ageNote: The stable formulation is cited from Golovko's 2020 survey of variants; Arnold (1986, Section 5) already compared stable and unstable critical-point minima.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 of the principal paper was read against Golovko's Conjecture 1.2; it claims a simply connected closed Kahler manifold of real dimension 1412 with a nondegenerate Hamiltonian having $\mathrm{SM}(M)-16$ fixed points. The companions claim a dimension-22 family with $\#\mathrm{Fix}\le(1-1/128)\mathrm{SM}$ and a dimension-3332 example attaining the cyclic integral Floer bound. Proofs not refereed; not formalized. Graded contested because Ma's 2013 preprint claims nondegenerate fixed points are always at least the ordinary Morse number, which is at least the stable Morse number; the stable-Morse papers themselves do not cite Ma.
fields.claimIssueNote: The release says: 'Ma [Theorem 1.5] asserted that the minimum number of fixed points over all Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms always equals Crit(M). fields.resultNote: Principal Theorem 1.1: a simply connected closed Kahler $M$ ($\dim_{\mathbb R}=1412$, $\mathrm{SM}=318968$) and a Hamiltonian with all 318952 fixed points nondegenerate and contractible. fields.name: Does the perfect matching polytope have a polynomial-size semidefinite lift?
fields.shortName: SDP lifts of the matching polytope
fields.field: Extended formulations; positive semidefinite rank, lower bounds
fields.statement: A semidefinite lift of size $r$ writes a polytope as an affine image of $L\cap\mathbb S^r_+$ for an affine subspace $L$; by Gouveia-Parrilo-Thomas the least such $r$ equals the PSD rank of a slack matrix. Yannakakis ruled out small symmetric linear programs for the perfect matching polytope, Rothvoss (2014) proved its linear extension complexity is $2^{\Omega(n)}$, and Braun et al. ruled out small symmetric SDPs, noting that it is natural to ask whether matching can be expressed compactly by semidefinite programming. Does the perfect matching polytope of $K_n$ admit an exact semidefinite lift of size polynomial in $n$?
fields.posedBy: G. Braun, J. Brown-Cohen, A. Huq, S. Pokutta, P. Raghavendra, A. Roy, B. Weitz, D. Zink, The matching problem has no small symmetric SDP, SODA 2016 / Math. Program. 165 (2017)
fields.ageNote: Posed in the abstract of arXiv 1504.00703 (April 2015) after Rothvoss's 2014 theorem; the manuscript itself states no posing source and cites this paper for the symmetric case.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 were read against the question. The paper claims $\mathrm{rank}_{psd}A_n(\rho)\ge2^{cn}$ for every fixed $0<\rho<1$ and hence that every exact semidefinite lift of the perfect matching polytope has size $2^{\Omega(n)}$. Proof not refereed. The challenges ComparatorChallenges/MatchingAffineLift.lean and MatchingPSD.lean are not in lean/formalization.yaml; they are found through lean/docs/126.md and their solution modules (OAI.Combinatorics.MatchingPSD.AffineLift and .Main) exist at the pinned commit. Statements read here: for every $C>0$ and large even $n$, every affine section of a PSD cone projecting onto the matching polytope has size $>n^C$, and the PSD rank of the unshifted slack matrix exceeds $n^C$. This states the headline (no polynomial-size lift); the exponential bound and the shifted matrices are not formalized. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is $c>0$ such that for every fixed $0<\rho<1$ the odd-cut matrix with entries $|M\cap\delta(U)|-1+\rho$ has real PSD rank at least $2^{cn}$ for large even $n$, with no symmetry or precision restriction on the factors. Corollary 1.2: every exact semidefinite lift of the perfect matching polytope has size $2^{\Omega(n)}$. The method follows Lee-Raghavendra-Steurer with a Grigoriev-type parity functional and new averaging lemmas. The endpoint $\rho=1$ has a polynomial factorization, and approximate lifts are not excluded (Kaniewski-Lee-de Wolf give subexponential approximations).
fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: Exponential PSD rank of positively shifted matching matrices
fields.significanceNote: The natural sequel to Rothvoss's celebrated matching-polytope theorem and a well-known open question in extended formulations since 2015, though narrower than the linear question. Placed level with Optimality of Greedy for Single-Pass Semi-Streaming Matching (35), above the Goemans-Linial sparsest-cut integrality gap (28), and below Khot's 2-to-1 Games Conjecture with perfect completeness (45).

fields.name: The scalar-curvature extension conjecture for Ricci flow in all dimensions
fields.field: Geometric analysis; Ricci flow singularities
fields.statement: A smooth Ricci flow $\partial_tg=-2\mathrm{Ric}$ on a closed manifold extends past a finite time unless the full curvature becomes unbounded (Hamilton), and a Ricci bound suffices (Sesum). The scalar-curvature extension conjecture asks whether scalar curvature alone detects singularities: is it true that every finite-time singularity of a Ricci flow on a closed manifold of dimension at least four has unbounded scalar curvature, i.e. does $\sup_{M\times[0,T)}|R|<\infty$ always allow the flow to be extended past $T$?
fields.posedBy: Stated as open in R. H. Bamler, Convergence of Ricci flows with bounded scalar curvature, Ann. of Math. 188 (2018), p. 756; known cases surveyed by C. Li and Y. Li (2026)
fields.ageNote: The manuscripts cite the conjecture from Bamler (2018) and a 2026 survey without naming who first posed it or when; it was known for Type I flows (Enders-Muller-Topping 2011) and Kahler-Ricci flow (Zhang 2010).
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the conjecture as the paper states it; it claims a Ricci flow on $S^2\times S^{q+1}$, $q\ge10$, with bounded scalar curvature and $\max|\mathrm{Rm}|\to\infty$ at a finite maximal time. Proof not refereed; no Lean formalization. The construction imports Stolarski's (2019) doubly warped conical-singularity flows and their quantitative profile estimates as stated inputs; the new work is the scalar bound. The paper says no dimension-four conclusion is asserted.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for some $q\ge10$ there is a smooth Ricci flow on the closed manifold $S^2\times S^{q+1}$ with $\sup|R|<\infty$ and $\max_M|\mathrm{Rm}|\to\infty$ at the finite maximal time; a corollary gives two-sided power-law curvature blowup with arbitrarily large exponents in one fixed dimension. This refutes the unrestricted all-dimensions conjecture. It relies on Stolarski's construction and gives no explicit dimension; it does not touch dimension four, which the companion proves true.

fields.name: The scalar-curvature extension conjecture for Ricci flow in dimension four
fields.field: Geometric analysis; four-dimensional Ricci flow
fields.statement: A smooth Ricci flow on a closed manifold can stop only if the full curvature blows up. Bamler and Zhang developed heat-kernel and compactness theory for flows with bounded scalar curvature and proved smooth extension in dimension four when $H_2(M;\mathbb F)=0$ for all fields; Simon continued such flows through orbifold limits. In dimension four: if a smooth Ricci flow on a closed four-manifold has uniformly bounded scalar curvature on $[0,T)$ with $T<\infty$, does it extend smoothly on the same manifold past $T$?
fields.posedBy: Stated as open in R. H. Bamler, Ann. of Math. 188 (2018), p. 756, with the four-dimensional theory of Bamler-Zhang (2017, 2019) and M. Simon (2020)
fields.ageNote: The manuscripts do not say when or by whom the dimension-four case was first posed; Bamler-Zhang's partial result (Adv. Math. 2017) shows it was open by then.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the problem as the paper states it; it claims smooth extension on the same closed four-manifold whenever $|R|$ is bounded up to a finite $T$. The long proof (blowup trees of Ricci-flat pieces, a renormalized Einstein-Hilbert functional) was not refereed and is not formalized. It depends on the companion's elliptic inequality on degenerating Ricci-flat trees as a stated input, and on Bamler-Zhang's estimates.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: a smooth Ricci flow on a closed four-manifold with $\sup_{M\times[0,T)}|R|<\infty$, $T<\infty$, extends smoothly past $T$; Corollary: at a finite maximal time $\limsup\max R=+\infty$. This removes the $H_2$ hypothesis of Bamler-Zhang and gives smooth continuation rather than an orbifold flow. The companion proves $E=o(M)$ for the renormalized Einstein-Hilbert functional on degenerating trees of Ricci-flat spaces. It is specific to dimension four; in high dimension the family's other paper shows the statement is false.

fields.name: The Gaussian propeller conjecture
fields.field: Gaussian geometry; partitions, kernel clustering
fields.statement: For a measurable partition $A_1,\dots,A_k$ of $\mathbb R^d$ and the standard Gaussian measure $\gamma_d$, let $z(A_i)=\int_{A_i}x\,d\gamma_d$ and $F=\sum_i\|z(A_i)\|^2$. Khot and Naor, studying approximate kernel clustering and its Unique Games hardness, conjectured that for $k\ge3$ the maximum of $F$ is attained by the propeller: three planar sectors of angle $2\pi/3$ times an orthogonal factor, giving $9/(8\pi)$. Heilman, Jagannath and Naor proved it in $\mathbb R^3$. Is $\sum_i\|\int_{A_i}x\,d\gamma_d\|^2\le 9/(8\pi)$ for every finite partition in every dimension?
fields.posedBy: S. Khot and A. Naor, Approximate kernel clustering, Mathematika 55 (2009)
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the conjecture as the paper states it with the Khot-Naor reference. The proof uses the Heilman-Jagannath-Naor $\mathbb R^3$ theorem (computer-assisted) as an established input and was not refereed. The challenge ComparatorChallenges/GaussianPropeller.lean (OAI.GaussianPropeller.all_partitions, in lean/formalization.yaml) was read here: for all $d,k>0$ and every measurable a.e.-partition, $\sum_i\|\int_{A_i}x\,d\gamma\|^2\le9/(8\pi)$, and for $d\ge2$, $k\ge3$ the explicit propeller attains it. This states the headline. Not rebuilt here. The kernel-clustering hardness consequence is not formalized and depends on the release's separate Unique Games theorem.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for all $d,k$, every measurable partition of $\mathbb R^d$ satisfies $\sum_i\|\int_{A_i}x\,d\gamma_d\|^2\le9/(8\pi)$, with equality for the propeller when $d\ge2$, $k\ge3$. The new step shows extremizers with five or more active cells cannot beat $9/(8\pi)$, using Ehrhard's inequality and residual-score estimates; four-cell configurations come from Heilman-Jagannath-Naor. Consequence stated: combined with the release's Unique Games theorem, NP-hardness of beating the factor $(8\pi/9)(1-1/k)$ for identity-target kernel clustering, $k\ge3$. Uniqueness of extremizers is not claimed.

fields.name: The P = W conjecture for fixed-determinant (SL_n) Higgs moduli in composite rank
fields.shortName: P = W for SL_n, composite rank
fields.field: Algebraic geometry; nonabelian Hodge theory, Higgs bundles
fields.statement: For a smooth projective curve $C$ of genus $g\ge2$ and $\gcd(n,d)=1$, nonabelian Hodge theory identifies the cohomology of the moduli space $M^L_{\mathrm{Dol}}(\mathrm{SL}_n)$ of stable trace-free Higgs bundles with fixed determinant and that of the twisted $\mathrm{SL}_n$ character variety. De Cataldo, Hausel and Migliorini conjectured that the perverse filtration $P$ of the Hitchin map matches the weight filtration $W$: $P_k=W_{2k}=W_{2k+1}$. Maulik-Shen and others proved it for $\mathrm{GL}_n$; for fixed determinant it was known in prime rank, where the variant cohomology was controlled. Does $P=W$ hold on the full cohomology, variant part included, for every composite rank $n$?
fields.posedBy: M. A. de Cataldo, T. Hausel and L. Migliorini, Topology of Hitchin systems and Hodge theory of character varieties: the case A_1, Ann. of Math. 175 (2012)
fields.ageNote: Year of the Annals paper the manuscript cites; it gives no earlier preprint date.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the conjecture as the paper states it; it claims $P_kH^m=W_{2k}H^m=W_{2k+1}H^m$ on the full rational cohomology for every composite $n\ge4$, coprime $d$, every $L$ and every genus $g\ge2$ curve. The proof (an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ operator built from logarithmic moving-pole moduli, following Hausel-Mellit-Minets-Schiffmann) was not refereed and is not formalized. It uses Mellit's toric stratifications and published logarithmic Hodge moduli constructions as inputs.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: $P_k=W_{2k}=W_{2k+1}$ on all of $H^*(X^B,\mathbb Q)$ for the smooth coprime fixed-determinant, trace-free moduli in every composite rank $n\ge4$, genus $g\ge2$, including the variant (non-$\Gamma$-invariant) cohomology; with the earlier prime-rank theorems this gives the fixed-determinant conjecture in every coprime rank. A corollary answers Maulik-Shen's Question 5.5 on Betti weights of endoscopic images. Non-coprime (singular) cases and other groups are not treated.

fields.significanceNote: P = W is a central conjecture of nonabelian Hodge theory, but its GL_n case was proved in 2022 and the SL_n prime-rank case earlier; the composite-rank fixed-determinant remainder is a significant but secondary step. fields.name: The Benson-Etingof-Ostrik conjecture for finite symmetric tensor categories
fields.field: Tensor categories; positive characteristic, Verlinde categories
fields.statement: In characteristic zero, Deligne's theorem gives every symmetric tensor category of moderate growth a fiber functor to supervector spaces. In characteristic $p>0$, Benson, Etingof and Ostrik constructed the tower of higher Verlinde categories $\mathrm{Ver}_p\subset\mathrm{Ver}_{p^2}\subset\cdots$ and conjectured that every symmetric tensor category of moderate growth over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$ admits a fiber functor to the union of this tower. Ostrik proved it for fusion categories (to $\mathrm{Ver}_p$). Does every finite symmetric tensor category in characteristic $p$, including $p=2$, admit a fiber functor to some $\mathrm{Ver}_{p^n}(k)$?
fields.posedBy: D. Benson, P. Etingof and V. Ostrik, New incompressible symmetric tensor categories in positive characteristic, Duke Math. J. 172 (2023), Conjecture 1.4
fields.ageNote: Year of the Duke publication cited by the manuscript; the preprint circulated earlier, which the manuscript does not date.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. The proof was not refereed and is not formalized. The paper itself limits the claim to finite categories and makes no assertion for general moderate-growth categories.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every finite symmetric tensor category over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ has a fiber functor to a single finite level $\mathrm{Ver}_{p^n}(k)$, including $p=2$. Consequences stated: classification of finite incompressible categories (the finite case of Coulembier-Etingof-Ostrik's Conjecture B), uniqueness of the functor in characteristic two via their subterminality theorem, and a generalized Tannakian realization. fields.name: The strong Kadison-Kastler conjecture
fields.field: Operator algebras; perturbation theory of von Neumann algebras
fields.statement: For von Neumann algebras $M,N\subseteq B(H)$ the Kadison-Kastler distance $d(M,N)$ is the Hausdorff distance between their unit balls in operator norm. Kadison and Kastler (1972) proposed that sufficiently close von Neumann algebras should be spatially isomorphic via a unitary close to the identity. This was proved for injective algebras (Christensen, Johnson, Raeburn-Taylor) and for certain crossed-product $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors (Cameron et al.). Is there, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a $\delta>0$ such that any two von Neumann algebras on the same Hilbert space with $d(M,N)<\delta$ satisfy $uMu^*=N$ for a unitary $u$ with $\|u-1\|<\varepsilon$?
fields.posedBy: R. V. Kadison and D. Kastler, Perturbations of von Neumann algebras. I. Stability of type, Amer. J. Math. 94 (1972)
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the conjecture as the paper states it with the 1972 reference; it claims a tolerance $\delta(\varepsilon)$ uniform over all unital von Neumann algebras, representations and Hilbert spaces. The proof was not refereed. The challenge ComparatorChallenges/StrongKadisonKastler.lean is not in lean/formalization.yaml; it is found through lean/docs/289.md and its solution module OAI.Analysis.KadisonKastler.StrongStability exists at the pinned commit. fields.name: Small spatial embeddings for one-sided near inclusions of von Neumann algebras
fields.field: Operator algebras; near inclusions, perturbation theory
fields.statement: For von Neumann algebras $M,N\subseteq B(H)$ with common identity let $\gamma(M,N)=\sup_{x\in M,\|x\|\le1}\inf_{y\in N}\|x-y\|$. Christensen showed that an injective $M$ with small $\gamma(M,N)$ embeds into $N$ by a unitary close to the identity. Cameron, Christensen, Sinclair, Smith, White and Wiggins asked the unrestricted one-sided question: for every $\varepsilon>0$ is there a $\delta>0$ such that $\gamma(M,N)<\delta$ always implies $uMu^*\subseteq N$ for some unitary $u$ with $\|u-1\|<\varepsilon$?

fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the question as the paper quotes it (paragraph before Theorem 2 of Cameron et al. 2012); it claims algebras $M_n,N_n$ on separable spaces with $\gamma(M_n,N_n)\to0$ such that every unitary with $uM_nu^*\subseteq N_n$ stays at distance at least $\varepsilon_0$ from the identity. Proof not refereed; not formalized.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there are $\varepsilon_0>0$ and pairs of von Neumann algebras on separable Hilbert spaces with common identity and $\gamma(M_n,N_n)\to0$ for which spatial embeddings exist but every implementing unitary satisfies $\|u-1\|\ge\varepsilon_0$. So the unrestricted one-sided question has a negative answer, in contrast with Christensen's injective case and with the two-sided strong Kadison-Kastler theorem in the same family. The obstruction is to small unitaries, not to the existence of embeddings.

fields.name: The spatial Kadison-Kastler problem for close separable C*-algebras
fields.field: Operator algebras; perturbations of C*-algebras
fields.statement: Kadison and Kastler (1972) initiated the study of close operator algebras. For C*-algebras, Johnson showed implementing unitaries need not be close to the identity and Choi-Christensen gave close non-isomorphic algebras, but only non-separable ones. Christensen, Sinclair, Smith, White and Winter proved that sufficiently close separable nuclear C*-algebras on a separable Hilbert space are spatially isomorphic, and discussed the separable spatial formulation: is there a $\delta>0$ such that any two norm-separable C*-algebras $A,B$ on a separable Hilbert space with Kadison-Kastler distance below $\delta$ satisfy $uAu^*=B$ for some unitary $u$?

fields.ageNote: The perturbation program is from Kadison-Kastler (1972); the manuscript cites the 2010 paper as discussing this separable spatial formulation.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 was read against the separable spatial question as the paper states it. It claims, for every $\varepsilon>0$, unital norm-separable C*-algebras on a separable Hilbert space with common identity, Kadison-Kastler distance below $\varepsilon$ and equal bicommutants, that are not unitarily conjugate. Proof not refereed; not formalized. The paper says it gives no abstract non-isomorphism and no von Neumann counterexample.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are unital norm-separable C*-algebras $A,B$ on a separable Hilbert space with $\mathrm{KK}(A,B)<\varepsilon$ and $A''=B''$ but no unitary with $uAu^*=B$. The construction uses sequence algebras over a deformation of the free-group regular representation (Pytlik-Szwarc family) and a tensor-norm obstruction. It does not show $A$ and $B$ are non-isomorphic, imposes no nuclearity (the CSSWW positive theorem needs it), and does not affect von Neumann algebras.

fields.name: Quasipolynomial-time solution of mean-payoff games with binary weights
fields.field: Algorithmic game theory; games on graphs; complexity of NP and coNP problems
fields.statement: In a finite two-player mean-payoff game on a directed graph with integer edge weights $w$ given in binary, Max wins from a vertex if she can force $\liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac1T\sum_{t<T}w(e_t)\ge0$. Ehrenfeucht and Mycielski proved positional determinacy, which puts the threshold problem in $\mathrm{NP}\cap\mathrm{coNP}$, and Zwick and Paterson (1996) gave pseudopolynomial algorithms, polynomial in the largest weight but exponential in its bit length; the best general bounds were randomized subexponential. The quasipolynomial algorithm for parity games (Calude, Jain, Khoussainov, Li and Stephan) does not transfer, since the reduction runs from parity to mean payoff. Can the winning regions of mean-payoff games be computed in polynomial time, or at least in quasipolynomial time, in the binary input length?
fields.posedBy: Uri Zwick and Mike Paterson, The complexity of mean payoff games on graphs (1996), as cited by the manuscript; the question is the polynomial-time status of a problem in NP and coNP
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Zwick and Paterson (1996) and Ehrenfeucht and Mycielski (1979) for the setting and does not quote a single posing sentence. The quasipolynomial form of the question became pointed after the 2017 parity-games breakthrough; this entry answers that intermediate question, not the polynomial-time one.
fields.aiRole: The release README says all results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. The manuscripts are credited to OpenAI with no human author named. The family has four manuscripts. The deterministic algorithm (25 September 2026) imports only the finite-box comparison facts from the randomized companion of the same date; the two October 5 manuscripts extend the method to turn-based stochastic games and to mean-payoff parity games. The randomized companion's main theorem has a Lean formalization in the release.

Theorem 1.1 of the principal manuscript was read against the question: a uniform deterministic algorithm outputs the full zero-threshold winning set with $2^{C(\log_2(L+2))^2}$ bit operations, $L$ the complete binary input length; Section 7 adds exact values and optimal positional strategies. The release formalizes only the randomized companion: ComparatorChallenges/RandomizedMeanPayoff.lean (declaration OAI.randomized_quasipolynomial_mean_payoff, file OAI/Computability/RandomMean/Main.lean, listed in formalization.yaml) states that one Turing machine with random bits halts within quasipolynomially many steps on every tape and outputs the exact winning set on at least 7/8 of tapes. It does NOT give a polynomial-time algorithm, which the paper names as a further improvement. fields.name: Quasipolynomial-time solution of simple stochastic and turn-based stochastic mean-payoff games
fields.field: Algorithmic game theory; stochastic games; complexity of NP and coNP problems
fields.statement: A simple stochastic game is a finite turn-based reachability game between two players in which some vertices are chance vertices choosing between two successors with probability $1/2$. Condon (1992) showed that deciding whether the value from a start vertex is at least $1/2$ lies in $\mathrm{NP}\cap\mathrm{coNP}$; Ludwig gave a randomized subexponential algorithm, and Andersson and Miltersen showed the problem polynomially equivalent to solving turn-based stochastic mean-payoff and discounted games with binary data. No algorithm subexponential and deterministic, or quasipolynomial, in the binary input length was known. Can simple stochastic games, and turn-based stochastic mean-payoff games, be solved in polynomial time, or at least in quasipolynomial time?

fields.name: The Eisenbud-Green-Harris conjecture over fields of characteristic zero
fields.field: Commutative algebra; Hilbert functions
fields.statement: Let $S=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a standard graded polynomial ring over a field, let $2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_c$, and let $I$ be a homogeneous ideal containing a regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ with $\deg f_i=a_i$. Eisenbud, Green and Harris, from their work on higher Castelnuovo theory, proposed that the pure powers $x_1^{a_1},\ldots,x_c^{a_c}$ can replace the regular sequence without changing the Hilbert function: there should be a monomial ideal containing $(x_1^{a_1},\ldots,x_c^{a_c})$, indeed a lex-plus-powers ideal, with the same Hilbert function as $I$. Known cases required fast-growing degrees or regular sequences of special form. Does every such $I$ have the Hilbert function of a lex-plus-powers ideal?
fields.posedBy: David Eisenbud, Mark Green and Joe Harris, Higher Castelnuovo theory, Asterisque 218 (1993), Section 4
fields.ageNote: The conjecture is usually stated over an arbitrary field; this entry covers characteristic zero, which is all the manuscripts claim.
fields.aiRole: The release README says all results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. The manuscripts are credited to OpenAI with no human author named. The principal manuscript constructs commuting linear forms with division-algebra coefficients and deduces the Hilbert-function statement; its companion of the same date uses that construction to prove the stronger lex-plus-powers Betti inequalities, listed as a separate entry.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Corollary 1.2 (Artinian case over $\mathbb C$) and the characteristic-zero corollary of the principal manuscript were read against the conjecture: every homogeneous ideal containing a regular sequence of degrees at least two has the Hilbert function of a monomial ideal containing the corresponding pure powers, for regular sequences of any length. The passage from Artinian to general uses the published Caviglia-Maclagan reduction and a coefficient-field descent. Positive characteristic is not addressed. No Lean formalization.
fields.resultNote: Claims the Eisenbud-Green-Harris conjecture over every field of characteristic zero, for homogeneous regular sequences of any positive length with all degrees at least two and with no growth condition on the degrees, via commuting division-coefficient linear forms whose ordered monomials form a basis of the whole polynomial algebra. It does NOT treat positive characteristic. The Betti-number strengthening (lex-plus-powers) is the companion's result, listed separately.

fields.name: The lex-plus-powers conjecture over fields of characteristic zero
fields.field: Commutative algebra; graded Betti numbers and syzygies
fields.statement: With $S=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, $2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_c$ and $P=(x_1^{a_1},\ldots,x_c^{a_c})$, let $I$ be a homogeneous ideal containing a regular sequence of degrees $a_1,\ldots,a_c$, and let $L$ be the lex-plus-powers ideal (lex segment plus $P$) with the same Hilbert function, which exists if the Eisenbud-Green-Harris conjecture holds. The lex-plus-powers conjecture, attributed to Charalambous and Evans, strengthens Bigatti-Hulett-Pardue extremality of lex ideals: $L$ should have the largest graded Betti numbers. It was known for ideals containing $P$ itself (Mermin-Murai) and for fast-growing degrees in characteristic zero (Caviglia-Sammartano). Is $\beta_{p,j}(S/I)\le\beta_{p,j}(S/L)$ for all $p,j$?

fields.name: The Lang-Plaut problem: does every doubling subset of Hilbert space bi-Lipschitz embed in some Euclidean space?
fields.field: Metric geometry; bi-Lipschitz embeddings and dimension reduction
fields.statement: A metric space is doubling if every ball is covered by a bounded number of balls of half the radius. Every subset of $\mathbb R^k$ is doubling, and Assouad's theorem embeds every doubling space bi-Lipschitzly into some $\mathbb R^k$ after snowflaking the metric to $d^\alpha$, $\alpha<1$. For $L_p$ with $p>2$, Lafforgue-Naor and Bartal-Gottlieb-Neiman found doubling subsets with no such embedding. Lang and Plaut asked the Hilbert case for the original metric, and Gupta, Krauthgamer and Lee asked it independently for algorithmic dimension reduction. Does every doubling subset of $\ell_2$ admit a bi-Lipschitz embedding into $\mathbb R^k$ for some finite $k$ and finite distortion?

fields.name: Pixton's conjecture: do Pixton's relations give all tautological relations on the moduli of stable curves?
fields.field: Algebraic geometry; moduli of curves; tautological rings
fields.statement: The tautological ring $R^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ is the image of the strata algebra of decorated stable graphs in the Chow ring. fields.name: Uniqueness of tangent flows at the first singular time of mean curvature flow of closed embedded surfaces
fields.field: Geometric analysis; mean curvature flow singularities
fields.statement: For the mean curvature flow $(M_t)_{t<T}$ of a smooth closed embedded surface in $\mathbb R^3$, parabolic rescalings $\lambda(M_{T+\lambda^{-2}s}-x_0)$ about a singular point subconverge to self-shrinking tangent flows (Huisken, Ilmanen), and Bamler-Kleiner proved the limits have multiplicity one. Uniqueness was known for compact shrinkers (Schulze), round cylinders (Colding-Minicozzi) and asymptotically conical shrinkers (Chodosh-Schulze), but a general shrinker may have both conical and cylindrical ends. Haslhofer formulates tangent-flow uniqueness as Conjecture 5.2. Is the tangent flow at every singular point unique, independent of the rescaling sequence, including its position and axes?
