fields.name: Polynomial-size black-box identity testing for noncommutative rational formulas
fields.shortName: Polynomial hitting sets for NC rational formulas
fields.field: Algebraic complexity; derandomization of polynomial identity testing
fields.statement: A noncommutative rational formula is a formula with $+$, $\times$ and inverse gates over noncommuting variables, evaluated on tuples of square matrices where every inverse is defined. Hrubes and Wigderson reduced its identity testing to noncommutative singularity, solved deterministically in the white-box model by operator scaling. In the black-box model, Forbes-Shpilka gave quasipolynomial matrix hitting sets for division-free formulas, and Arvind, Chatterjee and Mukhopadhyay gave deterministic quasipolynomial-size rational matrix hitting sets for rational formulas of any inversion height, asking in their conclusion for polynomial matrix dimension. Is there a deterministic polynomial-time construction of a polynomial-size list of matrix tuples hitting every nonzero rational formula of size $s$ in $n$ variables?
fields.posedBy: V. Arvind, Abhranil Chatterjee and Partha Mukhopadhyay, Black-box identity testing of noncommutative rational formulas in deterministic quasipolynomial time, arXiv:2309.15647 (2023), conclusion
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites the 2025 revision of the arXiv preprint (first posted September 2023) for the request for polynomial matrix dimension.
fields.aiRole: The release README says all results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. Its named exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human edited for readability) do not concern this family. The manuscripts are credited to OpenAI with no human author named. The family has three manuscripts: the rational-formula hitting lists (principal), a single rational hitting point for division-free formulas over every characteristic-zero field (same date), and a positive-characteristic version (4 October). The release formalizes the principal theorem and the single-point theorem in Lean.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Theorem 1.1 of the principal manuscript was read against the question: one deterministic machine, given $1^n,1^s$, outputs in polynomial bit time a polynomial-size list of rational matrix tuples of a common dimension, one of which gives every admissible nonzero rational formula of size at most $s$ a defined invertible value. ComparatorChallenges/RationalHitting.lean (OAI.RationalHitting.main, OAI/Computability/RationalHitting/Main.lean, in formalization.yaml) states exactly this, with a TM0 Turing machine, explicit binary output encoding, polynomial bounds on dimension, output length and steps, and inverse gates requiring two-sided inverses. Permitted axioms propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice. The companion's FormulaHitting challenge (OAI.NCHitting.universal_hitting, not in formalization.yaml) was also read; it states the single-tuple hitting property but not the construction-time bound. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Claims deterministic polynomial-time construction of polynomial-size rational matrix hitting lists for noncommutative rational formulas over $\mathbb Q$, with no bound on inverse nesting or constant heights, each nonzero formula receiving an invertible value. Companions: one rational tuple of dimension at most $2ns^2$ hits every nonzero division-free formula over every characteristic-zero field, and an analogous tuple over $\mathbb F_p$ works in each positive characteristic. It does NOT cover general noncommutative circuits, and the rational result is over $\mathbb Q$ only.
fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: Polynomial Hitting Lists for Noncommutative Rational Formulas
fields.significanceNote: Polynomial-size black-box identity testing for noncommutative formulas is a recognized derandomization target improving the quasipolynomial bounds of Forbes-Shpilka and Arvind-Chatterjee-Mukhopadhyay, known mainly within algebraic complexity. Above the Polynomial-Time Low-Degree Conjecture entry (30), below the CVP hardness entry (35) and permanent formula lower bounds (38).

fields.name: Deterministic black-box noncommutative singularity testing for rational linear matrices (Garg-Gurvits-Oliveira-Wigderson question)
fields.shortName: Black-box NC singularity over the rationals
fields.field: Algebraic complexity; noncommutative rank; operator scaling
fields.statement: A linear matrix $L=A_0+\sum_i A_ix_i$ with matrix coefficients is noncommutatively singular if it is not invertible over the free skew field, equivalently if $L(X)$ is singular for every tuple of matrices $X$ of every dimension. Garg, Gurvits, Oliveira and Wigderson gave a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for this problem that reads the coefficients (white box). In Section 6 of their Operator Scaling paper they asked for a black-box construction: a deterministic, polynomial-size list of matrix tuples, depending only on the sizes, on which every noncommutatively nonsingular pencil becomes invertible. Can such a list be constructed in deterministic polynomial time?
fields.posedBy: Ankit Garg, Leonid Gurvits, Rafael Oliveira and Avi Wigderson, Operator scaling: theory and applications, Found. Comput. Math. 20 (2020), Section 6, p. 280
fields.ageNote: The Operator Scaling paper first appeared as a preprint in 2015; the manuscript cites the 2020 journal version for the question.
fields.aiRole: The release README says all results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. Its named exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human edited for readability) do not concern this family. The manuscripts are credited to OpenAI with no human author named. The answer is a corollary in Section 5 (the pencil-hitting corollary) of the rational-formula hitting-list manuscript, which also gives a rank-detecting list for rectangular rational pencils.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. The pencil-hitting corollary of the principal manuscript was read: every rational affine pencil of order at most a bound $B$ that is invertible somewhere over an extension of $\mathbb Q$ becomes invertible at some tuple of the same polynomial-size list. The paper calls this the rational-coefficient version of the GGOW question, so coefficients outside $\mathbb Q$ are not covered. The Lean statement RationalHitting concerns formulas, not pencils, so it does not cover this entry. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Claims a deterministic polynomial-time, polynomial-size list of rational matrix tuples on which every noncommutatively nonsingular rational affine pencil of bounded order becomes invertible, and a list recovering the noncommutative rank of rectangular rational pencils from ordinary ranks. It does NOT treat pencils with coefficients from other fields; the GGOW question for general fields remains.
fields.sourceName: OpenAI math release: Polynomial Hitting Lists for Noncommutative Rational Formulas
fields.significanceNote: A black-box deterministic test for noncommutative singularity is a natural next step after the celebrated white-box operator scaling algorithm and is well known in algebraic complexity; this answers the rational-coefficient case. Above the companion rational-formula entry (32), level with the CVP hardness entry (35), below permanent formula lower bounds (38).

fields.name: The equivariant cohomological Hikita conjecture for quiver gauge theories
fields.field: Geometric representation theory; symplectic duality; Coulomb branches
fields.statement: Hikita conjectured that for a symplectic dual pair the cohomology ring of the symplectic resolution on one side is the coordinate ring of the scheme-theoretic fixed locus of a torus on the other, proving it for Hilbert schemes of points and some type A examples. For a quiver gauge theory the Higgs side is a Nakajima quiver variety $X$ and the dual is the Braverman-Finkelberg-Nakajima Coulomb branch $Y$. The equivariant form (Nakajima, recorded by Kamnitzer-Tingley-Webster-Weekes-Yacobi, formulated by Dumanski-Krylov) asks for compatibility with the tautological coefficient maps from $H^*_{G\times F}(\mathrm{pt})$. Is $H^*_F(X;\mathbb C)\cong\mathbb C[Y^\nu_{\mathfrak f}]$ as graded algebras over the common coefficient ring, for every quiver?
fields.posedBy: Tatsuyuki Hikita (arXiv:1501.02430, IMRN 2017); equivariant form in Kamnitzer-Tingley-Webster-Weekes-Yacobi (2019), Conj. 8.9-8.10; form proved: Dumanski-Krylov (2025), Conj. 2.1
fields.ageNote: Hikita's paper was posted in January 2015 and published in 2017. The quiver-gauge equivariant formulation the manuscript proves is that of Dumanski-Krylov (2025).
fields.aiRole: The release README says all results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. Its named exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human edited for readability) do not concern this family. The manuscripts are credited to OpenAI with no human author named. Single manuscript; no Lean formalization.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Theorem 1.1 was read against Dumanski-Krylov Conjecture 2.1, Equation (2.3), which the paper says it proves: for any finite quiver (loops and multiple arrows allowed), dimension and framing vectors, commuting flavor torus and regular stability (semistable equals stable, free action), both coefficient maps are surjective with equal kernels, giving the graded isomorphism with nilpotents retained. The regularity hypothesis is the paper's own scope limit. Inputs include McGerty-Nevins Kirwan surjectivity and Weekes's generation theorem. No Lean formalization.
fields.resultNote: Claims the equivariant cohomological Hikita conjecture for all quiver gauge theories with regular stability: the flavor-equivariant cohomology of the Nakajima variety is canonically the coordinate ring of the scheme-theoretic stability-cocharacter fixed locus of the flavor-deformed Coulomb branch, including the empty case. It does NOT prove the quantized Hikita statement, nor extend to arbitrary reductive gauge groups, where Hikita-type identifications can fail, nor treat non-regular stability.

fields.significanceNote: The Hikita conjecture is a well-known prediction of symplectic duality, studied by a sizeable geometric representation theory community; the quiver case is its main test bed. A conjecture famous within one community: level with the Period-Index entry (30), below the quantum geometric Langlands irrational-level entry (36) and the Toda Gepner conjecture (38).

fields.name: GOE bulk universality for random regular graphs of fixed degree
fields.shortName: GOE bulk universality, random regular graphs
fields.field: Random matrix theory; spectra of sparse random graphs
fields.statement: Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of a uniform random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices with $d\ge3$ fixed. Its eigenvalue density tends to the Kesten-McKay law, and Jakobson, Miller, Rivin and Rudnick predicted, with numerical evidence, that the local eigenvalue statistics in the bulk are those of the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble. Bulk universality was proved for growing degrees (Bauerschmidt-Huang-Knowles-Yau; Bourgade-Huang for $(\log n)^{24}\ll d\le n^{1/2}$), and edge universality at fixed degree (Huang-McKenzie-Yau). Bourgade and Huang state the fixed-degree case as Conjecture 2.11. For fixed $d\ge3$ and fixed bulk energy, does the unfolded eigenvalue point process converge to the GOE bulk process?
fields.posedBy: Dmitry Jakobson, Stephen D. Miller, Igor Rivin and Zeev Rudnick, Eigenvalue spacings for regular graphs, IMA Vol. 109 (1999); stated as Conjecture 2.11 by Bourgade and Huang (arXiv:2607.07617, 2026)
fields.aiRole: The release README says all results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. Its named exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human edited for readability) do not concern this family. The manuscripts are credited to OpenAI with no human author named. The principal manuscript (23 September) proves the clean fixed-degree case; a companion (5 October) adapts its entropy and Gaussian insertion arguments to weak fixed Anderson disorder. No Lean formalization.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Theorem 1.1 was read against the conjecture: for every fixed $d\ge3$ and fixed $E$ in the open Kesten-McKay bulk, Laplace functionals of the unfolded point process of a uniform simple labelled $d$-regular graph converge to those of the GOE bulk process, along all admissible $n$ with no conditioning. The paper says this proves Bourgade-Huang Conjecture 2.11 in a fixed-energy Laplace-functional form; the 1999 prediction was phrased via empirical nearest-neighbor spacings. Uses Huang-Yau rigidity and delocalization as input. No Lean formalization.
fields.resultNote: Claims fixed-energy GOE bulk universality of the full microscopic eigenvalue point process for uniform random $d$-regular graphs, every fixed $d\ge3$ including cubic graphs, at every energy in the open Kesten-McKay bulk. The companion extends this to sufficiently weak fixed iid uniform diagonal disorder on compact subintervals of the clean band. It does NOT address the spectral edges (already known), energy-averaged spacing statistics in the original JMRR form beyond what the point-process limit implies, or strong disorder.

fields.significanceNote: Bulk GOE statistics for sparse fixed-degree random regular graphs is a well-known prediction in random matrix theory, open since 1999 and the last missing case of a long universality program. fields.name: Voiculescu's question: do microstates and nonmicrostates free entropy agree when finite?
fields.field: Free probability; operator algebras
fields.statement: For a bounded self-adjoint tuple $X$ in a tracial von Neumann algebra, Voiculescu defined the microstates free entropy $\chi(X)$ from volumes of matrix approximations and the nonmicrostates entropy $\chi^*(X)$ from free Fisher information along free semicircular noise. They agree for one variable, and Biane-Capitaine-Guionnet proved $\chi\le\chi^*$ in general; equality is known under convexity hypotheses. Agreement was one of the questions of Voiculescu's unification problem, and Guionnet stated the finite-entropy form as a conjecture. Does $\chi(X)>-\infty$ imply $\chi(X)=\chi^*(X)$?
fields.posedBy: Dan Voiculescu, Free entropy, Bull. London Math. Soc. 34 (2002), Sections 3.5 and 3.8 (unification problem); finite-entropy form stated by Alice Guionnet, Probab. Surv. 1 (2004), Conjecture 7.1
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Voiculescu's 2002 survey for the unification problem; the question appears in Voiculescu's free entropy papers of the 1990s, which the manuscript does not quote for it.
fields.aiRole: The release README says all results were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model, the vast majority by one fixed procedure using on average about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result. Its named exceptions (the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, and the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region, whose write-up was human edited for readability) do not concern this family. The manuscripts are credited to OpenAI with no human author named. Single manuscript; it mentions the release's free group factor isomorphism paper only for contrast. The main theorem has a Lean comparator challenge in the release.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Theorem 1.1 was read against the question: a bounded self-adjoint $n$-tuple ($n\ge2$, large but fixed) in a von Neumann algebra with faithful normal trace with $-\infty<\chi(X)\le\chi^*(X)-1/2<\infty$, $\chi$ taken with operator-norm cutoff and limsup over matrix sizes. The Lean challenge ComparatorChallenges/FiniteEntropySeparation.json (theorem OAI.FiniteEntropySeparation.main, solution module OAI.Analysis.FreeEntropy.Main, present at the pinned commit) is not in formalization.yaml; it was found through lean/docs/298.md. Its statement was read here: it defines $\chi$ via microstate volumes with cutoff and limsup, $\chi^*$ via conjugate systems along a free standard semicircular tuple in the same algebra, and asserts exactly the displayed inequalities. Permitted axioms propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice. Not rebuilt here.
fields.resultNote: Claims a negative answer: a bounded self-adjoint tuple with $-\infty<\chi(X)\le\chi^*(X)-\tfrac12<\infty$, built as a small semicircular perturbation of free semicirculars tensored with a commuting discrete variable. It does NOT settle equality for every smaller number of variables (the example uses a large fixed $n$), and uses the limsup version of $\chi$; equality under the known convexity conditions is unaffected.
